tenure_kinds.source: #353 §15 `:537-544` — the seven Tenure kinds and their cardinalities; `reside` is plan position `19c`'s
tenure_kinds.note: ⚠ `reside` (Person -> Rung, ONE live per person) IS THE EIGHTH, AND IT IS WHERE A PERSON LIVES AS DISTINCT FROM WHERE THEY ARE. `contain` is where they are (`04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §B: *"its contain edge is where they are"*) and `move` re-homes it; `reside` is opened only by `migrate` (and minted beside the first `contain` by every world builder), so a `move` leaves it behind. It is what `world_q.population` counts and `world_q.capacity` throttles (`RULINGS.yaml` RR-2). Like `contain`, it is NOT in `release`'s domain: its end is a relocation (`migrate` closes the old edge as it opens the new), and a released residence would leave a person living nowhere. ⚠ `detain` (prisoner -> a seat) AND `ban` (person -> the excluding seat) ARE THE NINTH AND TENTH (#453 §10.4 step 3, K-53; ratified as intent, ED-IN-0288). Each is a disposal a determination opens under an arrangement whose `disposes:` names it (`loop/effects_information.py::_eff_determine`). Neither is in `release`'s domain (`data/rosters.py::RESTRAINT_KINDS`): a prisoner who could release his own custody, or an outlaw his own ban, would walk out of the sentence, which is why they are kinds and not an `oblige` (#453 §8.3). Their readers: `move`/`migrate` decline a person holding a live `detain`, a mustered army excludes him (`loop/sides.py`), `oblige` refuses a `ban` holder service and `confer` declines to seat one. `revoke` opens a `ban` too, on the man whose `appointed` seat it strips (`state/gate.py::REVOCATION_DISPOSAL`), so `ban`'s derived openers are `determine` and `revoke`; a revocation's ban has no term. `arrest` opens a `detain` too (on the seat that ISSUED the warrant), so `detain`'s derived openers are `arrest` and `determine`; and `pardon` is the CLOSER of both (`domain: [detain, ban]`, the loader's closer clause), through the seat that is the edge's object, under the gate's `determination` basis.

hold_object_kinds.source: `architecture/holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md` §15's Tenure table — *"`hold` | Person → Office | Rung | Record | Proposition | 1 per object"*. Item 16 of `proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-behaviour/01_THE_BUILD_ORDER.md` (⊕ R13).
hold_object_kinds.note: ⚠ THE CLASSES A `hold` MAY POINT AT, AND THE ROSTER IS THE OWNER RATHER THAN A LITERAL IN `add_tenure`. `holonic §15` states the domain and the codomain of every Tenure kind; `add_tenure` validates the KIND against `tenure_kinds` and `contain`'s DIRECTION, and this roster checks a `hold`'s object. A `hold` whose subject is a faction (a Proposition, not a person) would make `in_holdings` (which reads *a `hold` whose object is a Rung*) false for every person over every rung. ⚠ **AN UNRESOLVABLE ID PASSES, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN A HOLE.** `_rehome` exists because a Tenure may legitimately be added BEFORE its subject is in `w.persons`, so a guard that refused every unknown id would refuse the ordering the store is built to tolerate. The conjunct refuses only an id that resolves to a class NOT on this roster — a Site, or a person — which is what makes `Tenure(..., "fac_crown", "terr_T1", "hold")` raise while `Tenure(..., "p_late", "off_x", "hold")` still lands in `_unowned` and rehomes.

hold_subject_kinds.source: `architecture/holonic_ARCHITECTURE.md` §15 — the DOMAIN half of the same row: `hold` is a PERSON's edge.
hold_subject_kinds.note: One member, and it is a roster rather than an `is not None` because the codomain above is one too (§8 — the rule lives once) and because the next kind to acquire a domain check reads its own row here instead of growing a second spelling. A subject that resolves to none of the world's collections is UNKNOWN, not wrong, for the `_rehome` reason stated above.

record_kinds.source: `architecture/meta/04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §B.5's synthesis call, ratified (ED-IN-0204): *"`Petition` and `Dispensation` become `Record` kinds ... two existence rows collapse into one"*, and PART A row 11. The KEY LISTS are r2 `02_THE_WRIT_AND_THE_WORD.md` §A.3/§A.5's (ED-IN-0234, PROPOSED); plan position `15` builds them. `faction_sheet` is plan position `20-iii`'s (THE INFORMATION CLUSTER, narrative #14 §F -- `proposals/2026-09-12-emergent-narrative-primitives-v2/01_THE_TEN.md` proposal 14 -- `D1-a` of `proposals/2026-09-27-mc-v18-retirement-plan/PROPOSAL.md`).
record_kinds.note: ⚠ THE KEYS ARE EXACT, NOT A MINIMUM. `Record.__post_init__` (`state/carriers.py`) refuses a `subject_matter` whose key set is not its kind's IN EITHER DIRECTION, and refuses a kind that is not listed here -- r2 `05_LEDGER_AND_BUILD.md`'s ⊕L35. A missing key is an operand no reader can bind; an extra key is a second vocabulary. `text: []` is why every plain Record stays lawful: its `subject_matter` is `None`, which has no keys. ⚠ r2's `commission` (r2 item 11) IS NOT HERE, DELIBERATELY: it has no producer yet and lands with the effect that mints it. A kind nothing mints is a member no reader reaches (`ID-13`). (`faction_sheet` below is NOT r2's `commission` -- a commission is a document conferring a charge; a sheet is a description of a faction.) ⚠ `works` (r2 item 12, `04_MATTER_AND_WORKS.md` §A.6): `found` and `build` make what its `plan` names at the rung its `at` names, and `queries/world_q.py::ceiling` bounds a Site's condition by how many of its declared terms have matured. Its PRODUCER is the `create_record` that already runs (r2 §A.6.2 moment 1): an act declaring `kind: works` and `subject_matter: {plan, at}`. `plan` is a KIND -- a `rung_kinds` member for `found`, a `site_kinds` member for `build` -- and `at` is a RUNG id: "a <plan> at <at>". The verb says whether a Rung or a Site is made, so there is no `as` key. ⚠ THERE IS NO `stage` KEY -- r2 §A.6.1 RULED it out (an ungated write on `subject_matter`, which has no matrix row, and a second progress ladder beside `Site.condition`); the terms are `Record.stages`, matured at MATTER. ⚠ `faction_sheet` (producer `survey`, `loop/effects.py::_eff_survey`): a document whose content is `queries/faction_q.py::resolve`'s five-field view of ONE faction -- who is committed to it, the rungs and the seats they hold -- RESOLVED AT THE MOMENT OF WRITING and frozen there, so it goes stale as the world moves and nothing re-reads it. ITS KEYS ARE `faction_q.Faction`'s FIELDS, IN THAT DATACLASS'S ORDER, and `faction_q.py` REFUSES AT IMPORT if the two drift: the view owns the shape, this row owns what a Record of the kind may carry (⊕L35 reads it). It has NO addressee key, so `world_q.named` reads nobody out of it and a sheet summons no one into a question; its HOLDER learns what it says through the content deposit below, like any document -- holding a document is reading it, and no act is spent to do so. ⚠ THIS ROW IS ALSO A VOCABULARY OF THE `exists:` STEM. `requires_typed: {form: existence, kind: petition}` asks *a Record of kind petition exists* (`queries/world_q.py::WorldReader.read`), so a member here must never also be a `tenure_kinds` member -- `data/rosters.py` refuses the overlap at load rather than letting one reading silently shadow the other.

rung_kinds.source: #353 §10 — the containment ladder. `contain : Rung → Rung`, one parent

scale_of_rung.source: Plan position `20-ii` (U9/R-04). `.designs/systems/_architecture/reference/ scale_transitions_v30.md` §2's Scope column (ARCHIVED-NOT-CANON, quarantined -- read for VOCABULARY ONLY, per `CLAUDE.md` §1/§0.05; cited for the mapping's derivation, never as the reason it is correct). Canon's `Scope` cell per scale, verbatim: Object -- "one item, one wound"; Personal -- "one person"; Relational -- "small group, social agreement"; Territorial -- "a duchy, a district"; Structural -- "a kingdom, an institution".
scale_of_rung.note: ⚠ **A VOCABULARY MAPPING, AND ONLY THAT.** The eight `rung_kinds` admit neither `faction` nor `world`, and canon's five scales are a DIFFERENT vocabulary, so something must translate between the two ladders wherever a caller needs canon's scale-band language. This roster does **not** make a `faction`- or `world`-scale corpus CASE representable (neither is a `rung_kinds` member for the mapping to receive as a KEY); that is `harness/corpus_run.py::rescales` and the `cases/exercises/*.yaml` overlays (`H-95`). ⚠ **THE MAPPING IS DERIVED FROM THE SCOPE CELLS ABOVE, NOT INVENTED.** `person` is canon's own example of `Personal` ("one person"). `hearth`/`community` are sub-settlement social units, matching `Relational`'s "small group, social agreement". `Territorial`'s own example is *"a duchy, a district"*: `duchy` appears by name, and `settlement`/`territory`/`province` are every rung strictly between `community` and `duchy` on the SAME containment ladder, so all four take `Territorial`. `Structural`'s example is *"a kingdom, an institution"* -- `realm` is the one rung above `duchy`. ⚠ **`Object` RECEIVES NO RUNG, AND THAT IS AN HONEST GAP.** Canon's `Object` scale is "one item, one wound" -- sub-personal, with no analogue on the CONTAINMENT ladder (nothing in `rung_kinds` sits below `person`). Mapping a rung onto it would be fabrication (`CLAUDE.md` §0.05: "generate none automatically rather than fabricate"). `SCALE_OF_RUNG` is therefore a TOTAL map on `rung_kinds` (every rung has exactly one scale) and a PARTIAL map onto canon's five scales.

remit_acts.source: #353 §11 — the CLOSED five remit acts, plus `convene`
remit_acts.note: ⚠ H-52 turns on this roster. `ARCHITECTURE_V2.md` gates `open_case` on `remit:determine`, and #353's closed remit acts do not include opening a case — so V2 invented an eligibility. The roster is closed (#353 §11's five acts plus `convene`), and H-52's case is not added to it: a seventh value here would be the hardcoding the ruling above forbids.

remit_default.source: ⚠⚠ NOT CANON. A TESTING FIXTURE, RULED BY JORDAN 2026-09-18: *"anyway, for testing purposes for now, just build out a generic remit"*.
remit_default.note:
⚠⚠ **THIS IS A TEST FIXTURE AND IT IS OBVIOUSLY NOT A DESIGN. READ THIS BEFORE USING IT FOR ANYTHING.** It hands EVERY seated office EVERY remit act, which is exactly the authority `harness/populated.py` refused to invent on its own account: *"inventing one would silently hand somebody an authority nobody granted"*. That refusal stands; Jordan asked for a generic remit SO THE GOVERNANCE VERBS CAN BE EXERCISED AT ALL, and a value that is transparently wrong is safer as a placeholder than a plausible one, because nobody will mistake *"every office can do everything"* for canon.
WHY IT EXISTS. A holder's remit rides on their `hold` Tenure and `person_side_eligible` reads it (`H-71`, `ED-IN-0255`); an office with no remit blocks the governance verbs by DATA, not by any mechanism. This roster is that data, provisionally.
⚠ IT DEFERS TO ANY REAL REMIT AND NEVER OVERWRITES ONE. The three grounded overlays (NPC-008 `issue`; NPC-033 `issue`/`dispatch`; NPC-038 `issue`/`determine`/`dispatch`) keep exactly what their case text supports. This fills ONLY an empty remit.
WHAT REPLACES IT, and the shape is already known. A remit belongs to a POST, and an office is a post plus a scope. ⚠ BUT `Office.post` DOES NOT CURRENTLY HOLD A POST: the realm's posts include `"Cardinal Justice"`, `"Queen (Widow Regent if Almud eliminated)"`, `"Senior Jarl of the Western Highlands"` and `"Archbishop's Representative / Father"`, each fusing a post with a scope, a condition or a relationship. Jordan, 2026-09-18: *"cardinal is a post / king is a post / confessor is a post"*. So per-post remits need the post field normalised first.
⚠ ECCLESIASTICAL POSTS ARE THE AWKWARD CASE. Jordan: *"Confessor governs the Church tho"* and *"they are super weird in that they don't have territories at first"*. So a Confessor's scope is a BODY (`rosters.yaml` maps `"Church of Solmund": ecclesiastical`) and NOT a rung, with territory arriving later if at all. `data/cast.py::title_of` says `Doux`, `Confessor`, `Father` and `Prince` *"are real titles that govern no rung"* -- true of the RUNG LADDER, not of governing nothing. `Office.rung` is already `Optional` (*"null is the office-cluster case (S6.2)"*) and `Office.body`/`faction` carry the institution.
⚠ IT POINTS AT `remit_acts` RATHER THAN RESTATING IT: "every remit act" is what the fixture MEANS, so the pointer states the intent and carries no second copy (§0.05 cl.3). Narrowing it later means replacing `from_roster:` with a `values:` list, which the loader accepts and which is a visible edit rather than a silent divergence.

witness_channels.source: #353 §28 `:1004` — the five channels the fan-out computes an observer set from · order and `claim_source:` from proceedings `19_PLAN.md` step 4 (a)/(b), plan position `15d`
witness_channels.note: The channels are named; their PREDICATES are `H-33` and are graded `assumption` with total fan-out as the default and the control. Naming a channel is not specifying it. ⚠ ORDER IS SEMANTIC HERE (position `15d`): it is the PRECEDENCE, strongest first. A person admitted to one Event by several channels is credited to the FIRST of them (`epistemic.observers_for`), and that one channel sets the deposit's source through `claim_source:` below. The order follows `19_PLAN.md`'s ordinal of remove (*firsthand > knot-sourced > told*): presence first, so a person who WAS IN THE ROOM is never downgraded to hearsay because they also hold the changed thing or sit in the office whose remit covers it — which is what `19_PLAN.md` step 4's *breaks if wrong* names. Between the two `told_by` channels the order decides only which channel is reported, never the source: the holder of the changed thing before the public record. Editing the order changes who holds what as hearsay, a game change, which is why it is data. ⚠ `post_remit` IS LAST, AND THAT IS THE SAME ORDINAL TAKEN ONE STEP FURTHER. `19_PLAN.md`'s ordinal of remove is *firsthand > knot-sourced > told > inferred* in full (`:517`), and `post_remit` mints `inferred`, so it ranks below both `told_by` channels: an obligee who is ALSO admitted by the news of the Event's kind (`reach`, `event_reach` below) holds the Event `told_by`, never downgraded to `inferred`. `claim_source:` is keyed on exactly these five and names only `claim_sources` members (`data/rosters.py` refuses at import otherwise). `reach` is `told_by` on `04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §C.6's own row, and so is `post_remit`'s `inferred` (§C.6: *"the change claims, `inferred`"*). `post_remit` is the place-bound remit channel (r2 item 9: *"the place-blind remit channel -> obligees co-located, minting `inferred`"*); see `epistemic._ch_post_remit`. ⚠ `witness_key` ADMITS THE EVENT'S OWN ANCHOR AS WELL AS ITS KNOT PARTNERS (`_ch_witness_key`'s `pid == anchor`), and one channel carries one source. So an actor with NO PLACE -- whom `co_located` cannot admit -- holds their own act `firsthand_via_knot`, under the event id (S28's knot deposit). §C.6 separates the two (*"change claims about self; via a knot, the partner's deposits"*) and one channel cannot. A placed actor is credited first by presence (`co_located`).

seat_news_kinds.source: v11 CR-29, A-32 (one reach row for seat changes)
seat_news_kinds.note: The kinds tenure edges open or close. `witness_channels.event_reach` carries them (shipped at `realm`, by `from_stratum`); `Fixtures.seat_news: local` lifts exactly these from the `reach` channel, so the news travels by presence, jurisdiction and telling. ⚠ A HAND LIST, AND WIDER THAN ITS NAME: no owner of "the kinds a seat opens or closes" exists (`data/verbs.py`'s derived openers are per tenure KIND and `hold` covers Records and Rungs), and `tenure.closed` is emitted by `release` over six tenure kinds (`hold`, `commit`, `oblige`, `succeed`, `tie`, `knot`), so `local` lifts ALL tenure-kind news, not only seats'. Every member must be an Event kind with a reach in `event_reach` (`epistemic.py` refuses at import).

seat_founding_kinds.source: v12 B11 close, the merge with B21 (A-32's `vacant_named` against `establish`: a founded seat is empty from the moment it exists)
seat_founding_kinds.note: THE KINDS A SEAT'S FOUNDING EMITS. `queries/person_q.py::vacant_named` reads a seat as vacant from the claims a person holds of it, and a seat NO ONE HAS HELD has none that say somebody came to hold it or ceased to, so a founder was never offered `confer` on the office he had just founded (the world-sourced vacancy read it as empty at once; B11.08 moved the read to the ledger). A claim of one of these kinds about a seat says it exists and nobody holds it: it reads as a ceasing, the newest news until a `tenure.opened` follows. `epistemic.py::claim_subjects` already deposits it about the new office to the founder and to those who witness it. Every member must be an Event kind a verb writing `Office.exists` emits (`person_q.py` refuses at import). [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: an empty list, and a founded seat is offered only after someone has held and left it.]

seat_news_arms.source: v11 CR-29 (A-32: one reach row for seat changes at `realm`, B -- the seat-change kinds left out of the map -- the tested alternative), commit (2).
seat_news_arms.note: THE ARMS OF `Fixtures.seat_news` (`H-214`), read by `epistemic._ch_reach`. `realm` (SHIPPED) leaves the seat-change kinds (`seat_news_kinds`) at the reach `event_reach` gives them; `local` is the tested alternative: the `reach` channel admits nobody for those kinds, so a seat change reaches a person only by presence, the seat's jurisdiction (`post_remit`, `document_key`) and telling. `local` is a measurement arm, not a design.

strata.note: ⚠ ORDER IS SEMANTIC HERE, not alphabetical: the fold resolves in this sequence, so editing the order changes which acts see which world. That is a game change, which is precisely why it belongs in data rather than in a body.

eligibility_kinds.source: #353 §9.2 / ARCHITECTURE_V2.md §E4 — the four ways a verb can be made available
eligibility_kinds.note: ⚠ `capability` IS NOT AND MUST NEVER BE A MEMBER. #353 §9.2: "`capability` supplies dice and GATES NOTHING… The only class-shaped gate in the design is Thread Sensitivity." An office makes an ORDINARY verb eligible; no verb exists only for office-holders. Adding a fifth kind is a DESIGN CHANGE — a new way to make a verb unavailable to someone — and not a table edit, so it needs a ruling before it needs an entry.

brute_kinds.source: B05.24 (`ED-IN-0379`), `proposals/2026-11-13-verb-governing-attributes.md` §0: Jordan, 2026-11-13, a verb that is a brute function (authorised, gated or recorded by a seat, a standing or another's decision; its efficacy not in question) names no attribute and does not roll at all
brute_kinds.note: WHAT AUTHORISES A VERB THAT NEVER ROLLS, the value of a verb row's `brute:` (`data/verbs.py::_check_governing_attributes` reads this roster and refuses any other). `seat` -- a seat's remit, purview or conferral basis (the row's eligibility carries `remit:` or its referent class is `Office`); `own` -- an act on his own state or what he holds; `counterparty` -- another person's own decision completes it, drawn in that person's choice. A fourth kind is a design change: a new way for an act to happen with no draw.

person_inputs_kinds.source: B05.25 (`engine/season/verb_table.yaml`'s row shape): how a `contest_subsystems.prizes` row's module reads a person
person_inputs_kinds.note: THE VALUES OF A PRIZE ROW'S `person_inputs:`. `own` -- the module reads the person by its own rule (combat's `scores`, `addends` and mapped attributes, the field's records), so a verb contesting the prize names no `governing:`; `pool` -- the module takes the pool `seam/wrappers/pool.py::faculty` builds from the verb's `governing:` attributes (the social roll), so the verb names them and, contested against a person, the `opposed_attribute` of the person opposite.

pursuits.source: references/descriptor_registry.yaml `pursuit_roster`, count 15 (ED-IN-0261), exported to engine/engine_params/descriptors.json behind a BLOCKING --check (tools/export_descriptors.py).
pursuits.note: ⚠ **READ FROM THE SINGLE OWNER, NOT RE-TYPED.** The fifteen pursuits over seven axes (`ED-IN-0261`) are what this roster carries. JORDAN, 2026-09-02, VERBATIM: *"please note that convictions roster and axes etc may be modified in future."* Populating a roster from a single-owner export is a DATA EDIT, which the same ruling says is the correct shape; `open: true` says in data that the roster may change. ⚠ **THESE ARE PURSUITS AND THEY ARE NOT AXES.** The row below carries SEVEN bipolar axes; a person's pursuits are weights over THESE FIFTEEN, and they reach the axes only through `tables.pursuit_projection` (15×7).

V2 §F2's `conviction[axis]` is computed rather than looked up -- `Σ_conv conviction[conv] · projection[conv][axis]`. ⚠ `exposure` IS FORBIDDEN AS A BARE AXIS NAME and the loader RAISES on it — #353 `:1897` names "The Exposure collision — three senses of one word, including a need scalar and a per-person tally". Spell the sense you mean. ⚠⚠ **THERE IS NO `values:` LIST, AND THAT IS THE REPAIR (ED-IN-0230).** A literal copy here could disagree in silence with `engine/substrate/keys.py::AXES` (nothing under `engine/season/` read it), so a fifth axis in one place would leave the other scoring on four. ⚠ **`from_descriptor:` IS THE `conviction_roster` PRECEDENT.** The roster lives in `references/descriptor_registry.yaml` with `engine/substrate/descriptors.py` as the one code-side reader, so a fifth axis or a rename is ONE edit -- `axis_roster.names`.
