question_sources.source: ARCHITECTURE_V2.md §F1 (Q1–Q3) · PLAN.md `W5` (Q4 `need`) · folded to two at position `11a`, r2 `01_ATTENTION_AND_REACH.md` §A.2
question_sources.note: ⚠ TWO SOURCES (`ARCH §B.13` `ID-13` -- a declared source that reaches no code is the defect, not a design worth keeping). Dates coming due and bands being crossed fold into `claim_landed`: the underlying Event is already witnessable and already deposits a claim, and `reach`/`place_of` (`queries/world_q.py`) carry that claim to someone not standing where it happened as a FILTER over the claims a person's own ledger already holds, never as a new witness channel (`01` §A.4.4). ⚠ `need` IS THE SECOND SOURCE. PLAN `W5`: "**Without Q4 an NPC with a standing ambition and a quiet season forms no candidates at all**, which is most of the NPC corpus" (#353 `:509`, `:605`, `:1297`). A closed set that turned out to be missing a member is the strongest possible argument for keeping closed sets in data. THE ORDER IS A TIEBREAK WITHIN AN ATTENTION TIER (v9 IN-57, RS-22): `questions_for` sorts on `world_q.attention_key`, a tiered read of the person's own state, and `(order[q.source], q.id)` breaks ties inside a tier, so editing this order changes which question a budget-bounded person answers first only among questions of one tier. Within a tier `q.id` is still the last tiebreak.

referent_classes.source: v9 IN-53 (H-207 'VACANCY AS NEED', DECISION 2026-10-13 D1)
referent_classes.note: THE CLASSES A QUESTION MAY CARRY A REFERENT AS, and the closed set a verb row's `referent_class:` column may name (`verb_table.yaml`, validated by `data/verbs.py`). A CLASSED referent is a second partition of a question's referents (`state/carriers.py::Question.classes`), beside its plain `referents`: a row declaring a class forms ONLY on referents carried as that class, and a row declaring none forms ONLY on the plain ones, exactly as before IN-53 (`decision/options.py::opening_set`, through `VerbRow.referents_of`). It exists because `opening_set` has no World (L2) and cannot ask what kind of thing an id is. `Office`: the vacant seats a person may fill (`queries/world_q.py::vacancies`, IN-53) AND the seats he has been told of (`seats_named`, v9 IN-10 (a)), which `questions_for` adds to the question the person answers (`_stamped`); `confer` and `oblige` declare it, and since v10 REM-28 `revoke` (which the column keeps from forming on anything but a seat, and which still executes nothing: its `verb_table.yaml` note); a class is the carrier's own type name, so a stamp of a type this roster does not name is refused at the Question's construction. `Record` (v9 IN-09, H-203, DECISION 2026-10-13 [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): the writs a person HOLDS (`queries/world_q.py::writs_held` -- a live `hold` on a Record of a kind `data/verbs.py::RECORD_REFERENT_KINDS` derives from the rows declaring this class), which `questions_for` adds to the question he answers beside his seats; `comply` declares it, and since v10 REM-2B `evade / defy` and `construe` do too (H-203). REVERT: drop the value and the row's column. v10 REM-25 (B10-05, AM-A-10, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): WIDENED. `carry`, `found` and `build` declare it too, and the term gains its second half beside the writs (`queries/world_q.py::records_held_for_holding_rows`: the Records on a person's live `hold` edges of a kind in `data/verbs.py::HOLDING_RECORD_KINDS`, which that module derives from the `Record` rows whose cell also asks `held_by` of `subject` -- a petition, a works -- with no addressee test, since those rows ask only that the actor hold the document). The class is a collection and not a sub-kind, so it is SHARED: a held petition is a `Record` for all four rows and the fold refuses it on the kind the three others ask (`verb_table.yaml`'s `carry` note has the readings). REVERT: the three rows' columns and the term. v10 REM-2C (B10-05, AM-A-11, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): `research` declares it too, asking `existence` of the collection itself (any document, `data/verbs.py::_record_subkinds_answered` adds no kind to either set), and the class leaves `occasion_only_classes` (below), so the question's own Records are stamped as well (`own_referents_of_class`). REVERT: `research`'s column and `Record` back in `occasion_only_classes`. `Rung` (v9 IN-45 `migrate`, H-168 limit 1, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): the places a person has been told of and could settle in (`queries/world_q.py::places_named` -- a Rung his own ledger names, the §10 ladder seats him in, and he does not already live under), which `questions_for` adds to the question he answers beside his seats and writs; `migrate` declares it (and `requisition`, below, and since v10 REM-27 `march`, whose `subject` binds a stamped Rung as its field, and since v10 REM-28 `convene`, whose `subject` binds one as its venue), so its `to` binds ANOTHER place rather than the single referent of whatever he was asked about (most often his own residence). The destination channel H-168 names, on IN-53 D1's partition and `seats_named`'s knowledge source: no operand is added (`to` still binds the referent, `decision/options.py::_derive_operand`) and no Record kind. REVERT: drop the value, `migrate`'s column and `places_named`'s splice. v9 IN-49 `requisition` (H-163 limit 3, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): AND the larders a seat may requisition (`queries/world_q.py::larders_in_purview` -- a Rung his own ledger names, holding the fixtures' requisition of their matter, inside the purview of a seat of his granting the remit act of a row declaring this class, `data/verbs.py::RUNG_REMIT_ACTS`, and not that seat's own rung, its treasury), stamped after the places and never twice; `requisition` declares it beside `migrate`, so its `subject` binds a stocked rung in purview rather than whatever he was asked about. The class is shared, as `Office` is between `confer` and `oblige`: each row forms on both sources and the fold disposes. REVERT: `requisition`'s column (which removes `issue` from `RUNG_REMIT_ACTS`, the union over the `Rung` rows) and `larders_in_purview`'s splice. v11 CR-25 (CR-11's design, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: `establish`'s column and `holdings_to_found`'s splice]): AND the holdings a seat may found an office over (`queries/world_q.py::holdings_to_found` -- a rung on one of his own live `hold` edges that `founds_over` admits through a seat of his granting an act `establish` is eligible by, `data/verbs.py::FOUNDING_REMIT_ACTS`: held, in that seat's purview, below its rank, the seat on its parent), stamped directly after the larders and never twice. Since B21.08 (VB-A) only a holding whose office is not yet founded is stamped, and it is stamped twice, as `Rung` (the other `Rung` rows form on it, and the fold disposes) and as `Holding` (below), the class `establish` alone declares, so `establish` forms on no place named, no larder and no founded holding. `RUNG_REMIT_ACTS` no longer holds `confer`. v10 REM-21 (B10-05, AM-A-06, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): `Site`, `Proposition` and `Person` -- THE THINGS A QUESTION IS ITSELF ABOUT, carried as their kind. Not a standing occasion: `queries/world_q.py::own_referents_of_class`, one more term of `questions_for`'s splice, stamps the PLAIN referents of the question the person answers whose collection (`World.class_of`) is a class some verb row declares (`data/verbs.py::DECLARED_CLASSES`) and that `occasion_only_classes` (below) does not hold back. It reads the question and never the ledger, so a person who knows fifty people is offered none of them unless his question is about one. `Site`: a worked or built place standing on a rung (`w.sites`, `state/carriers.py::Site` -- a harbour, a seam, a works, a dwelling). `Proposition`: a stated thing a person may commit to, assert or dispute (`w.propositions`, `state/carriers.py::Proposition` -- an OUGHT, a covenant's term). `Person`: a person or cohort by his own id (`w.persons`, `state/carriers.py::Person`); his `person`-kind rung shares the id and `class_of` answers `Person` for it; `open_case` and `petition` declare it, and since v10 REM-28 `dispatch`. While no row declares one of the three, the term stamps nothing for it and no formation moves; a row's `referent_class:` naming it is what makes the term stamp it. REVERT: drop the three values and the term. v11 CR-28 (G-04 (a), B10-09 close two; CP-T02-05's re-take, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the term in `questions_for`]): `Proposition` GAINS A STANDING OCCASION beside the own-referent term -- `queries/world_q.py::propositions_heard`, the Propositions among `person_q.ledger_names` of the claims in a person's own ledger that do not record his own act (`Claim.doer`, the own-act screen's test): an `utter` he witnessed or was told of, another's commitment, a document whose terms name one. `questions_for` appends it last to its splice; `commit` and `argue` form on what it stamps, and `held_edge_declines` (below) declines `commit` on a cause he already holds. The class stays out of `occasion_only_classes`, so a question's own Propositions are still stamped by the own-referent term. `Detainee` (v10 IN-12 step 5, H-226 route (a) with the decline H-232 names [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the value, `interrogate` declares `Person`]): THE RESTRAINED-PERSONS CLASS -- a person held by a live `detain` whose object is a seat the asker holds, stamped by the standing occasion `queries/world_q.py::detainees_held` onto the question he answers. THE ONE CLASS THAT IS NO COLLECTION: the id is a `Person`, so `World.class_of` never answers it and the stamp names it (`data/verbs.py::DETAINEE_CLASS`); it is occasion-only (below). It exists because `Person` is filled with every person a question names, so custody could not be told apart in it. `interrogate` declares it. Empty while no live `detain` exists. `Enemy` (v11 CR-87, the WAR context of `violence_contexts` [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the value, and `war` has no reader]): A PERSON OF A FACTION AT WAR WITH THE ASKER'S, stamped by the standing occasion `queries/world_q.py::enemies_heard` onto the question he answers, `Detainee`'s shape (no collection; named by `data/verbs.py::ENEMY_CLASS`; occasion-only). No row declares it, so no verb FORMS on it: `decision/options.py::opening_set` reads it as the war context of the `fight` decline. Empty while no war Proposition is live, which is every buildable world before CR-91. `Disputant` (B11 lane A, the duel chain's second link [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the value, `challenge` declares `Person`]): A PERSON BESIDE THE ASKER WHOM HE HOLDS A DISPUTE WITH, stamped by the standing occasion `queries/world_q.py::disputes_held` (over `person_q.holds_dispute`, the one owner) onto the question he answers, `Enemy`'s shape (no collection; named by `data/verbs.py::DISPUTANT_CLASS`; occasion-only). `challenge` declares it. It is a class of its own, not `Person`, because `Person` is shared: stamped as `Person`, `capture` formed on the same men and executed where no context licensed violence (ED-IN-0337). `Holding` (VB-A): a rung the person holds and may found an office over, not yet founded (`world_q.holdings_to_found`); not a collection, stamped explicitly; `establish` declares it.

occasion_only_classes.note: THE REFERENT CLASSES ONLY A STANDING OCCASION STAMPS -- never from a question's own referents. `queries/world_q.py::questions_for` stamps a class onto the question a person answers in two ways: a standing occasion, a named term of its splice reading the person's own seats, edges and ledger (`vacancies` and `seats_named` as `Office`, `writs_held` and `records_held_for_holding_rows` as `Record`, `places_named` and `larders_in_purview` as `Rung`), or `own_referents_of_class`, which carries the question's own plain referents of every class a verb row declares EXCEPT the ones listed here. The three of REM-21 were held back because their rows (`confer`, `oblige`, `comply`, `migrate`, `requisition`, and `carry`, `found` and `build`) form on plain referents: carrying the question's own seat, writ or place as that class would widen them onto it. A member must be a `referent_classes` value (`data/rosters.py` refuses another at load). Removing a class from this list is the edit that lets the own-referent term stamp it. REVERT: with the term, the list goes. v10 REM-2C (B10-05, AM-A-11; M19 taken, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): `Record` IS NOT ON THE LIST. `research` declares it and asks `existence` of the collection itself (any document), which no standing occasion answers, so the own-referent term stamps the question's own Records too, beside `writs_held` and `records_held_for_holding_rows` (`_stamped` keeps one pair where both name one Record). The term reads the question and never the ledger. The class is shared, so `comply`, `carry`, `found` and `build` form on a question's own Record as well and the fold disposes (`verb_table.yaml`'s `research` note has the readings). A WRIT IS THE EXCEPTION: the term skips a Record of a writ kind (`data/verbs.py::RECORD_REFERENT_KINDS`), which only `writs_held`'s addressee test stamps, so a bystander who saw a writ issued is offered no `comply`. REVERT: put `Record` back here (with `research`'s column). `Detainee`, `Enemy` and `Disputant` are members because only their standing occasions (`detainees_held`, `enemies_heard`, `disputes_held`) stamp them: no collection is named so, so the own-referent term could never match them.

flow_stake_classes.note: THE CLASSES A FLOW'S STAKE MAY BE STAMPED AS (`queries/world_q.py::flow_stakes`, behind `Fixtures stamp_flow_stakes`, `hole_register.yaml` H-274): the rungs, persons and offices a strand names. Any other class `World.class_of` gives an id (`Record`, `Site`, `Proposition`) or none (a custody edge's Tenure id, an id the World does not hold) is left unstamped by `_of_stamped_class`, the one class test. `Enemy` is never among them: no row forms on it and the `fight` decline reads it as licence, so a flow a person knows of must never by itself make another man his enemy. A member must be a `referent_classes` value (`data/rosters.py` refuses another at load). REVERT: with the term.

person_predicates.note: THE PREDICATE VOCABULARY `standing` NEEDS (PLAN `W5`). A Claim carries `(subject, predicate, value)`; `standing` pairs claims ABOUT ME by predicate, so without a vocabulary "pairs by predicate" is pairing on a free string. #353 `:331` supplies one: these are the five things `marks[]` records about a person, which is the corpus's own list of what is readable off someone. Open, because a claim may assert something `marks[]` does not record.

view_builder_rules.source: #353 §18 `:623` — "at most K claim ids from the holder's OWN ledger -- built, not filtered"
view_builder_rules.note: ⚠ "BUILT, NOT FILTERED" SAYS WHAT A VIEW IS NOT AND NEVER SAYS WHICH K. PLAN `W5` names the gap: "`K = 12` says nothing about **which** K, and the instrument takes the last k". Each value here is one rule for choosing WHICH ids; `H-53` is the row, `recent` is its default, and all three are swept. `recent` is the instrument's incumbent and is kept as the default so the sweep has an honest control — not because it is argued for.

question_aggregation.source: PLAN.md §1.4 hole 15 / `H-54` — "nothing says how many questions a person forms per season"
question_aggregation.note: ⚠ `deliberate` once took `qs[0]` -- the first question in `question_sources` order -- with no row or marker, and `question_sources` is ORDERED, so that silently meant *a Date always beats a need*, an unruled priority rule that decides what every NPC does first. `first` is that behaviour DECLARED, kept as the default because it is the incumbent and a sweep needs an honest control -- not because it is argued for. `all` gives the person every question and lets the budget triage them, which is what §26.3's triage is FOR; `one_per_source` is the middle reading. `H-54` is the row.

scene_packing_rules.source: `W17` — which interactions share one scene. `player_agency_v30.md` §6.3 says a scene HOLDS 1–3 and never says WHICH
scene_packing_rules.note: ⚠ `H-76` registers HOW MANY interactions a scene admits; this roster says WHICH ones share one (`make_chooser` once answered it in a comment: *"the default policy fills scenes greedily in score order"*, which H-53 calls *"AN INVENTION"*). `greedy` is that invention DECLARED and kept as the sweep's control, not argued for. `one_per_scene` is the pre-ruling accounting — one interaction per scene action — and is the honest floor. `by_subject` is the reading `player_agency_v30.md` §6.3's own words suggest: *"one scene opportunity pursued"* is about SOMETHING, so the interactions sharing a scene are the ones sharing a subject. `H-78` is the row.

claim_subject_rules.source: #353 §20 — `Claim := (id, holder, subject, predicate, value, ...)`, and NOTHING says what `subject` is for a WITNESS deposit
claim_subject_rules.note: ⚠ WITNESS once deposited every claim with `subject = event.subject`, which the fold sets to the ACTOR, so every claim in the world was "I hold that <actor> did <kind>" and §F1's Q2 -- *"a claim landing in the holder's ledger whose subject is that person, SOMETHING THEY HOLD, or a Proposition they have committed to"* -- could never fire on its second clause. These rules say what a deposit's `subject` is. `actor` is the incumbent, kept as the sweep's control. `per_change` mints one claim per `StateChange` with the CHANGED THING as its subject, which is what makes "something they hold" reachable and what #353 §13.1's own narration needs — a copy that can be found, carried, hidden or destroyed. `both` keeps the actor claim and adds the per-change ones. ⚠ **THAT HOLDS ONLY WHERE `changes[]` IS NON-EMPTY.** An Event that WROTE NOTHING has no per-change subject to add, and under `per_change` and `both` alike its deposit is minted about WHAT THE ACT NAMED instead of about the actor (`H-102`): a claim about the teller can never satisfy *the holder, or something they hold*. ⚠ **THE PRICE: WHERE THE ACT NAMED SOMETHING, NO LEDGER RECORDS WHO SPOKE.** For a speech, a telling, a compliance or a refusal THAT NAMES ITS SUBJECT, the deposit no longer names the actor, so under the DEFAULT arm the attribution of that act is in nobody's ledger. The replacement is guarded on `any(refs)`: a write-nothing act that names NOTHING leaves `out` untouched, and the actor survives via the standing `out or [anchor]` fallback under `per_change` (`anchor_of` returns the same actor), and because the actor is already in `out` under `both`. That false arm is unreachable from the corpus as it stands (every Act the fold mints comes from `pack_scenes` with `payload={"subject": ...}` drawn from non-empty referents); `H-111`'s refusal question is where a witness would first appear. Attribution reads `causes[]` through `state/attribution.py` -- an Event carries no actor and no `subject` (`T-d`, `H-107`). The `actor` arm is where the incumbent behaviour survives. ⚠ **IT REPLACES RATHER THAN JOINS, AND THAT IS NOT A DERIVATION.** Joining mints one extra claim per write-nothing Event; the cap evicts on `(confidence, recency)`, and `H-40`'s decay sweep then read a minimum confidence of 100 in all three arms (a damping loop made unobservable by an amplifying one, `H-103`'s cite). The ground for the choice is that the teller is not the news. ⚠ THIS ADDS NO FIELD TO `Event`. `PLAN.md` §8.1 forbids adding a `target` or `actor` field to Event; `changes[]` already names what was written, so the subject is READ off the Event the design already has. `H-79` is the row.

observation_deposit_modes.source: `W-B`. #353 §28 says WITNESS deposits a Claim and never says whether a deposit may carry WHAT THE FOLD READ, or to whom. §20 types the Claim and stops there.
observation_deposit_modes.note: ⚠ THIS IS THE WRITE SIDE OF `H-116`. `belief_contradicts` evaluates the verb's own `requires_typed:` cell against `LedgerReader`, so the vocabulary a claim must be in to reach §F1 clause 4 is `stores:<kind>` / `condition` / `contain.path:<to>` / `claim.held` / `exists:<kind>` / a relation stem — the strings `Observation` DERIVES from the cell's own fields. A deposit carrying `predicate = e.kind` and `value = True` is a DISJOINT vocabulary and a value no comparator can send to False, so clause 4 could never fire on it. `none` is THE CONTROL (no read is deposited), so every measurement of this item has a baseline (`CLAUDE.md` §0.1 point 4). `actor` deposits an act's reads to the actor alone — the minimum that closes the loop, and the arm where every claim minted is one its holder can read back, because `belief_contradicts` binds `from` to the person's OWN containing rung and `actor` to their own id. `total` gives the reads the same fan-out the Event itself got, which is #353 §61's shape for the Event and is not stated for the read. ⚠ THE OBJECTION TO `total` IS §F1'S EPISTEMOLOGY AND IT IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS. The fold reads with `WorldReader` — world truth — so fanning a read to everyone teaches everyone a VERIFIED fact, and §F1 rests on people acting on beliefs that may be wrong. But `LedgerReader` resolves on `(when, confidence)` and the cap evicts, so a season-1 observation of `stores:grain = 5` is a STALE belief the moment the granary empties, and a person acting on it acts wrongly. The epistemic gap survives as RECENCY rather than as absence. That is a reading, not a result; the arm is swept and the measurement is on `H-122`. ⚠ UNKNOWN IS NEVER DEPOSITED IN ANY ARM. A read the world could not answer is the INSTRUMENT'S gap, and `H-94`'s `operands_for` refuses to mint an act with a hole precisely so that gap does not become a false belief; depositing UNKNOWN would reintroduce it from the other end. It is inert besides — it reads back UNKNOWN and can contradict nothing — while still costing a ledger slot the cap evicts somebody else for.

combat_degree_bands.source: JORDAN, 2026-09-03, VERBATIM: *"kill/wound degrees should be directly taken from scene combat, which is what actually needs to be called when kill/wound is considered."* And 2026-09-04: *"the combat engine determines the result there. your code just has to accept the result."*
combat_degree_bands.note: ⚠ THE ORDER IS SEMANTIC AND IT IS SEVERITY, WORST FIRST. `shape.py` unpacks this row positionally (`FELLED, WOUNDED, UNTOUCHED = COMBAT_BANDS`), so reordering it renames the bands rather than reordering them, and `verb_table.yaml`'s `kill / wound` keys its degree-keyed `writes:`/`emits:` on the same three strings. A drift between the two is loud at the first act that folds: `VerbRow.writes_at` refuses an unlisted degree and PRINTS BOTH SETS. ⚠ THESE ARE NOT THE LADDER'S FOUR BANDS AND MUST NOT BE CONFUSED WITH THEM. `S39.4` reads four bands off a MARGIN and its single owner is `engine/dice_engine/dice_engine.py:: degree_from_net`, which `shape.degree_of` IMPORTS AND CALLS. Combat is EXEMPT from that ladder by the ruling above: its bands are a READ of the engine's own `WoundTracker` — the subject went down, the subject bled, the subject was untouched — and every one of the three is a field `combat_seam.resolve` returns in `wound_state`. ⚠ WHY THERE IS NO FOURTH. The engine does not separate a DECISIVE win from a NARROW one beyond wound count on the victor, so an `Overwhelming`-vs-`Success` split has NO SOURCE IN THE DATA and is not invented. That is the whole of what survives in `H-98`.

wound_quantities.source: `seam/wrappers/combat.py::resolve`'s `wound_state` -- the fields of the engine's own `WoundTracker` that the seam lifts per party before `wrapper.fight` collapses the scene to an int. Jordan 2026-09-02: *"I do not want definitions etc to be hardcoded"* -- the list was a literal inside `_state`.
wound_quantities.note: ⚠ THIS ROW IS THE CLOSED SET `combat_band_edges` IS VALIDATED AGAINST, AND `_state` READS IT TOO. One owner, so an edge cannot name a quantity the seam does not lift: `_state` builds each party's `wound_state` from THIS list and refuses, by name, a member the `WoundTracker` does not carry; `combat_band_edges` refuses at load an edge on a member that is not here. The ORDER is the order `wound_state` has always been built in (`felled` first), kept so the lifted dict is identical to the literal it replaced. ⚠ A QUANTITY IS A NUMBER OR A BOOLEAN THE TRACKER COMPUTES, NEVER A DERIVED RATIO. A ratio (`health_remaining / health_full`) is a magnitude `wound_harm_models` already reads at its own site; an edge over one would be a second reading of the same quantity.

estimate_outcomes.source: CP-T03-05 (`H-251`, `-08` AM-C-02): the four ways a personal fight can end, as the player's odds display shows them.
estimate_outcomes.note: THE KEYS OF `seam/wrappers/combat.py::fight_estimate`'s shares, in the order `sigma.odds_of` returns them for a row contesting `the body`: the actor felled (the result is the subject's), the subject felled (the actor's), a yield (a standing party gave up, the engine's `surrender`), and undecided (the ruled outcome, result 0). The ORDER is the tuple's; the shares sum to 1.

fight_endings.source: CP-T03-02 (home `proposals/2026-10-23-subsystem-completion/` T03 §2): how each party's fight ended, as the band's Event carries it (`Event.ending`): fight/accept at Felled/Wounded, and capture at any band where an edge is opened.
fight_endings.note: ONE VALUE PER PARTY, read off the scene by `loop/effects_combat.py::fight_ending`: `felled` (his own band is `Felled`, `seam/ladder.py::party_degree` off the lifted `wound_state`), `yielded` (the scene's `surrender` names him), `prevailed` (B14.02, D-U1-11a: he is neither felled nor the yielder while the other party is -- the one left standing), `undecided` (neither party is felled or yielded). The ORDER is the tuple's: felled, yielded, undecided, prevailed. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: the field and the Observation]

margin_endings.source: SC-P1 (H-284): what a margin provider's contest leaves on its Events
margin_endings.note: THE SOCIAL PROVIDER'S ENDING SHAPE, beside `fight_endings` (the scene's): `Event.ending` of a margin provider's act is `((key, value), ...)` in THIS roster's order, built by `loop/resolve.py::_fold` from the result `seam/wrappers/sigma.py::resolve` returned and nothing recomputed: `pool` and `ob` the roll's, `net` the draw plus its boost, `margin` the real margin `net - ob` the ladder quantises once (the result's `settled_margin`), `terms` `Margin.terms` (the obstacle's named terms in roster order, summing to `ob`), `levels` `((source, aggressor n, defender n), ...)` one per `advantage_sources` member, `leverage` the act's net sigma. A refusal carries none: no dice were dealt. It names no actor, target or subject, and is no `Claim`'s predicate (`test_sc01_provider.py::test_no_claim_predicate_is_a_margin_ending_after_witness`).

proceeding_endings.source: B24p.20 (V2 p2 §C.1, §J): the tags of a proceeding's `Event.ending`
proceeding_endings.note: A PROCEEDING'S ENDING IS A TUPLE OF TUPLES, EACH BEGINNING WITH ONE OF THESE TAGS, in THIS order: `("proceeding", row id, form, ended, ended_by)`, one `("beat", ...)` per beat (a `Beat`'s fields in declared order, `terms` left out, `mood` replaced by its stance, `stance_bands`), one `("sitting", n, issue, points, live, tracks, cond, used, last_voice, ended)` and one `("verdict", id, band)` per verdict, every real a whole number of milli-units. Written by `loop/resolve.py::_proceeding_ending` from the outcome and the result `seam/wrappers/sigma.py::_resolve_proceeding` returned; read by `queries/world_q.py::ending_beats`, `ending_sitting`, `ending_verdicts`, `ending_rattles`. It names no `Claim`'s predicate. An ending of a single roll (`margin_endings`) holds none of these tags. B24p.22: the LAST tag is `("card", decided_by, arranged_by, tilt, tilted_against, ruled)`, the public cells of the card (who decides, who tilted the forum, how far and against which side) and a played adjudicator's departures (`Outcome.ruled`, `((decider, departure), ...)`), every real in milli-units; read by `world_q.ending_card`. It holds no true attribute: what the witnesses read of who decided and what the forum was is what the card showed every participant. `loop/witness.py` deposits what the sitting showed into each man's own ledger from the beats and this tuple. B24.14: AFTER THE CARD, one `("exchange", kind, item id)` per item a beat entered or struck (`queries/inputs.py::exchanges`, `kind` an `EXCHANGE_CELLS` name), in the beats' order, and NONE for a sitting that entered or struck nothing (so the ending of every such sitting is what it was); read by `world_q.ending_exchanges`. The same list is appended to the case file's `Record.stages` by `loop/effects_information.py::_eff_determine`. B24.29: AFTER THE EXCHANGES, one `("bench", ((seat, sign), ...))` where a seat who decides holds PUBLIC commits on the motion (`world_q.declared_votes_by_member`: a commit is public), `sign` the sign of his signed count (+1 for the motion, -1 against), in the bench's order; NONE where no seat holds one (every sitting the shipped cast holds, so such an ending is what it was); read by `world_q.ending_bench`. It is what every witness is shown of the bench; what each man comes to HOLD of it is his own drawn reading (`sitting_claims: leans`).

stance_bands.source: B24p.20 (V2 p2 §C.1; p4 §L 20): how a proceeding's `Event.ending` names the room's stance
stance_bands.note: THE FIVE BANDS OF A BEAT'S MOOD, THEN THE WORD A YIELD THAT DECIDED IS NAMED BY. The mood is the room's lean toward `for`, clamped to -1..1 (`modules/social_contest/proceeding.py::mood`); the record never shows the number. Its five bands are the five equal fifths of that range, in THIS order from the lowest: firmly with `against`, leaning `against`, hanging, leaning `for`, firmly with `for`. The sixth member is the stance of the beat on which a yield settled the matter itself (the act's band was the yield's: `act_band`'s `read` is empty), said to have decided and never a band of the mood. Written by `loop/resolve.py::_proceeding_ending` at the beat that TURNS the stance (the first beat, and each whose band differs from the beat before); read by nobody as a number. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; basis: V2 p2 §C.1 says "five bands of its mood (firmly with one side, leaning, hanging)", not their edges; equal fifths of the clamped range; revert: edit the edges in `_stance_of`]

sitting_claims.source: B24p.22 (V2 p2 §J: *every sitting also leaves, from the beats, ... a claim*; p4 §K B2, B4, B21, C1, C4): the claims a sitting deposits in the ledgers of those who saw it
sitting_claims.note: THE KINDS OF CLAIM A PROCEEDING'S WITNESSES HOLD, one member each; the PREDICATE is `<claim.predicate>:<kind>` (`sitting:rattled`), and the source is `claim.source`, a `claim_sources` member (each person present saw it: `firsthand`). Written by `loop/witness.py::_sitting_claims` from `Event.ending` alone (`world_q.ending_beats`, `ending_sitting`, `ending_card`), into the OWN ledger of each person in the sitting's room and no other. Every claim's SUBJECT is the person it is about; its VALUE is: `rattled` the man rattled; `shown` the item shown; `conceded` and `contumacy` the issue it was said on; `hypocrite` the issue of the speech his reading turned (held by those whose reading turned it, alone); `temper` the beat on which the man first spoke with his temper broken (one a man a sitting); `partial` a decider's `(conflict, lean)` in milli-units; `rigged` `(the side the forum worked against, how far)` with the arranger as subject; `overruled` how far a played adjudicator's ruling departed from his own track; `heard` the issue the sitting reached, held by each bystander who does not decide (he learns, he does not rule), about the man who bore the matter; `yielded` and `hinted` the matter's questioned man as subject and the issue reached as value, held by the questioner under the `yield` disposal at the band `arrangements.yaml: disposal` names, at confidence `confidence_default` times that write's `weight` in `disposal_writes`. NO VALUE IS A TRUE ATTRIBUTE OR A `terms` CELL. Regard, pursuits, standing and legitimacy are the fold's (B27.28, B33.51), and a conviction is never written (A-92, `04:251`). [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: the kinds' predicates, subjects and values, which V2 names in prose and no roster carried; `heard`'s subject is the bearer and not the matter, because `said_of` would otherwise offer the hearer's newest claim on the matter in place of what he believes of it; `partial` is deposited only where a decider's conflict reaches `recuse_at` (the host's own line for a partial seat); a sitting's claims are first-hand and never refracted (they are the typed record of what a man saw in the room, not a reading of an act).] B24.29: `leans` -- a seat's lean on the motion, `±1` (+1 toward the motion), the seat as subject, held by each person in the room who does not decide, as that man READS it: the sign the sitting wrote (`proceeding_endings: bench`), drawn on a keyed stream (`H(seed, tick, viewer, "bench_read:<seat>")`) and true with chance `(1 + acc) / 2`, `acc` his accuracy (`modules/social_contest/proceeding.py::accuracy`: his Attunement alone, opposed by nothing), so at `acc` 0 he guesses and at `acc` 1 he reads it truly; a wrong sign is possible at every Attunement. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; basis: the entry's "the chance the deposited sign is the true one is `acc`" read for a two-valued sign as the share of the truth `acc` reaches (`_Believed`'s reading of a claim), the rest a guess: read as `acc` itself a man of Attunement 2 would be wrong more often than right; revert: the chance is `acc`]

duel_terms.source: CP-T03-09 (`-08` AM-C-03; home `proposals/2026-10-23-subsystem-completion/` T03 §2): the terms a verb's fight is fought under.
duel_terms.note: WHICH TERMS A VERB'S SCENE IS FOUGHT UNDER -- `verb: term`. TWO ENTRIES: `capture: yield`, the fight ends when a party has yielded and the loser is taken into a seat's custody rather than killed (`loop/effects_combat.py`), and, since v11 CR-87, `accept: blood` (below). A verb NOT named here fights under the engine's lethal terms (`PersonalCombatInput.terms`' default, the string `'death'`), so `fight` is unchanged. READ BY `seam/wrappers/combat.py::combat_input`, which fills `PersonalCombatInput.terms` from it -- the ONE path a term reaches the fight by (PC-10b extends this roster and adds no second path). ⚠ THE CLOSED SET OF TERMS IS THE ENGINE'S (`modules/combat/wrapper.py::DUEL_TERMS`), NOT THIS FILE'S: `engine/season/data` may not import the module, so the loader (`data/verbs.py::DUEL_TERMS_BY_VERB`) refuses a verb the table lacks or a non-string, and `combat_input` refuses a value outside the engine's tuple, NAMING this roster, before the call -- a term is checked against that tuple and never re-declared here. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop this roster and `capture` fights to the death, which is `fight`.] ⚠ AN ACT WHOSE `subject` IS A `challenge` Record (`accept`) is fought under that Record's `stakes` (`challenge_terms`), read by the same `combat_input` into the same `PersonalCombatInput.terms`; a challenge naming no stakes falls through to this roster's `accept` line. `accept: blood` (ED-IN-0336, RS-25: *"a duel doesn't have to be lethal"*): a duel whose challenge names no stakes (every computed `challenge`: it carries no payload) is fought to the first wound, not to the death -- through `duel_terms_of`'s fall-through, the same one path; a challenge that names its stakes is still fought under them. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the `accept` line, and the duel is fought at `PersonalCombatInput.terms`' own `'death'` default.]

context_terms.source: B15.08 (PHY_A A3, ED-IN-0337): the terms a `fight` is fought under, by the context of violence that formed it.
context_terms.note: WHICH TERMS A `fight` IS FOUGHT UNDER BY ITS CONTEXT -- `context: term`, `duel_terms`' shape. A CONTEXT IS A NAME OF ONE READER IN `decision/options.py::VIOLENCE_CONTEXT_READERS` (`violence_contexts`' closed set): `opening_set` records the context that admitted the subject on the Candidate's payload (`data/rosters.py::CONTEXT_KEY`), and `seam/wrappers/combat.py::combat_input` fills `PersonalCombatInput.terms` by ONE path: a challenge's `stakes`, else `duel_terms[verb]`, else THIS roster's line for the act's `context`, else the engine's lethal default (`death`). `war` is lethal; a `crime` or a `defence` fight ends when a party yields (a warrant is served, a blow is answered; neither is a licence to kill). `duel` has no line: it is no context of `fight`, a duel is `accept`'s. An own-motive context joins this roster with its reader (A-16, B37). REFUSED AT IMPORT: a key that is no context reader (`options.py`), a term that is not a non-empty string (`data/verbs.py`). REFUSED AT CALL TIME, AND ONLY WHERE THE ENGINE IS PRESENT: a term outside the engine's closed set (`seam/wrappers/combat.py::duel_terms_of`). [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop this roster and every `fight` is lethal, as before B15.08.]

challenge_terms.source: v10 PC-10b (RS-25, Jordan 2026-10-14: *a duel doesn't have to be lethal*; H-240 route (1)): the terms a challenge may name.
challenge_terms.note: THE CLOSED SET OF A `challenge` RECORD'S `stakes` (`record_kinds.challenge`). Its members are the engine's (`modules/combat/wrapper.py::DUEL_TERMS`): `engine/season/data` may not import the module, so the two are held equal by a TEST (`engine/season/tests/test_pc10b_challenge_record.py`), never by an import and never re-declared unchecked. `_eff_challenge` refuses a `stakes` outside it; a computed challenge names none, and its duel is fought under `duel_terms`' `accept` line, `blood` since v11 CR-87. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct -- the three terms; revert: no terms, a duel is lethal, as before.]

mortal_causes.source: HAP_A edit 3; PHY_A A3's three terms and the spell of illness
mortal_causes.note: THE CLOSED SET OF CAUSES `queries/world_q.py::mortal_terms` ANSWERS FOR -- the pool and obstacle of the draw that decides whether a felled or stricken body dies, one owner. `death`, `yield` and `blood` are the three terms a fight is fought under (`challenge_terms`' members, PHY_A A3) and each has its obstacle in `Fixtures.mortal_wound_ob`; `spell` is the illness a spell lays, a member now and with NO obstacle until B37 (HAP_A edits 4 and 5) writes its branch, so `mortal_terms` refuses it by name rather than answering. A cause outside this set is refused at `data/rosters.py::require_mortal_cause`. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the roster and `mortal_terms`]

combat_band_edges.source: `H-98`, plan position `8` (closed; `workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v8_part4.md`, retired, at `FORK:7b619328`) -- the edge between the bands was two literals in `seam/ladder.py::combat_degree` (`if st["felled"]` / `st["wounds"] > 0`). Jordan 2026-09-02: *"I do not want definitions etc to be hardcoded"*. The bands themselves are `combat_degree_bands`, ruled 2026-09-03/04 as a READ of the scene.
combat_band_edges.note: ⚠ ONE EDGE PER BAND EXCEPT THE LAST, KEYED ON `combat_degree_bands`, AND THE LAST IS WHAT IS LEFT. `combat_degree` walks the bands in the order that row declares (SEVERITY, WORST FIRST) and returns the first whose edge HOLDS -- `quantity` strictly above `above` -- else the final band. `Felled` / `Wounded` / (`Untouched`) is therefore exactly the old `if felled: Felled; elif wounds > 0: Wounded; else Untouched`, and the SHIPPED values below reproduce it. The loader refuses a band with no edge, an edge on a band that row does not carry, an edge on the residual band, and an edge on a `quantity` that `wound_quantities` does not list (`rosters.load_combat_band_edges`). ⚠ `above` IS A COUNT OR THE NAME OF ANOTHER `wound_quantities` MEMBER, NEVER A RATIO AND NEVER A THIRD KIND OF THING. `felled` is a boolean the tracker computes and is compared as 0/1, so `{quantity: felled, above: 0}` is the engine's own verdict, accepted rather than re-decided (Jordan 2026-09-04: *\"the combat engine determines the result there. your code just has to accept the result.\"*). It is NOT swept, because sweeping it would re-decide who went down. ⚠ ONLY THE `Wounded` EDGE'S `above` IS A SWEPT FIXTURE -- `Fixtures.combat_wounded_above`, `None` meaning THIS ROW'S value (so `0` is authored once, here). The arms are on `H-98`: `0` (SHIPPED: any wound), `1` (the first wound is not enough), and `max_wounds` (the count must EXCEED the engine's own cap: a subject sitting exactly AT `max_wounds` reads Untouched). `wounds` is capped by the tracker at `max_wounds + 1`, so `wounds > max_wounds` holds only for a subject who reached the cap and is still standing -- NOT for nobody; it is the arm at which the `Wounded` band shrinks to that one case. ⚠ THIS IS NOT THE FOURTH BAND. A decisive-vs-narrow split has no source in the data and is not invented (`combat_degree_bands`' own note); this row moves WHERE the existing split falls.

wound_harm_models.source: `W-E`. #353's Part E `writes:` column names the CELL and never the VALUE, and no in-chain document says how much body a wound costs. `H-114` measured what the instrument did instead: `harm` defaulted to the person's whole body, so a fold at degree `Wounded` DELETED THE PERSON.
wound_harm_models.note: HOW MUCH BODY A WOUND COSTS, WHEN THE SCENE SAYS THE SUBJECT BLED AND DID NOT GO DOWN. `scene_fraction` is the DEFAULT and it introduces no constant: the body is scaled by the fraction of health the fight left standing (`health_remaining / health_full`), both fields the engine's own `WoundTracker` computed on Combatants `combat_seam` still holds. That is Jordan's 2026-09-04 ruling applied to the magnitude as well as to the band — *the combat engine determines the result there* — rather than a number this chain chose. ⚠ `total` IS THE CONTROL: `_eff_kill` subtracts `d.get("harm", p.body)`, i.e. the whole body, so every wound kills and `Wounded` is indistinguishable from `Felled`. Running this arm re-runs that defect deliberately, which is how the degree's worth is measured rather than asserted (`CLAUDE.md` §0.1 point 4). `none` is the SECOND control and isolates the other half: a wound writes nothing, the fold's own write-nothing guard emits the REFUSAL instead of the success, and what is left is only the difference the SELECTED WRITE SET makes. ⚠ A WOUND CANNOT KILL ON ANY ARM EXCEPT `total`. The band means the engine did not fell this person, so the body floors at 1 — `seam/wrappers/combat.py::party_end`'s own floor (*a dying person still fights*), followed rather than reinvented.

body_mark_models.source: v11 CP-T03-07 (P32, a permanent injury mark). A fight can wound and every recovery heals to the scale, so no fight leaves a lasting mark; `Person.body_ceiling` is the bound a recovery heals toward.
body_mark_models.note: WHETHER A FIGHT LEAVES A LASTING MARK. `deepest_gate` is the SHIPPED arm: a party who survives a fight at the engine's deepest gate short of felling (`wounds >= max_wounds` on his lifted tracker, both `wound_quantities` members) has his `body_ceiling` fall to one below the next `band_floors["body"]` floor beneath it, so the marks are as many as the body has floors (`loop/effects_combat.py::marked_ceiling`). `none` is the CONTROL: no ceiling moves and every outcome is the pre-item tree's (the field itself is still a schema mover). `drawn` (B14.23, `U5b_PC_residue` section 7) is NOT shipped: the same survivor at his limit rolls once, on the one sampler, against the fixture `mark_ob` -- Failure lowers the ceiling twice, Partial once (as `deepest_gate` does), Success and better not at all -- and the mark is told as the Observation `marked`.

field_degree_bands.source: M4, `ED-IN-0279` clause (a). The token every `march` fold writes -- `seam/ladder.py`'s `field_degree`, analogous to `combat_degree_bands` above.
field_degree_bands.note: ⚠ ORDERED, AND UNPACKED POSITIONALLY LIKE `combat_degree_bands`. `Declared` is first because it is the band ENCOUNTER's own declaration fold writes at RESOLVE (`04 §A.2`, amended 2026-09-28) -- the seventh-phase design's own deferral token, not a band any subsystem grades. `Won` / `Lost` / `Unopposed` are read off `seam/wrappers/mass_battle.py`'s lifted `unopposed` marker and each side's `routed` / `conceded` flags, the shape `combat_degree` reads off a scene's own `wound_state` one row above. ⚠ `Declared` COSTS SOMETHING AND THE COST IS STATED HERE, NOT HIDDEN. `04 §C.4:621` fixes a verb at five columns, none conditional on the outcome except through `contests:`; a prize row that defers to ENCOUNTER folds once at RESOLVE writing nothing, under this band, because nothing has been fought yet. That is the price of the seventh-phase timing Jordan chose (M4 planning round 2) over synchronous resolution at RESOLVE, paid in the open rather than smuggled into a verb row nobody reads twice. CP-T04-06 (B10-12) APPENDS `Invested` LAST, SO THE FOUR POSITIONS ABOVE DO NOT MOVE: the band a `march` under the `besiege` posture (`march_postures`) folds on when it meets an opposing side -- no battle is fought, nobody relocates, nobody is hurt, and the garrison Sites in the target's subtree lose condition (`loop/effects_combat.py::_eff_march`). It is read off the provider's `invested` marker (`seam/wrappers/mass_battle.py`), as `Unopposed` is read off `unopposed`. B17.01 APPENDS `Drawn` LAST, AFTER `Invested`, so the five positions above do not move: the band of a fought field in which both sides are out (routed or conceded) or neither is when the ticks ran down (`seam/ladder.py::field_degree`, the one owner of the rule). It writes each side's `body` by its own share and the ration debit, no stance row, and leaves every army at its station (`loop/effects_combat.py::_eff_march`).

field_casualty_models.source: M4, `ED-IN-0279` clause (a). How much `Person.body` a lost field costs -- `wound_harm_models`'s question above, asked of mass_battle's survivor-ratio result instead of a scene's `WoundTracker`.
field_casualty_models.note: ⚠ THE MODELS ARE INVENTED, AS `wound_harm_models`' WERE, AND FOR THE SAME REASON: no ruling states a magnitude. `total` and `none` are the same two controls that row ships: `total` re-runs "losing kills you exactly as winning it does" deliberately, and `none` isolates whether the WRITE ITSELF, rather than its magnitude, is what a defeated side's later choices track (`CLAUDE.md` §0.1 pt 4 -- a number without a control is not a measurement in either direction). ⚠ THE DEFAULT IS `scaled_by_degree`, SET THE SAME WAY `wound_harm_model`'s WAS: A READ, NOT A CHOICE. Jordan's 2026-09-04 ruling on that row -- *"the combat engine determines the result there"* -- is a general principle about who owns a magnitude the engine already computed, and `attacker_size_pct`/`defender_size_pct` (`seam/wrappers/mass_battle.py`'s own `resolve()` return, read from the real dice-pool engine call at `engine_resolve_field`, not invented in this chain) is that same shape of number for a field battle. No fresh ruling settles the magnitude, so this row still ships `assumption`-graded -- but the choice among the three arms is settled by that precedent, not by a pending measurement.

field_winner_casualty_arms.source: CR-24 (M4 Ask B (b)). Whether the WINNING side of a fought field takes casualties too -- `field_casualty_models`' question asked of the winner.
field_winner_casualty_arms.note: `off` is the field as ED-IN-0279 left it (a lost field writes the loser only; nothing is specified for the winner). `engine` writes each winner's `body` by his own side's or subunit's survivor ratio, `body` only: no stance row, no morale hit, and a winner is never appended to `touched`. Under `field_casualty_model: total` a winner takes the same body-to-0 and the same death write a loser does; `none` writes no body on either side.

march_postures.source: CP-T04-06 (B10-12; AM-C-11 REPAIR). How a `march` meets an opposing side: `storm` fights the field (today); `besiege` sits before the walls and wears the garrison.
march_postures.note: THE POSTURE A `march` DECLARES, A PAYLOAD KEY (`posture`) ON `confer`'s `term` PRECEDENT, NOT A `requires_operands` MEMBER: the closed operand vocabulary stays closed. Read by `seam/wrappers/mass_battle.py::resolve`, which answers an opposed `besiege` as `Invested` (no battle, `field_degree_bands`) and an unopposed one as `Unopposed`, as a storm would; `storm` is the default for an act that declares none. `loop/effects_combat.py::_eff_march` writes the wear on the `Invested` band: `condition -= _fall(w, site)` DIRECTLY, for each garrison Site in the target's subtree, because wear staged through `World.stage` at ENCOUNTER is never applied (`loop/encounter.py` has no `take_staged`; the accumulator is RESOLVE-scoped). ⚠ SHIPPED `[storm]`, AND A ONE-MEMBER ROSTER FANS NOTHING: `rosters.yaml: choice_sourced` ranges the posture, and `decision/options.py::_fanned_choices` skips a key whose range has one member, so no `march` Candidate carries a `posture` and every shipped season is what it was. `besiege` joins this list in its own declared-mover commit, whose body must state that `restore` executed on a garrison Site in a natural run (seeds 0-2) after REM-22: until then besiege-then-storm dominates storm, since the wear is permanent. `share` floors `n` at 1, so at a rung with one person present a single besiege act zeroes the walls. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete the roster, the `choice_sourced` line and the `Invested` band, and a march is a storm.]

march_target_kinds.source: M4, `ED-IN-0279` clause (a). What a `march` may target.
march_target_kinds.note: ⚠ A CLOSED SET, NOT AN OPEN ONE, AND THE ROSTER IS CLOSED FOR A REASON BOUND ELSEWHERE. Its members are `settlement` and, on Jordan's ruling (ED-IN-0306 phase 4), `territory` (a territory is marched on, occupied and seized). Person containment never terminates at a settlement rung -- every person's `contain` targets a `home` building beneath one (`harness/populated.py`) -- and `contain_ascends` (`state/world.py`) forbids a sideways move to a foreign settlement, so "the exact rung marched to" is vacuous read literally. Jordan's ruling (M4 planning round 2) is "settlement plus everything under it", which only a `Rung` of kind `settlement` can anchor -- a subtree read, matching `world_q.density`'s existing composition rather than a new one. #353 names no other march target and this roster invented none; a member is added the moment a kind is ruled, as `territory` was. `subtree_occupation_kinds` below says how each is occupied.

subtree_occupation_kinds.source: ED-IN-0306 phase 4. Which `march_target_kinds` are occupied by standing ANYWHERE UNDER them.
subtree_occupation_kinds.note: A settlement's people stand in buildings beneath it (`march_target_kinds`' note), so a faction is occupying a settlement when it is mustered anywhere in its subtree. A territory is not occupied that way: standing in one town of a territory is not occupying the territory, and reading it so would let one won settlement seize the land around it. A territory is occupied by an army that has ARRIVED AT IT (a won or unopposed `march` on the territory), and an army occupying a territory occupies the settlements beneath it as well, so it may seize them (`world_q.occupies`). Every `march_target_kinds` member not listed here is occupied by standing at it.

arrival_only_kinds.source: ED-IN-0306 phase 5. Which rung kinds a person is placed at ONLY by a `march`'s arrival.
arrival_only_kinds.note: A territory is occupied by an army standing AT it (`subtree_occupation_kinds`), and occupation is presence, so a `move` or a `migrate` that could seat a person at a territory would let one member of a faction walk onto a defended territory and seize it with no field. Both decline a destination of these kinds; a won or unopposed `march` is the only act that writes presence there (`_eff_march`'s relocation).

raze_target_kinds.note: `raze` deletes the rung and closes every edge naming it. It stays a settlement's act: `march_target_kinds` gained the territory (a territory is marched on, occupied and seized), and razing the land a duchy stands on is not a thing any act in the game does.

witness_channel_predicates.source: #353 §20 names the five witness channels and gives NONE of them a predicate. `S61`: *"WITNESS AS SPECIFIED FANS EVERY EVENT TO EVERY PERSON. Nothing said in private is private."*
witness_channel_predicates.note: ⚠ THESE PREDICATES ARE AN INJECTED DEFAULT, NOT SOMETHING #353 STATES. `H-33` is graded `assumption` for exactly that reason, and its declared sweep is `total / presence-only / all five`. ⚠ **`total` IS THE CONTROL AND THE SPECIFIED BEHAVIOUR, AND IT IS NOT THE DEFAULT** (`ED-IN-0205`). `R7` chose the architecture model over the echo model -- *legitimacy falls where the news has reached* -- and total fan-out is that echo model at the deposit layer. The shipped arm is `all_five`, in `data/fixtures.py`. **The GRADE does not move with it**: `R7` rules which arm ships and says nothing about what these five predicates are, so they remain an injected default and this row stays `assumption`. ⚠ **UNDER `all_five` THESE PREDICATES DECIDE EVERY DEPOSIT.** Under `total`, `observers_for` returned everyone and they were never consulted. Only THREE of the five can admit anyone in a world the fold can currently drive (`reach` matches nobody there, no `binding_decision` verb resolving, and `post_remit` needs an obligee standing at the seat an act was exercised through; `test_w6_every_named_channel_has_a_predicate_and_they_are_data` asserts exactly which two are inert). Every predicate below is computed from WORLD STATE and never from a recipient the emitter declared -- §19.3 is explicit that an Event carries NO TARGET, *"observers are computed at WITNESS from presence; the emitter declares no recipient"*, so a channel that needed the emitter to name someone would be a different design and not a fill of this hole. ⚠ `reach` IS DELIBERATELY NOT `everyone`. A public channel that matched every person would make the `all_five` union identical to `total`, and the sweep would have two points that are the same arm wearing different names -- an arrangement that cannot measure anything. It admits the persons standing within the reach the Event's kind states (`witness_channels.event_reach`): what a binding decision emits is news to the realm it is the decision of, because a binding decision is the design's own category for an act whose effect is institutional rather than private. A person outside it, or a decision with no place, is not admitted. (It REPLACED `chronicle`, CR-29: a kind filter that read no person and so admitted every person alive, wherever they stood.)

predicates.co_located: the person shares a live `contain` Tenure with the Event's place -- the presence index S28 already builds and the fan-out never read
predicates.document_key: the person holds a live `hold` Tenure over something THIS EVENT CHANGED -- a subject named in `changes[]` (a Record, a store). ⚠ THIS ROW READ *the Event's SUBJECT* until `R8.4`, and that clause is why the channel could not fire on a single act: every fold-emitted Event sets `subject = a.actor` and no `hold` takes a PERSON as object, so the equality held only on `MATTER`/`CALENDAR` kinds, which carry no verb and no actor. The parenthetical was always right and the clause it qualified was wrong. Corrected here in the same change as the predicate, because this row is where the meaning lives (see the note above) and `R5` quotes it verbatim as the channel's definition
predicates.witness_key: the person IS the Event's anchor (`state/attribution.py::anchor_of` -- the actor where one acted, the written thing otherwise; it read the deleted `Event.subject` until G1b), or shares a live `knot` Tenure with it -- S28's knot deposit, which already reuses the Event id
predicates.post_remit: the person is an OBLIGEE of the seat the Event's act was exercised through (`Act.via`) -- a live `oblige` Tenure to it, read through `queries/world_q.py::establishment_of`, the one owner of that set -- AND stands AT that seat: the seat's rung is where they are or above it (`state/gate.py::purview_reaches`). Plan position `17a`, r2 item 9. ⚠ THIS ROW READ *the person holds a live office Tenure whose remit covers the verb that emitted this kind* until `17a` -- a remit-holder learning of every covered act anywhere in the realm, the place-blind broadcast r2 `02` §A.7 and `01` both delete. An Event no act caused, or an act exercised through no seat, admits nobody through this predicate. ONE other admission rides this channel's source (`inferred`) and its live/off switch, in `loop/witness.py` (v9 IN-22): an ACTORLESS Event's observation READS (MATTER's recorded shortfall) go to the holders of a live seat whose purview reaches the read rung (`queries/world_q.py::governors_of`) -- reads only, never an event-kind, `seen` or `content:` claim
predicates.reach: the Event's kind has a reach in `event_reach` and the person stands within it -- in the Event's own place for `room`, else inside the rung of that kind that contains the Event's place (CR-29: news of an event reaches persons by the event's kind, at a stated reach)

observation_terms.source: `R8.1`, `references/design_rulings_2026-09-06.md` -- Jordan: *"I saw this person doing y, but I don't know what y is"*, *"someone looking like y did x"*, *"they saw someone skulking around for no reason they could discern"*. One `seen` claim per (witness, event), BESIDE the two existing deposits; its value is a frozen struct of these four terms, each `None` where the channel withholds it
observation_terms.note: `values:` IS THE STRUCT, IN FIELD ORDER -- `epistemic.Seen` refuses at import if its fields and this list differ, and every term needs a `_term_<name>` reader there (the `CHANNEL_PREDICATES` precedent: a named member with no reader RAISES, never quietly reads `None`). `stratum` is the coarse WHAT (`strata`), never the verb TOKEN -- a witness can say *someone was doing something social* without naming `tell`. ⚠ Not never the INFORMATION: `movement` has two members (`move`, `migrate`), so a `movement` witness does not know which (`epistemic._term_stratum`'s docstring). `marks` is the actor's appearance and carries ONE member, the actor's `Person.heritage` (descent): `(heritage,)` where it is authored and `()` where it is not (`epistemic._term_marks`), public at co-location and deposited true and verbatim, as `who` is. `()` means *seen, and nothing describable*, and `None` means *this channel does not show a body at all*. `who` is the actor's id. `why` is an antecedent claim the witness holds (below), not a motive. ⚠ `supplied_by:` IS WHAT EACH CHANNEL SHOWS, and a witness's struct is the UNION over the channels that admit them under the live `fan_out_mode` (`epistemic.live_channels`). The `total` arm is `H-33`'s control and shows EVERY term to every witness, so this table is read only by the narrow arms. Two cells are ruled: `R8.5` quotes the ratified line *"a co-located witness saw who acted; a document holder saw only that the document changed"* -- so `document_key` shows NOTHING, and its witness holds an all-`None` struct, which IS deposited (the claim's subject still says WHERE something happened). `witness_key`, `post_remit` and `reach` are unruled: they withhold rather than invent, and are an injected default in `H-33`'s sense, exactly as the channel predicates themselves are. `why` IS THE ANTECEDENT A WITNESS HOLDS AND MAY CONNECT, NOT THE ACTOR'S MOTIVE (B09.17, `R8.4` narrowed; the engine keeps no motive: `Candidate.why` is dropped at `pack_scenes` and `Act` carries none): the id of a claim in the witness's OWN ledger that was deposited from an antecedent Event of the one he witnessed (`epistemic._term_why`). A channel that supplies `why` (`co_located`, `witness_key`) makes the witness ELIGIBLE; whether he connects them is one keyed draw at `Fixtures connection_chance` (`H-458`), which ships 0.0, so no deposit carries `why` until B98 raises it, and case 4 (*no discernible reason*) is still every deposit. `document_key` never supplies it (`R8.5`, ruled). `Person.heritage` has ONE writer, the world build (`data/cast.py::heritage_of`), and `marks` shows it wherever `who` is shown -- so case 2 (*someone looking like y*, `who=None`) is supported by the struct and reached by nothing until a recognition producer exists (`R8.2`).

undeposited_kinds.note: ⚠ THE EVENT KINDS WHOSE EVENT-KIND CLAIM WITNESS NEVER MAKES (`loop/witness.py::witness`): an Event of one of these kinds stays in the log and in its act's causes and is witnessed like any other Event -- the actor's own observation reads (at `observation_deposit_mode: actor`; a refused `examine` leaves its actor the refusing `present_at` read, so his next deliberation declines it) and the `seen` claim of each witness present (a bystander holds that someone tried) -- but nobody holds `(subject, <kind>, True)`. obstacle_terms.source: B05.14, B05.15, B05.17, B05.21 (`proposals/U5c_SC_one_obstacle_form.md` §1, §2; 29_DICE Item 29-4 step 4; PES-A; `proposals/13_SC_tuning_tables.md` T2-T4): the members the obstacle is composed of, in OBS §2's order
obstacle_terms.note: THE TERMS OF THE SOCIAL ROLL'S OBSTACLE, IN COMPOSITION ORDER (`roll.py::obstacle` sums them, then the document's lane A step, then the ceiling and the floor). `even` -- the pool's even line, `MU_PER_DIE x pool_add` (`sigma_leverage.even_line`); `difficulty` -- the act's own, its level's size (`Fixtures.difficulty_ob`); `opposition` -- the one acted against, `opposed_ob(opposing attribute + skill score, opposition_rate)`, or the untrained score where no person is opposite (never absent); `standard` -- what the room demands (OBS §2 member 3; B05.21): for an act a bench hears on a docketed matter, the size (`Fixtures.difficulty_ob`) of the `standard:` level of the arrangement row the matter is docketed under; `stakes` -- the weight of what the act would take or impose (member 5): `Fixtures.stakes_ob` of the Tenure kind the act opens (a kind the verb alone opens, or the one the docketed row `disposes:` for a verb that opens several); `rank_gap` -- how far the person acted on or for stands above the actor's exercised seat (member 6; B21.09, landed with its first reader, `establish`): `rank_step x` the `rung_kinds` steps from the rung of the seat `Act.via` names up to the subject's (a rung's own kind; a person's highest held seat's rung), 0 where the subject stands at or below it; `regard` -- the counterparty's hostility to the actor (member 7): `regard_step x clamp(-stance / STANCE_MAX, 0, 1)` over the stance rows he holds toward the actor (`person_q.stance_toward`), for one person counterparty and no audience (its favourable half is leverage, `advantage_sources: favour`); `reception` -- the audience's hostility (OBS §2 member 8; B05.17): a bench that regards the speaker ill raises the obstacle by `reception_gain x |reception|` (`world_q.reception`, the hostile half, for a prize a room hears, 0 where none hears it; its favourable half is leverage, `advantage_sources: favour`); `capability` -- a circumstance that punishes a want, the sum over the `circumstance` rows of `tables: capability_uses` for the act's site whose `when` holds, each its held value times its `gain` (B05.15; no row ships, so it stands at 0); `cross_chain` -- a conferral across chains of seats (OBS §2 member 29; B21.61, `confer`'s): `cross_chain_step x` 1 where the seat the act names and the seat it is exercised through are of different factions (`gate.across_chains`; the seat is read off a prize row saying its act names one, `loop/sides.py::seat_named_by`); `faction_power` -- the power of the holder's faction against the host's (B21.69, `IS-B3-FA-07`, A-105; the act is `revoke`, a reduction of a sitting holder's grant included, or any act whose prize says it names a seat and is opposed by that seat's holder): `faction_power_step x` 1 where the faction the live holder coheres under outweighs the faction of the seat the act is exercised through (the band above 1 of `faction_q.weight` of the one over the other, read as a comparison so a faction with no members divides nothing), and nothing where it is the same faction or the weaker (`sigma.py::_faction_power_of`). Every member stands AGAINST the act and is never negative. `even`, `difficulty`, `opposition`, `reception` and `capability` stand in every act's terms (at 0.0 where they weigh nothing); `standard`, `stakes`, `rank_gap`, `regard`, `cross_chain` and `faction_power` are listed only where they weigh, so a world whose five are at their control sizes carries the terms it carried before them (the terms are folded into the Event's `ending` and so into the content hash). A member lands with its host function in `sigma.OBSTACLE_TERMS` and no other code; later members are those the verb lanes add (OBS §2's table). B24p.05: EVERY MEMBER IS BOUND (`bound:` below) to ONE reader, never both and never neither. `host` -- read by its function in `sigma.OBSTACLE_TERMS` (the eight above). `module` -- the proceeding's own, supplied by `modules/social_contest/proceeding.py` (its `TERMS`, B24p.07) as a raw operand and a step on the record the one composer (`roll.py::obstacle`) reads, so there is no second composer: `weary` (the Will his staying power has spent, V2 p2 §C.2's `weary(V)`), `standing` (the other side's circumstances unless his Reason accounts for them, `gap(V)`), `press` (`press_ob`, on a press only) and `gravity` (the close's and the abridged form's). `data/rosters.py::obstacle_bound` reads the column and refuses a value but these two; `sigma.py` refuses at import a `host` member with no function (and a function with no member) and, at the first call of the module, a `module` member the module's `TERMS` lacks. `standard` stays `host`: inside a proceeding the venue's standard is Grace's `esteem` on the leverage, never an obstacle (B24p.19 omits it for an act on the `proceeds=` path). No leverage source is module-bound. B24.06 adds `answer` (module-bound, last): the hostile weight of an answered exhibit over its answer, `answer_step x max(0, w_target - w_answer)`, on the roll of an `answer` move only (HEAR_B's table; a heavier answer is never a subtraction, A-25, it is the closing draw's `proof_level`). B24.26 adds `first_heard` (module-bound, last; OBS §2 member 11, ADM edit 4): `first_heard_ob` for the answer to an item the room heard FIRST (a `filed` stage's first-heard mark, `Item.first`), the answer move's own roll and the answering `speak`'s (`Input.first_heard`, which the host builder reads off the stages its `answers` name), listed only where it weighs. One reader: the proceeding's `TERMS`; the single-roll host never composes it, the answering `speak` being an act that proceeds.

contest_subsystems.note: ⚠ A CONTEST IS A DISPATCH, NOT A GENERIC ROLL. Jordan, 2026-09-02: *"a contest seems like it can be a call for a different subsystem like personal combat, mass battle or social contest."* The three subsystems each have a doc, a sim module and a declared resolver (`d_sigma` for all three), so the seam dispatches to them rather than rolling generically. ⚠ JORDAN, 2026-09-02, VERBATIM: *"we aren't using the .md or anything for those systems. those are super outdated. you are allowed to refer to the currently existing python work for those systems (and only those systems) in repository."* So the LIVE artifact for each is its Python, not its `*_v30.md`: `systems/combat/combat_engine_v1/`, `systems/mass_battle/sim/`, and for the social contest `modules/social_contest/` (its SC05 kernel, `systems/social_contest/sim/contest/`, was retired at B24.33, ED-SC-0045: its game lives in the hearing). `contest_subsystem` reads `sim_module:` and never `doc:` for that reason. This roster maps a PRIZE to the subsystem that owns it. The prize is what Part E's column carries; the subsystem is what `module_contracts.yaml` already names, so neither half is invented here.

The host input builder's own site (`seam/wrappers/sigma.py::_obstacle_of`, once the former row H-127) was deleted at step 14; the social contest module composes the obstacle (`modules/social_contest/roll.py::obstacle`, under `H-213`'s ceiling). So `interim: true` carried CLAUSE (2) ALONE, and steps 13 + 15 discharged it: the row names `social_contest` (`02 §D.4`).
