knowledge_kinds.source: `H-85`; NPC-087's own `season_requires` supplies the two values
knowledge_kinds.note: ⚠ THE GATE IS NOT HERE AND THAT IS THE POINT. #353 §9.2 says *"The only class-shaped gate in the design is Thread Sensitivity"* and supplies no carrier, no predicate and no taxonomy for it to gate OVER. This roster is the taxonomy half — the half `rosters.yaml` is the ruled home for. The VERB gate is built since v9 PC-06 K-3 (`thread_read`'s typed cell over `Person.thread_sensitivity`, `H-85`/`H-239`); a gate over these KINDS is not: no code reads this roster, so `thread_substrate` gates nothing yet (`H-85`). The two values are NPC-087's own: material "retainable by ordinary non-sensitive minds" against "Thread-substrate knowledge subject to the setting's epistemological barrier". A third kind, or a per-subject scheme, is `H-85`'s sweep, not an edit anyone should make here without moving the row.

site_kinds.note: ⚠ THE SET IS EXTENSIBLE AND THE LOOKUP STILL REFUSES, and those are different properties. Adding a kind means adding a row here; asking about a kind that has no row RAISES, because §42.2.1's worked example is exactly this table: *"a wear table that returns 20 for an unregistered site kind does not fail — it answers, plausibly and wrongly, forever."* ⚠ `harbour`, `seam` AND `body` ARE THE INSTRUMENT'S, NOT #353's, so `H-07` is `assumption`, not transcription. ⚠⚠ `body` IS NOT A SITE. It is `(Person, body)`'s band row, here because `band_floors` keys on THIS roster and `H-38` ruled *"`Site.condition` is the model"* — no second scheme. See `p32`. ⚠ `dwelling` IS JORDAN'S, 2026-09-25 (`ED-SE-0055`): `ED-SE-0051`'s `capacity(w, rung)` counts *"the rung's dwelling Sites"*, and he chose to make that phrase literal rather than re-read it as the hearth rungs. `harness/populated.build_realm` mints one per `hearth` rung. A site kind needs a `wear_per_season` and a `band_floors` row (`data/fixtures.py`'s `_load_matter_tables` refuses one without); `dwelling` has no `site_yield` row, because a dwelling produces nothing and that table's `default_cell` is 0. ⚠ `garrison` IS JORDAN'S, 2026-09-28 (`ED-IN-0279` clause (a), M4): asked how a settlement's fortification should be modelled, given he wants it build-able and upgradeable, he chose *"a Site's condition"* over a cohort-Person alternative -- `H-38`'s *"`Site.condition` is the model"* ruling applied to fortification rather than a second scheme invented for it. It needs the same two rows `dwelling` does, and has no `site_yield` row for `dwelling`'s reason: a wall produces nothing. The `restore` verb (`writes: Site.condition`) raises any fabric its actor stands at toward the ceiling a works allows (the full scale where none names it).

matter_kinds.source: #353 §10.4 VERBATIM: *It is a type parameter, not an enumeration. Grain, salt, timber, ore and coin are rows in a registry, not members of a closed set in a source file.*
matter_kinds.note: ⚠ OPEN MEANS ADDABLE, NOT UNCHECKED — and this file is the registry §10.4 asks for. #353 forbids *a closed set in a source file*; it does not license a lookup that answers for a kind nobody registered. Both halves hold here: add a kind by adding a row, and a draw against an unregistered kind raises. ⚠ THE FIVE ARE #353's OWN EXAMPLES and nothing more. It names them as illustrations of what a row looks like, so starting the registry with exactly them is the least-invented content available — but it is still a choice, which is what `H-11` grades.

arms_kinds.source: v11 CP-T03-03 (`-08` AM-C-04; T03 home §2): arms are `matter_kinds` members, so a person's kit is what the rungs he holds store.
arms_kinds.note: `kinds:` maps an ARMS KIND to the one Combatant field it fills and the key it sets there: `{<kind>: {field: weapon|armor, key: <a weapons.py WEAPONS key | an armour tier>, rank: <int>}}`. Each kind must be a `matter_kinds` member, `field` one of the fields `engine/substrate/combat_kit.py::FIELDS` names, `key` a member of THAT FIELD'S closed set in the same module (the typed `kit` section of `engine/engine_params/combat_engine_v1.json`, `tools/export_engine_params.py --check`) and `rank` a whole number, unique among the kinds of one field; refused whole at import otherwise (`data/rosters.py::_check_arms_kinds`). The key sets are never copied here. `queries/world_q.py::kit_of` is the one reader: per field, the highest-ranked kind with a positive count in the stores of the rungs the person holds, else of his residence, else the Combatant's own default. ⚠ EMPTY ON PURPOSE: which arms exist, which key each sets and how they rank is Jordan's content and is not invented here (`-08` AM-C-04). While `kinds:` is empty `kit_of` returns the Combatant default for everyone and every fight is dealt exactly as before the mechanism existed.

arms_at_build.source: v11 CP-T03-03 (`-08` AM-C-04): the arms a rung is built holding, by the rung's kind [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct].
arms_at_build.note: `kinds:` maps a RUNG KIND to the stores that kind of rung is seeded with when a realm is built: `{<rung kind>: {<arms kind>: <positive whole number>}}`. Every key must be a `rung_kinds` member, every inner key an `arms_kinds` member (so a seed can only name an arm that has a kind), every amount a positive whole number; refused whole at import otherwise (`data/rosters.py::_check_arms_at_build`). `harness/populated.py::build_realm` is the one seeder (`seed_arms`). ⚠ EMPTY ON PURPOSE, as `arms_kinds` is: the inventory is Jordan's content, so no rung is built holding arms and `build_realm`'s world is unchanged.

wear_per_season.source: #353 §22 assigns `wear per site kind` to params; no in-chain table exists. `H-07`.
wear_per_season.note: ⚠ `W8`: per-kind wear and floors are registry rows rather than `DEFAULT_FIXTURES` literals. `DEFAULT_FIXTURES` READS this mapping, so the declaration lives once. ⚠ `dwelling: 0` IS THE CONTROL ARM, SHIPPED DELIBERATELY, and it is `H-07`'s own *"no wear at all"* sweep point applied to one kind. ⚠ **NOT THE SAME SHAPE AS `body_step = 0`**: that arm `continue`s past the write itself (`loop/matter.py`), so nothing is emitted at its control arm. `wear_per_season` skips the same way since `H-135` (B09.21): MATTER does not write a Site whose wear is 0, so `dwelling: 0` emits nothing (see below). A dwelling sits AT a hearth and persons live in hearths. A non-zero rate together with any floor in `band_floors.dwelling` would let a dwelling's condition cross it; the crossing Event is witnessed `co_located`, and the claim it deposits (subject = the dwelling) would then reach every co-located resident as a live `claim_landed` question, once `reach`/`place_of` (`queries/world_q.py`) admit a claim about a place through a person's own ledger. That would put a dwelling-condition Question in front of every resident every season, which is exactly what `test_24d_i_the_control_arm_crosses_no_band_and_moves_no_question_in_one_season`'s control-arm identity pins against. Either half at its control arm blocks the crossing; both ship there. At 0 no dwelling's condition moves. ⚠ ZERO IS SILENT SINCE `H-135` (B09.21). `loop/matter.py`'s wear loop writes a Site only where its wear this season is non-zero, and `World.write` emits one `condition.worn` per write (`H-12`), so a dwelling emits no wear Event and its residents witness no claim of it. A non-zero rate is chosen with a consumer in front of it, at `24e`/`24f`, never here. ⚠ `garrison: 0` IS `dwelling`'s CONTROL ARM FOR THE SAME REASON (M4, `ED-IN-0279` clause (a)): a non-zero rate would erode every garrison's condition every season, silently drifting every field battle's fortification term toward zero over a long campaign. The rate is a pacing decision (where every fabric sits at rest), registered rather than taken -- `H-165` and `H-07` (the rate). `restore` is formed nowhere since REM-22 (its `verb_table.yaml` row: no question the realm delivers carries a Site among its referents) until `16_PESSIMIST_WR_B` edit 4 (B12a.66), and since then only where a person witnesses a crossing at the rung he stands on; at a broken Site it is declined under the coupling (B12a.65). The settlement fabrics (harbour, seam) wear at rate 10, so `H-165`'s limit is the DWELLING/GARRISON rate specifically, both `0`.

capacity_floor.source: `RULINGS.yaml` RR-2 (`ED-SE-0051`, ruled 2026-09-17): *"a `capacity(w, rung)` QUERY over the rung's dwelling Sites, with a FLOOR — never a fixture table"*; `01_THE_BUILD_ORDER.md` S10: *"the floor is a table keyed on site kind, beside `band_floors`"*. Plan position `24d-ii`, landed with its caller at `19c`.
capacity_floor.note: ⚠ ITS CELLS HOLD THE FLOOR AND NOTHING ELSE (plan `24d-ii`). A cell is a LOWER BOUND on `queries/world_q.py::capacity`'s derived quantity -- `max(floor, the dwelling Sites at the rung and below)` -- never what one dwelling houses: a per-kind *houses N* cell is capacity AUTHORED per kind, the `hearth_capacity` fixture RR-2 refused, a second home for a fact the Sites carry. What is derived is the count of Sites itself. ⚠ WHY 1 FOR `dwelling`: RR-2's own reasoning -- the floor keeps a population from being throttled to zero by a rung with no dwelling at all, *"the same shape as `W5`'s own floor-of-1 choice for budget"*. The number is that precedent's, not a ruling's, so `H-167` grades it and sweeps it: `zero` is RR-2's refused reading and the CONTROL (a rung with no dwelling houses nobody), `doubled` the other side. ⚠ THE OTHER FOUR CELLS ARE 0 AND `capacity` READS NONE OF THEM TODAY: it counts `dwelling` Sites (`world_q.DWELLING_KIND`, Jordan's `ED-SE-0055`: *"capacity queries descendant Sites of that kind"*). They are here because the table is keyed on the whole `site_kinds` roster and `data/fixtures.py` checks it in both directions, as it checks `wear_per_season` and `band_floors` -- so a missing `dwelling` row REFUSES at load instead of silently flooring every rung at nothing. A second housing kind is a roster row, a cell here, and `capacity`'s count widened with it.

works_cost.source: v9 IN-28 (`H-166` limit 1, its own design order: the cost first). r2 `proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/04_MATTER_AND_WORKS.md` §A.6.6 (intent): *"the cost is paid by `transfer` into the works' rung"*, and nothing debited that rung when the place rose. `proposals/2026-09-10-settlements-factions-populations/04_EVALUATION.md` §6 (intent): `found` costs *"the stake"*, `build` costs *"timber"*.
works_cost.note:
WHAT A WORKS' PLAN COSTS: `{plan kind: {matter kind: amount}}`, paid out of the WORKS' RUNG (`Record.rung`, where the works is kept and where `transfer` delivers to it) when the place rises. `loop/effects_founding.py` is the one reader. `found` moves its stake TWO-SIDED into the Rung it founds, so the grain stays in the world and provisions the new hearth (`_shift`, the one body of a conserved store move). `build` CONSUMES its cost into the fabric, one-sided, a lawful sink. 04_EVALUATION §6 S passes the pair in exactly that shape: *"`build` debits one side as a lawful consumption sink; `found` is two-sided"*. ⚠ A PLAN KIND WITH NO ROW HAS NO PRICE, SO NOBODY CAN PAY FOR IT, AND `found`/`build` REFUSE IT. That is a refusal that emits, never a free place: a missing row is not a cost of zero. The loader checks one way only -- every key a `rung_kinds` or `site_kinds` member, every cell non-empty, every matter kind a `matter_kinds` member, every amount a positive int (`data/fixtures.py::_load_works_cost`). It is NOT keyed on `site_kinds` in both directions as `wear_per_season` is, because three groups of members get no row by design:
  * `body` IS NOT A SITE (`site_kinds`' own note). A works planning one is refused here, by the
    roster, rather than by a kind literal in `_eff_build` (`H-166` limit 4, narrowed: `body`
    stays in `site_kinds` for `band_floors`).
  * `person` is CENSUS's to mint (F.30), never a works'.
  * `settlement` and above are unpriced: founding a settlement collides with SE-9(a)'s held
    question (*"never adding nodes"* to the fixed settlement registry), and 02_PROPOSALS P4
    restricts founding to `hearth` and `community` for that reason.
[ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete this roster and its reader, and `found`/`build` cost nothing again (`H-166` limit 1 reopens)]. THE KINDS are 04_EVALUATION's (grain for the stake, timber for a fabric). THE AMOUNT IS INVENTED and it is ONE number, 10, for every row: `site_yield.seam.timber` is 10, so a fabric costs one season of a full seam's timber, and the stake reuses the same magnitude so the two verbs share one scale rather than two. `H-166` sweeps it; `halved` and `doubled` scale every cell.

site_endowment.note: WHAT PRODUCING SITES A SETTLEMENT IS GIVEN AT THE WORLD'S MAKING, keyed on the geography's territory code and, past it, on a settlement code (`data/fixtures.py::endowment_for` is the one reader; `boot/realm.py::build_realm`'s site loop the one minter). `uniform` is the control, today's placement at every settlement; `ground` is the arm, read when `Fixtures.endowment_mode` is `ground`. A list names one Site per entry; a kind named twice is two Sites. The loader (`data/fixtures.py::_check_site_endowment`) refuses a territory holding a settlement with no row, a kind outside `site_kinds`, an empty list, and a key no geography row carries. Every row is [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: `endowment_mode` `uniform`]. T15 holds no settlement, so it has no row.

subsistence_weight.source: `H-11` — *the subsistence formula over an OPEN MatterKind registry*. ARCHITECTURE_V2.md's default: *draw from the containing rung's stores, scaled by weight*.
subsistence_weight.note: ⚠ THE WEIGHTS ARE INVENTED AND THE ROW IS WHAT MAKES THAT LAWFUL. #353 states the SHAPE — a draw from the containing rung's stores, scaled per kind — and supplies no numbers, so this is an injected default with a `site:` and a sweep, exactly as `wear_per_season` beside it. ⚠ A KIND WITH NO WEIGHT IS NOT A KIND WITH WEIGHT ZERO. A missing row RAISES rather than drawing nothing, for `wear`'s reason: a silent zero is a person who eats nothing and never starves, which is a plausible wrong answer that no test would ever surface. ⚠ ONLY `grain` AND `salt` CARRY A WEIGHT, and that is deliberate rather than an omission: timber, ore and coin are stored and not eaten. They are registered in `matter_kinds` and absent here, so a draw against them raises — which is the refusal above doing its job on the very first kind somebody adds to a larder by mistake.

hunger_bands.source: REM-50, as repaired by AM-A-04 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v10_part13.md`, REM-50): a settlement's hunger, read by `world_q.hunger`
hunger_bands.note: The bands of a settlement's hunger, MOST SEVERE FIRST. The first, `starving`, is `unmet > 0` (the next draw leaves a mouth unfed) and the last, `fed`, is "under no floor"; neither is a floor. The members between them are the FLOOR bands, in the order `Fixtures.hunger_band_floors` lists their floors (`world_q.HUNGER_FLOOR_BANDS`). A roster of fewer than two members cannot name `starving` and `fed` and raises at import (`world_q`'s unpack).

seasons_of_year.source: ED-IN-0332 (RULED, D-U1-10): the year is a roster; `data/fixtures.py` already speaks of "two years at four seasons"
seasons_of_year.note: THE YEAR, IN ORDER; ITS LENGTH IS THE YEAR (`data/rosters.py::SEASONS_OF_YEAR`, the one owner). The season of the year a tick falls in is `tick % len(SEASONS_OF_YEAR)` (`world_q.season_of_year`), read off the clock and stored nowhere; every age in seasons, every yearly term and the weather read the length and no file states a literal. `season_factor_draw`, when non-empty, holds one entry per member here, in this order, and is refused at `season_factor_of` otherwise. The four names are `[ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]`; the length is the ruling.

factions.note: ⚠ SOURCED FROM `systems/world/` BECAUSE JORDAN RULED THE PRECEDENCE. Jordan, 2026-09-02: *"systems/factions, systems/settlements are for inspiration/reference only. systems/world contains information to use regarding factions ... but for the identity/names/organizations it is canon"*, then: *"systems/factions if it concerns directly the identity of a faction can be concerned near-canon but superseded by anything in world."* A faction's NAME is identity, so this roster is world's to give. See the file header for the three-tier order. ⚠ `Ministry of the Peninsula` IS EXCLUDED BY THE NEAR-CANON SOURCE'S OWN WORDS. It appears ZERO times in all of `systems/world/`, and `faction_canon_v30.md:374` says of it: *"Treated as institutional infrastructure, NOT a faction."* An office may still BELONG to a ministry — that is `office_bodies`' `Ministries` row, which is what a ministry actually is here. ⚠ TWO NAMES IN CIRCULATION ARE SUPERSEDED AND ARE NOT MEMBERS. `People's Revolution` (`southernmost_v30.md` §6.2, one occurrence) is the old name for `Restoration Movement` — `geography_v30.md`'s ED-061 is *"'Revolution' -> 'Restoration Movement' naming standardisation across all docs"*, i.e. the rename is ordered and unpropagated, not a second faction. `Niflhel` is DISSOLVED: `worldbuilding_v30.md` §3.2 renames the mechanic *"Olafsson-Broker Exposure (formerly Olafsson-Niflhel)"* and §10 says *"post-Niflhel-dissolution"*. ⚠ `Schoenland` IS A MEMBER AND IS FOREIGN. Canon gives it T16 and Altonian naval passage (`geography_v30.md`). ⚠ THE TYPED LAYER CARRIES NO T16 ROW AND THAT IS DELIBERATE, NOT A GAP TO FILL: `references/world_initial_state.yaml:44` (retired) — *"There is no T16 — the gap is in the source data"* — and `harness/populated.py:331`. No `role_template`; recorded, not filled. ⚠ REFERENCE, NOT MECHANISM (§0.05), AND A FACTION STILL NEVER ACTS. `ARCHITECTURE_V2.md:93` lists a faction acting among five refusals held under all 143 cases. This roster names what an OFFICE BELONGS TO; the actor is always the person holding the office.

role_templates.source: `systems/factions/reference/faction_canon_v30.md` §4 'Role Templates and Expected Convictions', per PP-686 §3.3.1 over the PP-684 13-Conviction taxonomy.
role_templates.note: ⚠ TIER 2 — NEAR-CANON, AND IT SURVIVES BECAUSE WORLD IS SILENT, NOT BECAUSE IT OUTRANKS ANYTHING. Jordan: *"systems/factions if it concerns directly the identity of a faction can be concerned near-canon but superseded by anything in world."* §4 binds each template to a weighted conviction vector and to a player-eligible faction — that is directly a faction's identity — and `systems/world/` has no competing role-template concept, so there is nothing to be superseded BY. The day world says otherwise, world wins and this roster changes. ⚠ TWO FACTIONS HAVE NO TEMPLATE, RECORDED AS AN ABSENCE BY NAME (the roster's size is not an invariant — RULED 2026-09-19; v9 IN-36 adds a THIRD, `Altonia`, which has a head and no template, below). §4's player-eligible column covers Crown, Church of Solmund, Hafenmark, Varfell, Löwenritter and Restoration Movement. `Guilds` and `Schoenland` are absent from it. `faction_role_template` leaves them out rather than assigning a plausible one — inventing `mercantile-procedural` for the Guilds is exactly the fabrication the source-precedence ruling exists to prevent, and it would read as canon a session later. ⚠ `intelligence-diplomatic` IS UNCLAIMED BY ANY FACTION AND STAYS IN THE ROSTER. §4's own note assigns Varfell to `military-order` on Jordan's 2026-04-19 decision that Vaynard expansion is *"purely military"*, leaving this template a candidate nothing holds. It is a member because a corpus case may name an intelligence office; it binds to no faction.

faction_leaders.source: systems/factions/reference/faction_state_authoring_v30.md — each faction block's own `leader:` field (crown :44 `almud`, church_of_solmund :92 `cardinal_himlensendt`, hafenmark :144 `baralta`, varfell :193 `vaynard`, restoration_movement :248 `yrsa_vossen`, lowenritter :302 `ehrenwall`). TIER 2, and it survives because `systems/world/` names no competing leader.
faction_leaders.note: ⚠ **WHY A FACTION NEEDS A PERSON AT ALL: Q4's REFERENT.** ⭐ Jordan ruled 2026-09-13 that a faction's creed is an `OUGHT`. `world_q.questions_for`'s Q4 raises a standing question from every live `commit` to an OUGHT and emits `(prop.subject,)` as the referent — and a faction NAME is not a person and not even a rung, so a creed subject-ed on the faction would put a non-entity into every member's deliberation (`ED-IN-0210` Ruling 1: *"verbs invoke mechanisms or interactions between a character and another entity/character. they are not fiats."*). So the creed is subject-ed on the faction's LEADER, who is a person an act can name. ⚠ **EACH AUTHORED SLUG RESOLVES TO EXACTLY ONE OF THE 46 REGISTRY ROWS**, by surname match: `cardinal_himlensendt` is Arne Himlensendt (NPC-021) and `ehrenwall` is Lisbeth Ehrenwall (NPC-070) — neither spelling appears in the roster the way the faction file writes it, which is why this is a transcribed mapping and not a runtime string match. ⚠ **SIX OF EIGHT, AND THE SAME TWO ARE MISSING AS EVERYWHERE ELSE.** `Guilds` and `Schoenland` have no authored leader — and no `role_template`, and no expected-conviction vector. That is consistent rather than coincidental: a faction canon gives no head and no expectations has no creed to commit to, and this file does not invent one for it.

foreign_cast.source: v9 IN-36 (#457 D4, answered RS-21 item 4 [medium; Jordan to correct]: one foreign faction, two seats, in `references/npc_registry.yaml`), read by `harness/populated.py::build_realm(foreign=)` through `data/rosters.py::FOREIGN_CAST`.
foreign_cast.note: WHAT THIS IS. The factions whose persons and places `build_realm(foreign=True)` seats and `foreign=False` (the control arm; the shipped default is `True` since ED-IN-0310) leaves out of the world: a faction named here has no Proposition, no member, no seat, no goal and no rung in the control arm, so that arm is byte-identical to the realm before the empire existed. A foreign faction is still a `factions` member in BOTH arms (`names_index.yaml: token_class: faction` is its owner), which is what puts it in `data/rosters.py::FACTION_BY_PROP` and lets `cast.faction_of` resolve its cast rows with no edit. ⚠ `Schoenland` IS NOT HERE AND IS FOREIGN ALL THE SAME: its persons and its T16 root are already in the realm as built (`build_realm` keeps T16 out of the realm by giving it no parent), so a switch on it would move a world that does not need to move. This block is the factions whose WHOLE existence is new, and it is not a roster of every foreign faction. WHAT A ROW SAYS. `territory` is the foreign ROOT RUNG, a `territory` with no `contain` edge into `r_valoria` -- never a `realm`, so `endings_reached`'s victory selector (every territory under a `realm` rung) and `populated.census`'s `uncontrolled_in_realm` do not count it; the BORDER is that absence. `settlement` is the one place its persons live, under the root. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct] The codes are the author's, and a place has a code and no name because a `Rung` carries no name (`state/carriers.py`): canon names Altonia's chokepoint only as T3's `Lowenskyst Fortress` (`venues.yaml`), not a homeland place. `ALT` is the empire's frontier territory and `ALT-1` its staging post, the settlement the Katepano and the Kommerkiarios seat at. office_bodies.source: `systems/world/reference/worldbuilding_v30.md` §6.1 (Court Parliament and Governance), §3.1 (Church Four-Cardinal structure), §4.1 (Löwenritter internal structure), §5.1 (Guild structure).
office_bodies.note: ⚠ THIS IS THE *TYPE OF OFFICE* AXIS JORDAN ASKED FOR, AND IT IS CANON'S OWN ORGANIZATION NAMES RATHER THAN A TAXONOMY FOLDED OUT OF THEM. Jordan, 2026-09-02: *"does the office schema include faction belonging, scale of office, type of office, etc?"* World gives four tables of bodies with a Function column each; collapsing those functions into a tidy set (`judicial, military, economic, knowledge, administrative, ...`) is NOT TAKEN. World is canon for ORGANIZATIONS; an invented functional taxonomy sitting where canon named bodies would read as canon to the next session, which is the defect the precedence ruling names. ⚠ `faction` AND `function` ARE PROPERTIES OF THE BODY, SO AN OFFICE AUTHORS ONE FIELD AND DERIVES TWO. `office.body` is the authored value; the faction it belongs to and what it does are looked up here. Where a case's office has no canonical body — the Restoration Movement's authority is *"informal"* (§8) and it has no organ in world — `office.faction` is authored directly and `body` is absent. That is a real gap in canon, carried as one. ⚠ THE `function` STRINGS ARE QUOTED, NOT PARAPHRASED. Each is world's own Function/Portfolio cell, so a reader can diff this against the source table without interpretation in between. ⚠ `Lions' Helm` CARRIES ITS OWN CANON WARNING. §4.1's cell is literally *"Naval affairs [NO MECHANICS — ED-NEW-10: future naval design question]"*. It is a member because it is a real arm of a real faction; an office seated in it has no mechanical support and canon says so. ⚠ SCALE IS NOT HERE. An office's scale is the rung it is seated at (`rung_kinds`), which the case's `scale.is` already carries. A body does not fix a rung: `Praefectures` administer regions and `Ministries` serve the realm, but the SEAT is where the person sits.

goal_object_kinds.source: v9 IN-66 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md` A-31; ED-IN-0293 (8)) -- what a goal's `object:` may be, each kind with its reader (IN-67).
goal_object_kinds.note: WHAT AN ORGANIZATION'S GOAL IS ABOUT, read by `data/goals.py` (the ONE loader of `engine/season/goals.yaml`), which refuses a row whose `object.kind` is off this list. `person` -- one named person (`case:`, a cast case id). `seat_holders` -- the live holders of the listed `seats:` ("the monarch", "the royal family"), so the goal survives a succession. `rung` -- a place (`rung:`, a rung id; checked at seeding, IN-68, because a rung exists only once built). `deed_doers` -- the doers of a declared deed class, read from the holder's OWN ledger ("threats", "heretical activity", "corruption"): ONE of the `forms:` below. `orientation` -- a pure condition ("stability", "security") that mints no Proposition (an OUGHT about nobody is not a motive, the rule in `harness/populated.py::build_realm`'s want block); its `pursuits:` join the organization's expected vector. `open: false`: a sixth kind is a new reader, a design change and not a table edit. ⚠ `forms:` IS THE `deed_doers` KIND'S OWN CLOSED SET, kept on this row because it is that kind's referent grammar and nothing else reads it. `against` -- the doers of deeds whose patient is in a named goal's referents (`against: <goal id>`). `engaging` -- the doers of a deed whose kind engages a named affiliation (`engaging: <affiliation>`). `kinds` -- the doers of the listed deed kinds (`kinds: [<deed kind>, ...]`). A `deed_doers` object names EXACTLY ONE form.

goal_derivations.source: v9 IN-66 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md` A-31, A-32; ED-IN-0293 (8)) -- how a goal at one organizational level derives from a goal at the level above.
goal_derivations.note: THE TWO WAYS A GOAL'S `derives: {from: <goal id>, kind: ...}` MAY RELATE IT TO ITS PARENT, read by `data/goals.py`, which refuses a kind off this list. `establishes` -- the child goal REPLACES the parent for the child organization's members (an office's mandate is the faction's goal made specific). `influences` -- they commit to both. requires_operands.source: `W-A`. The names a `requires_typed` cell may bind, closed.
requires_operands.note: ⚠ THE OPERAND VOCABULARY IS CLOSED, AND THAT CLOSURE IS WHAT STOPS THE GRAMMAR BECOMING A SECOND RESOLVER. A cell naming an operand outside this roster REFUSES AT LOAD. Coining one is filling `H-94` by keyword argument, which only the position `H-94` reserves it to may do. (`comply`, `evade / defy` and `construe` need no new name: the act's `subject` IS the held writ, a `Record` of kind `dispensation` -- `verb_table.yaml`'s `comply` row.) ⚠ `return_kind` AND `return_amount` (v9 IN-33, H-58) ARE `exchange`'S OTHER SIDE: `return_kind` -- the matter kind the actor RECEIVES IN RETURN -- and `return_amount` -- how many units of it. In an exchange the actor gives `amount` of `kind` from `from` to `to`, and `to` gives `return_amount` of `return_kind` back. `kind`/`amount` keep their one meaning (what moves from `from`), so no name carries two. The closure still binds: the roster is closed over its `values`, and a cell naming any other operand refuses at load (`data/requires.py::_build_clause`). Derived person-side in `decision/options.py::_derive_operand`. ⚠ WHERE AN OPERAND COMES FROM IS NOT THIS ROSTER'S QUESTION. Today it is `Act.payload`, which carries only `subject` for a computed act, so most cells bind incompletely and evaluate to UNKNOWN -- which the fold reports as a refusal, exactly as the untyped predicates did.

read_to_addressee.note: THE RECORD KINDS WHOSE MAKING IS PUT TO THE ADDRESSEE'S FACE -- a map from a `record_kinds` member to the verbs whose mint of that kind is put to its addressee. WITNESS deposits a document's content (`content:<kind>`) to its new holder; for a kind listed here it deposits it too to a witness the document is addressed to (`loop/witness.py::addressee_reads`, the addressee test `person_q.addressed_to`'s), so he reads what was put to him while the Record stays in its maker's hand (ED-IN-0292 (1), RULED NO on a mint into the addressee's, stands). `challenge`: its cell asks the challenged present (`with`), so a challenge is issued to him in person; without this deposit `accept` could not tell it from any other document. Refused at import (`data/rosters.py:: check_record_verb_rosters`, `data/verbs.py::_check_record_verb_minting`) for a key that is no record kind, a key whose content keys hold no addressee key, a verb that is no `verb_table.yaml` row or whose effect does not mint that kind, and a kind also in `proclaimed`. record_sourced_operands.source: #453 (`proposals/2026-10-03-verb-coverage-and-gap-fill.md`) §10.1, *the shared enabler*, plan position IN-10 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md`); it replaces plan position `15c`'s flat `writ_sourced_operands` (`to, kind, amount`), whose source was r2 `02_THE_WRIT_AND_THE_WORD.md` §A.13.
record_sourced_operands.note: PER RECORD KIND, WHICH OF THE CLOSED OPERANDS (`requires_operands`) A RECORD OF THAT KIND ANSWERS, AND FROM WHICH OF ITS OWN CONTENT KEYS -- `operand: content key`. `data/requires.py` refuses at import a kind that is not a `record_kinds` member, an empty entry, an operand that is not in the closed roster, a content key that is not one of THAT KIND's keys (`record_kinds.values`), and `from` on any kind. ⚠ `from` IS ON NO KIND, r2's own ruling: a document naming *where the actor stands* would let a Duke's writ reach into a larder the executor is not standing in. `at` is no operand (r2: *"I do not coin a ninth operand"*), so no kind maps it. ⚠ `kind` AND `amount` LEFT WITH THE FLAT LIST: no live kind carries either key, so they declined every time and dropping them moves nothing; a later kind that carries them (the deferred `debt`) adds them here. ⚠ TWO READERS, `decision/options.py`, ONE MAP. (1) A QUESTION ABOUT A DOCUMENT (`q.about` names a `content:<kind>` claim in the asker's own ledger, `_from_content_claim`): the document answers every name it maps BUT `subject`, which stays the question's referent -- the act is about the document itself (`give` it, answer it). `15c`'s channel; it moves nothing. (2) A HELD RECORD (`held_record_claims`: the asker's own live `hold` on a Record whose content claim he holds): the document answers every name it maps, `subject` included -- the act is about what the document SAYS, so a held dispensation's `terms` answers `subject` (`_derive_operand`'s `held=`). `operand_bags` forms one bag per held Record whose `terms` is the referent the Candidate is formed on, on a row whose second side a known person fills (`known_person_operands`): the document's addressee is then a second side beside the persons the holder knows. No faction actor, no new form, no ninth operand, no coined name. ⚠ `faction_sheet` IS THE SHEET CONSUMER (v9 IN-45 `forge`, H-169 limit 5: *"no operand, cell or score reads `members`/`holdings`/`seats` off a `content:faction_sheet` claim"*), on H-169's own design order -- *"a sheet-sourced operand, `15c`'s route"* -- and so a ROW HERE, not a branch. A sheet answers `to` with the `head` it names: on a question about a sheet its holder holds, a petition (`to` bound without `subject`, reader (1)) is ADDRESSED TO WHOEVER THE SHEET SAYS HEADS THE FACTION -- the decision H-169's `unblocks:` names (*"a petition's addressee"*). A stale or forged sheet addresses it wrongly, and nothing tells the petitioner. `head` and not `members`/`seats`: it is the sheet's one single-person key, so it answers without `_content_answer`'s singleton collapse; `seats` are offices and a petition's addressee is a Person (`verb_table.yaml`'s `petition` row). `subject: proposition` keeps reader (2) on its own rule -- a held sheet adds a fanned bag only on an act about the faction it describes -- where a sheet mapping no `subject` would pass that check vacuously on every referent. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop this row and the sheet is read by nothing again.] `head` is `None` on every true sheet this tree builds today (`queries/faction_q.py:: head`: no `commit` carries a degree), so a true sheet answers nothing and falls through to the referent exactly as before; a forged one names its forger (`loop/effects_information.py:: _eff_forge`).

warrant_sourced.source: #453 (`proposals/2026-10-03-verb-coverage-and-gap-fill.md`) §9.1, the `seize` row: *"the warrant is the Candidate's source (a held dispensation whose `terms` names the Record)"*, and the Warrant row of its documents table (*"`dispensation` whose `terms` is a Person or a Record"*); plan position IN-12 step 6 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md`).
warrant_sourced.note: WHICH VERBS TAKE THEIR `subject` FROM A HELD WARRANT, AND WHICH RECORD KIND IS THE WARRANT -- `verb: record kind`. ONE LOADER, `data/verbs.py::WARRANT_SOURCED`, read once beside the verb table and refused at import when a line names a verb the table lacks or a kind `record_sourced_operands` gives no `subject` key; both readers below import it from there. A verb named here is formed person-side ONLY on a `subject` that a held Record of that kind names (`decision/options.py::opening_set`: `held_record_claims`, answered through `record_sourced_operands`' `subject` key, the one map of what a Record's content says), and the effect's RECORD half licenses the act on the same reading read WORLD-side (`loop/effects_information.py::_held_warrant_names`, called by `_eff_seize`). ⚠ WHY A ROSTER AND NOT A FAN: IN-10's held-Record fan (`operand_bags`) is bound to a known-person operand (`known_person_operands`), and `seize` names no second party (#453 K-04), so the fan never reaches it; this is the one place that says a verb's referent comes from a warrant instead of from the question. Without the line a `remit:issue` seat forms `seize` on every Record any question names and the fold refuses it each time -- `requisition`'s scene tax (H-163) for a licence nobody holds. A warrant naming a PERSON (`arrest`, step 5) adds its own line here; a Person `subject` is declined by `seize`'s effect (since v9 IN-13 the row's `existence` conjunct is gone: its object widened to a Rung, and the effect, `_eff_seize`, declines anything that is neither a held Record nor an occupied settlement). The Rung half forms person-side wherever a held dispensation's `terms` names the rung (`test_season_shape.py` plants one on a hearth); at the effect it licenses on OCCUPATION, not on the warrant, so the formation and execution licences differ for the Rung half; no computed source of such a warrant has been measured. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop this roster, its loader (`data/verbs.py::WARRANT_SOURCED`) and its readers (`decision/options.py::opening_set` and `loop/effects_information.py::_held_warrant_names`), and `seize` forms on any referent, refused in the fold.] v9 IN-12 step 5 ADDS `arrest`, the line this note foresaw (*"a warrant naming a PERSON"*): it forms person-side only on a person a held dispensation's `terms` names, and its effect (`_eff_arrest`) reads the same held warrant world-side (`world_q.warrants_for`, `seize`'s reading shared) and opens the `detain` on the seat that ISSUED it. H-94's "a Person (warrant) term has no route" is answered for `arrest` by this line.

terms_sourced.source: #453 (`proposals/2026-10-03-verb-coverage-and-gap-fill.md`) §10.1, *"What it unblocks: ... `commit` (a covenant dispensation's `terms` answers `subject`)"*, and §10.4 step 7's falsifier, *"the addressee's `commit` to the covenant's Proposition, formed from the held dispensation after a `give`"*; plan position IN-12 step 7 (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md`), the route `hole_register.yaml` H-94 records as missing (*"Proposition terms (a covenant, `commit`) have no route"*).
terms_sourced.note: WHICH VERBS MAY ALSO FORM ON WHAT A HELD DOCUMENT SAYS -- `verb: [record kinds]`. A verb named here forms, BESIDE its own referents, on the `terms` of each Record of a named kind that the question carries as a held writ (`queries/world_q.py::writs_held`: a Record on the person's own live `hold` whose addressee list names him, stamped `Record`-classed onto the question he answers), read off the person's OWN content claim on it (`decision/options.py:: held_record_claims`, answered through `record_sourced_operands`' `subject` key -- the one map of what a Record is about). The act is about what the document SAYS, as IN-10's held-Record channel reads it (`_derive_operand`'s `held=`); the writ is the referent, so §F1 clause 3 is not widened past the question -- a person holding no such writ, or answering a question that does not carry it, forms exactly what he formed before. ⚠ WHY NOT IN-10's FAN: `operand_bags` fans held Records only on a row binding a known-person operand, and only where a Record's `terms` IS already the referent; `commit` binds `subject` alone, and nobody's question is ABOUT a Proposition he has only been handed, so the fan never reaches it. ⚠ WHY NOT A `referent_class: Proposition` (the v9 reasoning; SUPERSEDED at v10 REM-23, B10-05, which gave `commit` that class under M19 and took the loss, `verb_table.yaml`'s `commit` note): a row declaring a class forms ONLY on that class (`Question.referents_for`), so `commit` would lose the plain referents IN-11's utterer route forms on. ONE LOADER, `data/verbs.py::TERMS_SOURCED`, refused at import when a line names a verb the table lacks, or a kind that is no record term's occasion (`RECORD_REFERENT_KINDS`, which `writs_held` stamps, or `HOLDING_RECORD_KINDS`, a held document a holding row asks for; v10 IN-12 step 5a) or whose `subject` no held Record answers -- either would form for nobody. Whether the act then passes is the fold's (`commit`'s own cell: the terms exist and are a Proposition; a writ whose terms name a person is refused there, `commitment.refused`). [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop this roster, its loader and its reader in `opening_set`, and `commit` forms on its question's referents only -- a covenant's addressee then never accepts it.]

rig_levels.source: B24p.24 (V2 p2 §H): *`rig` is the arranger's one choice (0, 0.5, 1)*; V2 p4 §F 19: each level is best somewhere on `2 x stake x P(carried) - rig_price x tilt^2`.
rig_levels.note: HOW HARD THE ARRANGER RIGS THE FORUM -- the closed set of `rig`, a PAYLOAD KEY on `open_case` and `convene` (`rosters.yaml: choice_sourced`'s shape: no cell binds it, the closed operand vocabulary stays closed). `0` is no rig and the act that carries none. Read by `data/rosters.py::RIG_LEVELS`: `loop/effects_information.py::_eff_open_case` refuses a level outside it, `decision/options.py::rig_offer` reads the levels above 0 as the ones it may offer, and `seam/wrappers/sigma.py::proceeding_input` reads the rig as the number it multiplies the tilt by. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: a one-member roster `[0]` offers no rig and refuses any.]

rigged_verbs.source: B24p.24 (V2 p4 §H item 13): *the arrangement reaches the builder as operands of `open_case` and `convene`*.
rigged_verbs.note: THE VERBS THAT CARRY A `rig` (`rig_levels`): the act that puts a matter before a room (`open_case`) and the one that convenes the sitting (`convene`). Read by `decision/options.py::opening_set`, which offers a rig on these alone and only where the actor's power exceeds the other party's (the host's reading of the room, `View.odds.arranged`), and by the two effects, which write it. Refused at import for a verb the table lacks (`data/verbs.py::RIGGED_VERBS`).

choice_sourced.source: v11 CP-T04-02 (B10-12): `decision/options.py::operand_bags` *"ranges `role` and `retreat_at` over their closed sets, or no NPC marshals"*, after `confer`'s `to` (a known person) and `train`'s vocation (`vocation_sourced`).
choice_sourced.note: WHICH VERBS CARRY A CHOICE, AND OVER WHICH PAYLOAD KEYS -- `verb: [key, ...]`. A verb named here forms ONE bag per COMBINATION of its keys' closed sets (`data/verbs.py::CHOICE_RANGES`: `role` is `order_roles`, `retreat_at` is `order_retreat_at`), each value riding on the act's payload under its own name. ⚠ THE KEYS ARE NOT `requires_operands` MEMBERS and a cell never binds them: the closed operand vocabulary stays closed (`challenge`'s `stakes` is the precedent for a payload key the effect reads). ⚠ THE CHOOSER IS CONTENT-BLIND UNTIL A CELL IS AUTHORED: Candidates score on `(verb, subject)` (`decision/choose.py`), so the fan is a draw among equally scored orders, not a judgement of which role suits the field. CONTENT ENTERS AT ONE PLACE, `tables.alignment`'s optional `choices:` block (B10.56, shipped absent): a cell there on a key this table names scores that value in `score_terms`' `pursuit`, through the person's own axis weights. ⚠ THE FAN IS A COST, MEASURED AT ITS LANDING (`hole_register.yaml` `H-361`): 15 roles x 3 `retreat_at` values = 45 bags per settlement a marshal forms on. ONE LOADER, `data/verbs.py::CHOICE_SOURCED`, refused at import for a verb the table lacks, a key without a range, or a key whose carrier the verb's row does not write (`role`, `retreat_at`: `Record.exists`; `posture`: `Site.condition`). ⚠ A KEY WHOSE RANGE HAS ONE MEMBER IS NOT FANNED (`decision/options.py::_fanned_choices`): CP-T04-06's `march` ranges `posture` over `march_postures`, shipped `[storm]`, so no `march` Candidate carries a `posture` and the shipped season does not move. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete the row, and `marshal` forms one Candidate with no order.] v12 B11.10 (`08_FI_02` edits 7-8): `tell` AND `lie` CARRY TWO CHOICES, `said` AND `in_confidence`, on `marshal`'s precedent. `said` is WHAT is told: one Candidate per claim among the top `Fixtures.said_choices` the teller's slant ranks for the subject (`queries/person_q.py::said_set`, `said_of` or `lie_said_of` over the teller's own ledger), and a claim is scored by `deed_valence` under the teller's own projected pursuits inside the `pursuit` term (`decision/choose.py::score_terms`) -- no new term. Who hears is unchanged (presence). ⚠ A TELLING WRITES NOTHING, so the carrier a key is checked against is the kind its deposit is: the row must emit `news.told` (`data/verbs.py::CHOICE_CARRIER`). shortfall_sourced_operands.source: plan position `19d` (DEMAND · DELIVERY), `workplans/2026-09-28-the-plan-one-order-mc-v18-retired.md` §3.2 row 11, and the driver-retirement plan's G3: *"wiring the existing `transfer` verb's operands from a shortfall claim"*.
shortfall_sourced_operands.note: ⚠ `record_sourced_operands`' CLAIM-SOURCED SHAPE, ONE ROW DOWN, FOR A SECOND KIND OF CLAIM: the operand names a SHORTFALL CLAIM may answer, before `decision/options.py::_derive_operand` falls through to the referent or the fixture. A subset of `requires_operands`, refused at import otherwise (`data/requires.py`). The claim is `(rung, "<predicate>:<kind>", units)`: MATTER records it on the `stores.changed` Event of a larder the draw ran dry with a mouth unfed, as `demanded - delivered` over the rung's subtree (`queries/world_q.py`), and WITNESS deposits it into those who witness that write. ⚠ TWO NAMES, NOT THREE, AND `to` IS LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. For a `claim_landed` question the referent IS the claim's subject (`questions_for` builds `(c.subject,)`), so `to` already binds the drained rung through the referent rule. A claim branch for it would always return the same value as the fallback beneath it, and a branch that can never change an outcome is `ID-13`. A document maps `to` because a writ's addressee is NOT its subject (the Record). `from` stays the actor's own rung for r2 §A.13's reason: a claim about somewhere else must not reach into a larder the actor is not standing in. ⚠ THE PREDICATE STEM IS DATA, AND IT MAY NOT BE A WORD THE `requires` GRAMMAR READS: a claim whose stem `LedgerReader` answered would become a belief about a store LEVEL. It may not be the content stem either. `data/requires.py` refuses both collisions at import.

known_person_operands.source: telling workplan `T4` (`workplans/2026-10-01-telling-workplan.md` §3 and §4, `ED-IN-0282`): *"`known_persons`: ids from truthy `exists:Person` claims, `Seen.who`, told `chain[-1]`; minus self and referent"*, and one Candidate per known person.
known_person_operands.note: ⚠ THE SIBLINGS' SHAPE FOR A THIRD KIND OF ANSWER: the operand names a person answers with SOMEBODY THEY KNOW rather than with the question's referent. A subset of `requires_operands`, refused at import otherwise (`data/requires.py`). `decision/options.py::operand_bags` forms one operand bag per known person, and only for a row whose typed cell binds `subject` SEPARATELY from the name -- `tell`, whose topic is `subject` and whose hearer is `to`, since plan position `14` `give`, whose Record is `subject` and whose receiver is `to`, and since plan position IN-10 (#453 §10.1) `issue`, whose `terms` is `subject` and whose executor is `to`, so a writ is no longer addressed to what it is about. A row binding `to` without `subject` (`petition`) keeps the referent rule: what it is addressed to IS what it is about there, `H-94`'s single referent. Since IN-10 a held Record's addressee is a second side too (`record_sourced_operands`, reader (2)). ⚠ `claim` IS WHERE A PERSON BECOMES KNOWN, and `queries/person_q.py::known_persons` reads it: `predicate` -- a truthy existence reading of a person (deposited by the `existence` form's fold); `seen_term` -- the `seen` claim's term naming who was seen doing something. The third source, the teller of a told claim (`Claim.chain[-1]`), is structural and needs no row here. Nothing else makes a person known: no roster of acquaintances, no world read.

intent_claim.source: v9 IN-16, telling `T7` (G9, declared intent; `workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part4.md`, `ED-IN-0282`): *"a teller may tell a hearer an act they have CHOSEN-AND-NOT-YET-DONE, as a position and a claim kind"*.
intent_claim.note: THE CLAIM KIND A DECLARED INTENT IS. `decision/choose.py::declare_intents` mints it at CHOOSE, through `queries/person_q.py::intent_said`, onto a telling's `said`, so the told deposit lands it in each hearer's ledger as `(teller, <stem>:<verb>, ((name, id), ...))`: `claim.predicate` is the STEM, the intended act's verb its argument, and `values` are the operand names of the intended act whose ids the value carries, in this order. `queries/world_q.py::named` reads those ids back (through `person_q.intent_named`), so a hearer whose reach covers a person or place the intent names is raised a `claim_landed` question about the teller. ⚠ NOT A CELL: the stem is refused at import if it is a `requires` grammar stem (it would read as a world fact and `record` would pair it), the `seen` predicate, the `content:` predicate or an emitted event kind (`person_q._check_intent_claim`). Whether the act was later done is not read by anything (`hole_register.yaml` `H-191`).

absence_claim.source: B11.83 (`U5c_VERBS_residue` §3 steps 1 and 3; SOCIAL1 D2, decision register D-46: a man who seeks someone who is not there is refused, learns nothing and forms the same act again).
absence_claim.note: THE CLAIM A REFUSAL ON THE `with` CONJUNCT TEACHES ITS ACTOR: `(<the person sought>, absent, <the rung the refused act stood at>)`, firsthand, deposited by `loop/witness.py::witness` to the ACTOR ALONE (whatever `observation_deposit_mode`: the claim is his reading, not an Event's public payload) when the read that decided the refusal is a `with` read the world answered False. A `with` read is observed and never deposited (`WORLD_ONLY_STEMS`: the person side cannot answer it), so this is the one claim the refusal leaves of it; a read the world could not answer (UNKNOWN: no place) teaches nothing. The value is the place, so a reader can ask whether the absence was HERE. A bare stem, held by the checks at the predicate's reader: not a `requires` grammar stem, not the `seen` or `content:` predicate, not an emitted event kind (`loop/witness.py`). No roster of claim predicates existed for it to join: the deposits' predicates are declared one roster each (`observation_terms.deposit`, `record_content`, `intent_claim`), and so is this one. `queries/person_q.py::present_persons` reads it back (B11.84): a person the holder's newest `absent` claim names is left out until a newer firsthand sighting.

stance_polarities.source: v9 IN-18 `G2` (telling workplan §5, `ED-IN-0282`): *"polarity in §F2 term 2"* -- the score's regard term read by the ROLE the regarded party plays in the act, with `declared` against `legacy` as the falsifier's two arms.
stance_polarities.note: THE ARMS OF `Fixtures.stance_polarity` (`H-194`), read by `decision/choose.py::stance_term` (its `_stance_arm`), score term 2. `legacy` is the pre-G2 term, `+ stance_toward(p, c.subject)` for every row -- the CONTROL (shipped until CR-16): an act against a disliked opponent then scores LOWER, the sign §F2's term never distinguished. `declared` reads `regard(p, c.subject)` (G1's, so its judged and told halves enter at their own gains) and NEGATES it where the subject is the act's OPPONENT (`decision/options.py::subject_is_opponent`: the row contests and its second side is its subject, `VerbRow.opponent_operand()`), so fighting the disliked scores higher. A Rung subject reads 0 at G1's control; at live gains it reads the deed claims held about it (`transfer.made` on a changed rung, under `claim_subject_rule: both`). Its regarded party under the ROLE reading would be its HOLDER, and no ledger holds a `held_by` claim (M0g, `H-195`). `regard` is the midpoint: G1's regard with `+` on every row, so the sweep separates what regard adds from what the sign adds. `beneficiary` (B10.69, `17_CENSUS_C1A_02` W4) is `declared` with the regard read toward the person the act is done FOR (`choose.beneficiary_of`) in place of its subject; a row with no such person reads the subject. said_slants.note: THE ARMS OF `Fixtures.said_slant` (`H-196`), read by `queries/person_q.py::said_of`. `newest` is the pre-G3 pick -- the newest non-`seen` claim about the subject, then the most confident -- the CONTROL, shipped. `valence` first narrows the teller's claims about the subject to those THEY judge most strongly (the largest `|deed_valence|` by their own pursuits) and picks among those by the same comparator; with no valenced claim it is `newest` exactly. `unshared` (v12 B11.09, `08_FI_02` edit 2) never passes on the transport's own kinds -- the teller's claims whose predicate a `tell` or a `lie` row emits (on success or on refusal) are dropped from the pool -- and so retells what the room did not see for itself. `unshared_first` is `unshared` that then picks, by the same comparator, within the first non-empty tier of its `prefers:`, and a `seen` claim remains the last resort as at every arm. THE TWO KEYS ARE DATA, PER ARM, under `arms:` (read by `queries/person_q.py::_load_slant_arms`, refused at import): `excludes_kinds_of` names VERBS of `verb_table.yaml` (a name the table lacks refuses, as `lie_verbs` does; the excluded predicates are those rows' `emits` and `emits_on_refusal`, derived, never spelt) and `prefers` is an ordered list of tiers, each one `person_q.py::_SLANT_TIERS` reads (told: a claim with a chain; inferred: `source == "inferred"`; deed: `is_deed`; quantity: a claim on a stem of `data/verbs.py: QUANTITY_STEMS`, so an existence reading is not one; other: anything else).

beneficiary_kinds.source: `CAT-2`, closed at step 5 (`proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-behaviour/RULINGS.yaml`). The carriers a verb's `beneficiary:` column may name -- *"a carrier a Candidate ALREADY holds (the actor, `subject`, or a named operand), NOT a fifth field on `Candidate`."*
beneficiary_kinds.note: ⚠ THIS IS A SUBSET OF `requires_operands` PLUS TWO, AND IT IS NOT THAT ROSTER. The operand vocabulary says what a PRECONDITION may bind; this says who an act is taken FOR THE GOOD OF. `from`, `site`, `kind`, `amount` and `floor` are absent because none of them names a person, and a beneficiary that is not a person is not a beneficiary -- it is the `none` member. ⚠ `actor` IS A MEMBER HERE AND IS NEVER CARRIED IN `operands` (`operands_for` skips it: *"`actor` is structural on both sides and is never carried"*). That asymmetry is the point. The actor is the one carrier every Candidate holds unconditionally, so a verb declaring `beneficiary: actor` resolves for every candidate ever formed, where `to` resolves only where the cell binds it. ⚠ `none` IS A DECLARATION, NOT A BLANK, and the loader requires the column on every row. An act whose good accrues to a Record, an Office, a Site or a Rung has no person-beneficiary the Candidate carries, and saying so in the data is what distinguishes it from a row nobody graded. Absence would read as `false` for every verb -- the UNKNOWN/False collapse `operands_for` refuses one level down. ⚠ WHAT THIS ROSTER DOES NOT DECIDE: the WEIGHT. `synthesis.md` §1.3 spells the term `orient · benefits_me(c)`. The missing piece is the STATE: `Person` has no `orient` field and `references/npc_registry.yaml` authors no such value (its 28 per-row values were deleted at B04.12, unread, `ED-IN-0260`). The term is `6f`'s. This roster and its column deliver `beneficiary_of(p, c)`, which no game code reads (tests only).

requires_forms.source: `architecture/meta/04_CODE_ARCHITECTURE.md` §F.24a -- SEVEN forms, read off the 32 live `requires` cells rather than designed. `F.24` had said *"assumed: a small typed predicate grammar"* and supplied none.
requires_forms.note: ⚠ CLOSED AT SEVEN. A cell naming a form outside this roster REFUSES AT LOAD, because an eighth form is a new thing a precondition can ask and that is a design change, not a table edit -- the same polarity `eligibility_kinds` already carries against a fifth kind. ⚠ TWO OF THE SEVEN HAVE NO TYPED CELL TODAY AND THAT IS NOT AN OMISSION. `cardinality`'s and `basis`'s only live cells are `confer` and `revoke`, whose eligibility is `remit:` and not `own`; `W-A` types the `own`-eligible rows, so those two keep their `REQUIRES_PREDICATES` entry and this roster records that the grammar has room for them. ⚠ `existence` IS READ WIDER THAN §F.24a's ONE-LINE GLOSS, DELIBERATELY. The gloss says *"existence over an edge kind"* and names `repudiate` (a live `commit`) and `revoke` (a live `hold`). But §F.24a also claims the seven forms close 30 of 32 cells, and `carry` (*a Petition exists*), `commit` (*the Proposition exists*) and `dispatch` (*the named person exists*) fit no other form -- so the closure claim is only true if `existence` covers an OBJECT of a named class as well as an EDGE of a named kind. It is read that way here, and the widening is stated rather than left for a reader to infer from a passing test. DORMANT BRANCH (ID-13 shape): v9 IN-11 cut `repudiate`, and no `requires_typed` cell in `verb_table.yaml` names a tenure kind now (the `existence` cells name Person, Proposition, petition, Record, works, Rung, Site and DocketItem), so `queries/world_q.py`'s `exists:<edge kind>` branch is reached by no cell; it stays, unchanged. ⚠ CONJUNCTION IS NOT AN EIGHTH FORM. `restore` (*the site exists AND the actor is present at it*), `confer` and `revoke` all carry an `and` IN THE PROSE, so a cell may be written as `all: [<form>, <form>]`. §F.24a enumerated the ATOMS; the `and` was already in the cells it read. Disjunction is deliberately absent: `confer`'s `or` is the only one, `confer` is not `own`-eligible, and adding a combinator no cell uses is the dead carrier `ID-13` refuses. `needs:` is the closed set of operands a cell OF THAT FORM may reference -- checked at load against `requires_operands`, so a form cannot quietly reach an operand its shape has no use for.

conferral_bases.source: JORDAN, ED-IN-0256 ruling (2), 2026-09-18, VERBATIM: *"appointed, elected, annex"* -- HOW A SEAT IS FILLED. Plan position `13d-i`.
conferral_bases.note: ⚠ THE VALUES ARE THE RULING'S, THE SHAPE IS r2's (`proposals/2026-09-17-governance-and-holdings-r2/03_SEATS_AND_CONTENT.md` §A.4). r2 spelled this roster `[confer, determine, succeed]`, keyed on the ACT that opens the hold; that list predates ED-IN-0256 and is superseded by it. The two vocabularies do not correspond by name, so no r2 seat's value carries over -- a seat's basis is authored against THIS list. `open: false`: a fourth way to fill a seat is a design change, not a table edit. READ BY: `Office.__post_init__`, which refuses a declared basis off this list (the `remit_acts` refusal's shape, so a typo is loud rather than a seat nobody can ever fill), and `state/gate.py::has_conferral_basis` (moved from `loop/predicates.py` by G3, since the gate asks it and may not import the loop; `predicates.py` re-imports the name), the ONE basis test `_req_confer` and `_req_establish` share, and `state/gate.py::REVOCATION_DISPOSAL` (v9 IN-31: what a revocation costs, by this basis). ⚠ NOTHING DISCRIMINATES BETWEEN THE THREE YET: `confer` admits a seat declaring any of them. Which act fills an `elected` or an `annex` seat is not ruled, and no election or annexation verb exists; narrowing `confer` to `appointed` would leave the other two seats fillable by nothing. v10 IN-61 (RS-27, B10-09) ADDS A FOURTH, `inheritance`: Jordan 2026-10-14, *"designated heir is not a verb but a status or title. the heir still has to claim their throne"*. A seat declaring it is filled by the claim of the holder of its `successions` title (below), never by `confer`. WHICH GATE BASIS MAY OPEN A HOLD ON A SEAT OF EACH CONFERRAL BASIS is `state/gate.py::FILLED_BY` (the first narrowing: `inheritance` to the claim basis alone; the other three keep `conferral`), and what a revocation of one costs is `REVOCATION_DISPOSAL["inheritance"]` (nothing); both are refused at import unless total over this list. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the member, the two mappings' keys, `successions` and `off_king`'s basis (back to `null`).]

successions.source: v10 IN-61 (RS-27, B10-09; `workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v10_part4.md` IN-61, part (1)): Jordan 2026-10-14, *"designated heir is not a verb but a status or title. the heir still has to claim their throne"*. RS-29 ratified the title carrier (2026-10-14).
successions.note: WHICH TITLES A SEAT OF CONFERRAL BASIS `inheritance` PASSES TO -- a mapping, `{seat: [title, ...]}`, every member an `offices.yaml` row id (realm seat ids equal their row ids since CP-T02-02); a bare string reads as a one-title list. THE TITLES WHOSE HOLDERS MAY CLAIM THE SEAT; A LIST IS ELIGIBILITY, NEVER AN ORDER (HAPPENINGS-B, A-19): who takes the seat is `succeed`'s draw, and the founding order is a head start, never a right. A title is an ordinary seat, filled by `confer` (`off_heir`, `appointed`) or, for the two houses' heads, by their own basis: designation is no verb. The seat is claimed by a title's holder through `succeed` (`loop/predicates.py::_req_succeed`, `loop/effects_governance.py::_eff_succeed`, the write gate's claim basis), admitted only while the seat has no live `hold`; the claim opens EVERY vacant seat that lists a title he holds and lays down each such title that exists only to pass a seat (`conferral: appointed`, an empty remit -- `state/gate.py::passes_a_seat`), in one act: a duke who takes the throne keeps his duchy. LIMITS: the route only awards a vacant seat; the first valid claim wins; one title deep (a title laid down by a claim passes to nobody). READ BY `data/rosters.py::SUCCESSIONS`, refused at import when a key or a member is no `offices.yaml` row, a list is empty, a key's row is not `inheritance`, or an `inheritance` row has no key (a seat nobody could ever fill). `off_duke_valorsmark`'s row (B21.51, `16_PESSIMIST_FA_A` edit 1) lists `off_king`'s own titles: whoever wins the deed race for the throne takes the Crown's duchy in the same write. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: the single title (`off_king: off_heir`), the claim closing the heir's title alone; for the duchy, drop its row and its `conferral: inheritance`.]

continuation_ties.source: v10 CP-T02-06 (B10-10; M7 taken (b), `workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v11_part6.md` DECISION: *title, then oath*). The seated person's line CONTINUES or ENDS (`-02` §2 CP-T02-06, P30 heir transfer, P42 a dead line).
continuation_ties.note: WHO MAY CARRY ON A SEATED PERSON'S LINE WHEN HE DIES, AND IN WHAT ORDER THEY ARE OFFERED -- a closed ORDERED roster (the order is semantic: `ordered: true`). `heir_title`: the holders of the `successions` titles of a seat the person holds (the registry above; the list's order is the offer's only). `sworn`: a person with a live `oblige` to a seat the person holds (`state/gate.py::sworn_to`, the one walk `establishment_of` composes on). A person who is both is offered once, at the earlier tie. WHAT EACH TIE MEANS IS CODE: `queries/world_q.py::_TIE_READERS`, one reader per member; `check_continuation_ties` REFUSES AT IMPORT a member with no reader and a reader with no member, and `continuations` iterates this roster, so a `Continuation` tagged with a kind off this list is never returned. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: bind to the first living tie in this order without offering a choice (`carry_on` takes `offer[0]`), or drop `sworn`, or append `follower`.]

revocation_bases.source: JORDAN, ED-IN-0256 ruling (3), 2026-09-18, VERBATIM: *"rung above of same faction"* -- WHO MAY STRIP A SEAT. Plan position `13d-i`; closes the `is_title` branch (`H-109`).
revocation_bases.note: ⚠ TWO VALUES. `rung_above_in_holdings` (JORDAN, 2026-10-12: *"it's not ONLY based on hierarchy of rungs, but also where it is placed in holdings"*): the seat's rung is one of the revoker's HOLDINGS and the revoker sits on the rung directly above; a seat whose rung nobody holds is stripped by nobody, its holder resigns. `rung_above_same_faction`, the one value ED-IN-0256 ruled: the holder of a seat on the rung DIRECTLY ABOVE the seat's own rung, in the SAME faction -- structural, NOT a rank comparison, and applied to every seat alike. A seat with NO declared basis (`None`) is revocable by nobody, which is what r2's `none` meant; it needs no member of its own. ⚠ THIS ROSTER NAMES THE BASIS AND NOTHING ELSE -- the `fan_out_modes` split above. The rule is BEHAVIOUR and lives in `state/gate.py` (`REVOCATION_RULES`), which refuses at IMPORT if a member here has no rule there or the reverse, so the roster cannot grow a value the resolver silently treats as another.

ONE VALUE, because one was ruled: `members_by_admission`, the `Office.binds` default on every seat in the tree. A person joins by their OWN `oblige` (`own`-eligible), so admission is the joiner's act and `remit_acts` needs no sixth member -- the cost `ARCH F.17` warns of (*"a ruling, not a row"*), avoided. interposition_kinds.source: `proposals/2026-09-05-proceedings-subsystem/03_PARAMETERS.md` PART D's `interposed:` schema comment -- Fig. 24 -- and §E.2's twelve worked rows, every one of which draws its `interposed:` list from exactly this set. Plan position `18` (PROC-A).

genres.source: `03_PARAMETERS.md` §B.3 / Fig. 23 -- the genre triangle. `genre` is DERIVED from the bench's remit acts (a Query, never an authored key on a row -- §B.3: "not a field on the game"), and is a SET, not a single value (the assembly-as-magistrate bend needs both `forensic` and `deliberative` at once). This roster is the closed CODOMAIN that derivation may return into, the same relationship `rung_kinds` has to `title_domain`.
genres.note: `forensic` -- a PAST matter, did it happen: the issue ladder runs. `deliberative` -- a FUTURE matter, shall we do it: no issue ladder: the fact is not in dispute. `epideictic` -- no bench at all: amplification; the only prize is standing. ⚠ NOTHING DERIVES `genre` YET (the Query is `19_PLAN.md` PHASE 2/3 work, not this position's five parts) -- this roster is the closed set that derivation will read into, authored now because `speech_kinds`' own "which genres it is apt in" column already needs somewhere closed to point at.

ladder_rungs.source: `18_FINDINGS.md`:180 and §5 item 5 (Fig. 27) -- the forensic CHARGE LADDER a party descends under `interrogation`'s `order: scripted` / `registers: [restricted]`, verbatim: "deny, cite something incompatible, impugn the motive, concede the fact, concede the harm, hand the error back." Plan position `18` (PROC-A).
ladder_rungs.note: THE CHARGE LADDER (Fig. 27): the positions a party takes under a charge. It is not the issue ladder (`issue_rungs`: the questions a court tries, from procedure to justification); the two share no member. ⚠ SIX RUNGS, ORDERED HIGH-TO-LOW (deny is the strongest position; handing the error back concedes everything). `speech_kinds` reuses these SAME SIX AS ITS ONLY SIX MEMBERS (below, itself flagged partial against the ten `19_PLAN.md` step 7 promises) rather than minting a second vocabulary for what is, on this corpus's own reading, one ladder read two ways -- a RUNG one descends and a KIND OF SPEECH one performs to descend it are the same six acts. `impugn_motive` is `18_FINDINGS.md`'s *"Partial by construction"* figure (Fig. 24's fixed native band, §5 item 5) -- reachable-bands data on `speech_kinds`' own row, not a second roster.

ground_reads.source: V2 p2 §A.2 -- what a ground's fit reads: a channel of the bearing reading, or the item's `credit` for `evidence`.
ground_reads.note: THE CLOSED SET `grounds`' `reads` cell is a member of. `item` -- the proof the speaker shows, through its `credit`; `want` -- what the listener wants; `hold` -- what he holds; `bond` -- whom he stands with. A ground naming any other reading is refused at import.

proceeding_effects.source: V2 p2 §B -- a move is read by its `effect`, never by its id.
proceeding_effects.note: THE CLOSED SET `proceeding_moves`' `effect` cell is a member of. `track` -- the speech moves each listener's own track; `strike` -- it presses the man who made the point on the table; `yield` -- the speaker concedes the issue; `none` -- he rests. B24.03 adds the hearing's five (HEAR_B's six moves): `exhibit` -- a party enters an item of his side on the board; `answer` -- he contradicts a standing item, or a finding that its origin is forged; `impugn` -- he attacks the origin of an opposing item; `rule` -- the bench closes the sitting now; `adjourn` -- the bench holds the stage to the next sitting. No effect names a winner or a side: the close is each adjudicator's own draw (V2 p2 §D), and the hearing's closing draw is the determiner's.

grounds.source: V2 p2 §C.2 (`content[g]`, Reason's share of a speech's dice by ground, R11) and §A.2 (`reads`); V2 p4 §F 10 (`consequence` is pathos, `evidence` alone logos).
grounds.note: WHAT AN ARGUMENT APPEALS TO: the proof shown, what the listener wants, what he holds, or whom he stands with, in that order. `reason` is Reason's share of a speech's dice on that ground before the venue's lean, a whole number of tenths in [0, 1]; `reads` names what the ground's fit reads (`ground_reads`). B24p.01 left every `reason` at the control, 1.0 (the dice Reason alone); B24p.23 wrote the shipped column of V2's model (`sc2/host.py::GROUNDS`: evidence 0.8, consequence 0.7, authority 0.4, solidarity 0.2). [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: every `reason` below is V2's shipped value -- basis: `sc2/host.py::GROUNDS` as the running model reads it, cited not copied; revert: 1.0 on every ground, the control.] B24.35 (WGM edits 2-3): `backed_by` (optional) is what has to hold for the ground to BACK an act with a hearer who is moved by it -- a `when` key of `capability_when_keys` (not `rank_at_least`) and its argument. The hearer's own `Person.traits` say which grounds move him (`descriptors.TRAITS[*].seated_by` is a ground id); one who holds none is moved by every ground as before, and one who holds some is moved by those grounds whose `backed_by` holds for this act and by none other (`seam/wrappers/sigma.py::_backed`, `Present.backed`). A ground with no `backed_by` is backed wherever it is a susceptibility. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct: each `backed_by` below is the entry's own, `record` for the cited kind and a regard floor of 3 -- basis: WGM edit 3's four rows' `when`; revert: delete the cell and the ground backs wherever it is a susceptibility.]

proceeding_moves.source: V2 p2 §B (a move is read by its `effect`), §A.1 (`rank`, his rank in the proceeding's skill); V2 p4 §F 1 (the ploy is carried by `insincerity` on `argue` and `press`; `deceive` and `divert` are not built).
proceeding_moves.note: THE MOVES A SPEAKER MAY MAKE, ONE ROW EACH, so that no move id is ever compared in code: the module reads `effect` and `draw`. `draw: true` moves roll the speaker's dice; `capability` is the skill whose rank joins them and is refused on a `draw: false` row. Whom a move is resisted by is not a cell: Will is the resisting attribute of every listener (A-137, V2 p4 §F 26). B24.03 added the hearing's `present`, `answer`, `impugn` and the bench's `rule`, `adjourn` to THIS roster, never a second one; `descends: true` (optional, a bool) says a yield also descends one rung of a type that has an issue ladder (`concede`'s). The sitting reads `descends` and the hearing's five rows; a rite lists the moves it admits, and the `default` and `inquisition` rites name them. `capability` is a skill id, or a map from EACH `issue_rungs` member to one: the rung argued is what is in issue (D-U1-03), so `argue` and `answer` draw on `law` on a rung of procedure or definition and on `argue` on one of fact or justification. A drawing move carries one; a draw-free move none; `rhetoric` is not a skill (the audience reaches the roll as `reception`). A map's rungs are read at the first rung of a rite's `issues` only (`sigma.py`, `rite.issues[0]`); `sigma._rank_key` reads the single-id rows. [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: `impugn` and `press` draw on `argue` on every rung -- basis: an attack on a source is made to the room, not to the rung (HCAP "What draws on what"); revert: a map for the row.]

proceeding_faults.source: HEAR_B (`05_SC_playable_hearing_B.md`) "Faults": a fault is a condition on the typed board, and none names a winner.
proceeding_faults.note: THE FAULTS A SITTING RECORDS, in the order HEAR_B states them; a rite lists those that apply. Each is a condition on the board and a cost on the closing draw, never a verdict: no row names a winner or a side, and the bench may still find for the party at fault. `self_contradiction` -- two standing items of one side disagree: the lighter is struck, one level against that side. `silence` -- the bearing side rests with nothing standing on the rung, or the other side rests under an unanswered standing item: two levels against that side on the closing draw, never an automatic concession. `forgery_found` -- recorded only by an `answer` graded Overwhelming: every item of the forged Record's origin is struck. `irrelevance` -- an item entered off the rung tried enters at half weight and counts the fault. The conditions are read by the sitting's code by id. [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: the four ids and the order -- basis: HEAR_B's "Faults" paragraph, which is design intent, not code.]

proceeding_ends.source: V2 p2 §C.5 -- the three ends of a sitting.
proceeding_ends.note: HOW A SITTING ENDS. `budget` -- the turns ran out; `rested` -- every speaker rested, so the close is drawn on what was said; `yielded` -- a side conceded the issue. Ordered as V2 lists them.

issue_rungs.source: V2 p2 §B's stasis table (A-134): what each issue weighs.
issue_rungs.note: THE ISSUES A MATTER MAY BE DIVIDED INTO, in the order a sitting takes them; `weighs` maps a ground to the weight it carries on that issue, and a ground a rung does not name weighs 1.0 (so a rung with no `weighs` names none). `procedure` (B24.03) heads them and names none: every ground weighs alike on whether the matter is properly before the court. [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: each weight below -- basis: V2 p2 §B's stasis table; the running model is evidence only.]

authorities.source: V2 p2 §H and §I -- who sits above a proceeding, and the regime's weight for his authority in `power`.
authorities.note: WHOSE AUTHORITY A VENUE RESTS ON. `parties` -- the parties themselves; `polity` -- the crown and its courts; `church`; `guild`; `none`. `by_faction` maps each faction the realm seats to one member: a person's authority is read off the faction he serves. [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: the whole mapping -- basis: `venues.yaml`'s `serves:` tags (Crown, court and Parliament together; Church; Guild). The Crown (Valorsmark), the duchies and the Restoration Movement, and the two foreign factions, are `polity`; the Church of Solmund is `church`; the Guilds are `guild`. `faction x` is a placeholder naming no polity (`names_index.yaml`), and carries none. `guild` is reached through `Guilds`, which `role_templates.by_faction` does not key -- hence the mapping is checked against the `factions` roster and must cover every `role_templates.by_faction` key.]

matters.source: V2 p2 §G -- the twelve kinds of worldly matter; it absorbs the `proofs` roster (retired at B24p.03).
matters.note: WHAT AN ITEM MAY BE, ONE ROW PER KIND: a typed reference, never text. `carrier` is the tree's type the item references (`Record`, a ledger `Claim`, a `Tenure` kind, an earlier matter's case-file stages, the strife reading); `brings` is who may bring it; `cost` is what bringing it writes (read by B24p.22 and the fold). `title`'s carrier is a `hold` Tenure; an `Office` is what it holds. `brings` and `cost` are the table's own words as tokens, checked only as present, until a reader names a closed set. [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: the spelling of every `brings` and `cost` token and of the `carrier` suffix after the colon -- basis: V2 p2 §G's table gives them in prose.] `bears_on` (B24.17; EVID_B "Exact edits" 1) is the `issue_rungs` member an exhibit of the kind bears on: an item's `rung` is derived from its kind, read off this column, never typed on the item. It is a member of `issue_rungs`, refused at import (`data/rosters.py::_load_matters`). [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: `fact` for the four kinds `proofs` held (record, testimony, oath, confession) -- basis: EVID_B's "`fact` for all four members"; and `fact` for the other eight -- basis: none in a document, the same reading carried over, so that no kind bears on a rung the evidence rule does not yet weigh (V2 p2 §G names `precedent` as bearing on `definition`, and EVID_B leaves that fifth member to FI, so it stays `fact` here).] [ASSUMPTION: the refusal of a `bears_on` outside `issue_rungs` -- basis: every closed-set column in this roster file is refused by its loader, `_refuse_not_in`'s practice.]

disposal_writes.source: V2 p2 §J -- the typed writes the fold performs on a sitting's outcome; `arrangements.yaml: disposal:` names them by id.
disposal_writes.note: THE CLOSED SET OF A DISPOSAL ROW'S WRITES, one row each. A `disposal:` cell naming an id outside it is refused at load (`data/arrangements.py::_load_disposal`). `weight` is the one cell a write may carry: how much a claim written to a ledger counts (a yield 1, a hint 0.4: V2 p2 §J); a write with no `weight` carries none. Nothing performs a write until B24p.20 (the sitting) and B24p.22 (the witnesses' ledgers); a bounded write (regard, pursuits, standing, legitimacy, strife) is B27.28's and B33.51's, on B24p.04's fold table. module_kinds.source: plan v8 `_part5` `### A-25` (`ED-IN-0284`, revised by `ED-IN-0285`) -- the seven headings of its roster paragraph.
module_kinds.note: WHAT A `modules:` ENTRY IS, one word each, defined here and in `data/rosters.py` where the loader reads it (`CLAUDE.md` §4). `minigame` -- a scene the player can also play as a game inside the game (combat, mass battle, social contests, fieldwork). `management_space` -- a scene played as an interface over the world (governance, faction management, the character sheet). `world_surface` -- where the player meets NPCs and events: DELIBERATE's player mode, unbuilt. `loop_resident` -- computation that runs inside the season loop's own steps. `data_register` -- a module that is a centralized register of information the loop reads. `host` -- a module of the season loop itself, not one registered into it. `stub` -- not a system of gameplay, kept so its name still resolves.

modules.source: plan v8 `_part5` `### A-25`'s roster paragraph -- authored from the list `ED-IN-0284` and `ED-IN-0285` rule, NOT from the directories that hold code (that test drops `factions`, whose directory holds at most an untracked identifier census).
modules.note: THE ONE OWNER OF RETENTION (A-25, `SM-14`): what the repository keeps as a system, a host concern or a stub, and where each one lives. The KEY is the entry's one identity -- for a module, its directory name (A-25: `combat`, never `personal_combat`; a `provider:` name on a prize row says what runs and is a different name). `kind:` is a `module_kinds` member. `home:` is the repo-relative path the entry lives at -- a directory ends in `/`; `npcs`' is the one file that holds it; a home may not exist yet (`game/` is unbuilt) and nothing here moves a file (`31a`-`31c` move module code into `modules/<name>/`, which A-25 derives from the composition rows, not from this roster). A `systems/<name>/` directory that no entry names as its `home:` is not retained as a system: `R04_PENDING_SUBSYSTEMS` is computed from exactly that. ⚠ [ASSUMPTION, position `30`] the four stubs' homes follow `ED-IN-0284`'s own reasons -- `articulation` and `ui` are presentation (holonic §45's `game/`), `victory` is a set of conditions the host would evaluate (`H-176`; built since as `world_q.endings_reached`, v9 IN-27), `_architecture` is not a system and its subject is Layer 1's -- so none is a `systems/` home, and a `systems/<stub>/` directory, where one exists, stays in `R04_PENDING_SUBSYSTEMS` as `ED-IN-0284` rules (with `npcs`). `factions` keeps `systems/factions/` (`ED-IN-0283`: the folders are the homes of their systems); its automated play is `decision/` (A-25).
