A hearer who holds, untold, a dominance-kind deed done TO the speaker by somebody else (`person_q.suffered_deeds`, the `seen.who` pairing) stops counting every dominance-kind deed of the speaker's no newer than it. Every member must be a deed kind (`data/verbs.py::DEED_KINDS`); `data/verbs.py::_check_dominance_kinds` refuses at import otherwise. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct -- the membership: which acts are coercive is stated nowhere in the corpus; revert: an empty `dominance` list, and no hearer's weight is ever eroded -- and, since v9 IN-23, `person_q.UNREST_KINDS` is empty too, so `person_q.stability`'s deed half counts nothing.]

inquiry_modules.source: v9 FI-02 (`SM-3`, Jordan 2026-09-05: *"investigation is not a contest seam. it is its own thing."*), built in one landing with FI-03 (`ED-FI-0002`, the counter-espionage loop with fieldwork as host): the second role in `manifest/registry.py::_ROLE_ROSTERS`, `inquiry`.
inquiry_modules.note: ⚠ KEYED BY THE KIND A FINDING EMITS, NEVER BY THE VERB. `graded_tasks` is already the verb-keyed table, and FI-01 rules it a ROUTE that carries `{provider, module_entry}` and, from B07.01, `form` and `armed_by` (`data/verbs.py`), so a second verb-keyed table would be two tables on one key. A prize is what is contested; the inquiry analogue is what is FOUND, so the key is the Event kind -- `undeposited_kinds`' keying, for its reason. A `Failure` inquiry emits `finding.none`, which no row claims, so `manifest.resolve("inquiry", ...)` answers `None` and nothing is found, with no branch on a band anywhere in the host. An ungraded `finding.made` (`interview`, `reconstruct`, `thread_read`) reaches the row and finds nothing: it carries no degree, and `finding_terms` keys on the degree. Each row names `module:` (the module's one identity, its directory, A-25), `provider:` (`@provider("inquiry", ...)`, `seam/wrappers/fieldwork.py`) and `module_entry:` (the composition row the provider calls through `MODULE_ENTRIES`). Refused at driver construction by `manifest/registry.py::check_inquiry_modules`, and at boot by `check_rows()` naming the row.

finding_terms.source: v9 FI-03 (`ED-FI-0002`): what a graded finding learns of a trail, by its degree. The terms are `observation_terms`' (`epistemic.Seen`'s fields): the finder holds what a witness of the act would have held, through the same deposit shapes, masked to these terms.
finding_terms.note: [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: every finding band shows the hand (the partial band gains `who`)]. KEYED BY DEGREE BAND (`engine/dice_engine/dice_engine.py::DEGREE_LABEL`, the one owner; a key off the ladder is refused at load, `data/rosters.py::_load_finding_terms`) and valued in `observation_terms` members (a term outside them is refused). A band with no row uncovers nothing: the failing band has none, and an ungraded finding has no band. In words: a partial finding learns THAT the deed was done to the thing, and a better one also learns WHOSE HAND did it. ⚠ A PARTIAL FINDING WITHHOLDS `who` FROM THE FINDER (an inference is less than a sight) -- both the `seen` claim's `who` term and the event-kind claim anchored on the actor. A WITNESS'S anchor claim is NOT masked: a witness admitted by any channel holds `(actor, kind, True)` under `claim_subject_rule: both` whatever its channel shows of `who`. So the two quantities differ BY DESIGN -- a finder's knowledge of a hand is graded, a witness's event-kind claim is not. `why` is never shown to a finder: no band lists it (`epistemic._term_why`'s antecedent is a witness's). The better bands are identical: depth has no carrier (FI-01's own note on the finding bands). ⚠ `bands:`, NOT `values:`: the mapping's keys are the ladder's labels, which this file does not own, and a `values:` row is read as a roster of its keys (`test_season_shape.py`'s duplicate-roster scan), so the ladder would have read as declared twice. B11.71 (`08_FI_03` §2, FRES §8): THE SAME ROW ALSO LISTS WHICH `look_reads` A BAND DEPOSITS, so one band-keyed table owns what a finding shows -- of a trail (the terms) and of what is looked at (the reads), never two tables. A row lists a read by its `look_reads` name; a verb row's `observes:` says WHAT IS LOOKED AT and never a band, and `loop/witness.py` deposits an observed read only where the Event's band lists its stem. In words: a look at `Overwhelming` or `Success` teaches every read; at `Partial` all but `held_by` (who holds a thing is the sight a good look gives), a number through the lossy-copy rule (`loop/witness.py::_told_value`); at `Failure` -- no row -- none, and the reads the row's own cell made (the gating reads) are deposited at every band and on a refusal, as before. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: every look read at every finding band, `held_by` included.] B24.34 (ARCS item 4; [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop `holds` from the three bands and from `look_reads`]): `holds` -- WHO HAS A RECORD IN HIS KEEPING, as a claim about the holder -- is listed at EVERY finding band, `Partial` included: the finder learns the person even where `held_by`, the same fact said of the Record, is withheld. That is two bands for one fact, kept because ARCS's gate reads `Partial` and the B11.71 withholding is its own assumption.

look_reads.source: B11.71 (`08_FI_03` §2, FRES §8; C-24, R-35, H-218): THE READS A LOOK MAY TAKE -- the closed set a verb row's `observes:` entry names (`data/verbs.py::Look.read`) and a `finding_terms` band row lists. A read is named by the predicate stem it deposits under.
look_reads.note: `condition` of a Site (`(site, condition, n)`); `stores` of a Rung (`(rung, stores:<kind>, n)` for each kind it holds; a Site's look reads the rung it stands in); `held_by` of a Rung or a Record (`(thing, held_by:<holder>, True)` for each live `hold`); `content` of a Record (`(record, content:<kind>, <what it says>)`, the claim a holder's deposit mints, read without taking the hold). The answerer is `queries/world_q.py::WorldReader.look`, which dispatches on exactly these members and answers nothing for a subject of another class; a member no row's `observes:` names is a read nothing takes. Disjoint from `observation_terms` (the trail's terms), refused at load. B24.34 (ARCS item 4; `12_ARCS_cited_evidence` named an `observation_terms` member `holder`, but `observation_terms` IS `epistemic.Seen`'s struct, a mask over a `seen` claim about a trail, and a look at a Record is not a trail; this roster is the one a look is listed in): `holds` of a Record (`(holder, holds, record)` for each live `hold` a PERSON has over it, the claim about the holder, held WITHOUT taking the hold). Named for its predicate, as every member is. A look never teaches a man a claim about himself (`loop/witness.py`).

covert_kinds.source: v9 FI-03 (`ED-FI-0002`): the deed kinds that leave a FINDABLE trail -- an Event an inquiry can uncover for someone no witness channel admitted (`epistemic.trail_of`).
covert_kinds.note: DATA, NOT A WALK OF EVERY DEED KIND: a kind joins the trail by a line here, and each member must be a deed kind the verb table emits (`data/verbs.py::DEED_KINDS`; refused at import, naming it, `data/verbs.py::_check_covert_kinds`), so a misspelling cannot find nothing and report the trail built. A deed that writes a place, an alias or a person leaves a trail (B11.59, CP-T06-01 with `16_PESSIMIST_FI_C` edits 1-2): `record.forged` (`forge`, v9 IN-45), `site.damaged` (`sabotage`, a place), `cover.assumed` (`conceal`, an alias: the cover Record), and the deeds done to a person -- `person.died`, `body.changed`, `person.captured`. A covert `destroy_record` (H-75), `arrest` and a costed `surveil` (ED-FI-0009) are unbuilt and belong to their own positions. THE MEMBERSHIP RULE, so the next member is decided by it and not by taste. A deed kind is covert when (i) no `binding_decision` row emits it, so `reach` (`event_reach`) never carries it; (ii) its row has no `remit:` eligibility, so it is not done through a seat and `post_remit` never reports it; (iii) it writes a thing some graded inquiry takes as its subject (a Site for `examine`, a Record for `research`, a Person for `interview` and `surveil` at the place -- the card's "or a person"). AT THIS TREE, (i) holds for all six; (ii) holds for `record.forged`, `site.damaged`, `cover.assumed` and for `fight`'s and `accept`'s `person.died` and `body.changed`, and not for `capture`'s (a `remit:dispatch` row, which also emits `person.captured`) or `march`'s `person.died`; `body.changed` has a `reach` (`event_reach` `from_unrest`: settlement), which admits the settlement's own persons by news and leaves the trail to everyone else. The six are the card's list (FI_C edit 1), kept whole; a seat-done emission also reaches the obligee, which closes his own trail through `holds_trail`. `trail_of` keeps only Events a person did (a MATTER `body.changed`, from hunger, is no trail) and `holds_trail` excludes a finder who witnessed the deed. Why a trail is reachable only through a plant: see `epistemic.trail_of`.

strife_kinds.source: CR-75 (workplan v11, batch B11-S3): which Event KINDS the person reading may count as a strife move. Read by `data/rosters.py::STRIFE_KINDS`; checked at import against `EVENT_KINDS` in `data/verbs.py::_check_strife_kinds`. A step of the loop reads it: `queries/world_q.py::questions_for` through `flows_known` and `flow_stakes` (CR-78's stamp, `stamp_flow_stakes`, shipped ON).
strife_kinds.note:
WHY A KIND LIST. The person reading sees an Event's kind and nothing else, and the registry's `kinds` columns (`harness/strife_moves.yaml`) are upper bounds: read as the definition of a move they would make `news.told`, `duty.taken` and `travel.moved` strife, and strands ordinary life. THE FOUR LISTS (under `lists:`, because `roster_map` returns a mapping; `values:` names them, so the loader spells none of them and refuses a missing or an extra list):
  opens     a kind whose presence alone meets the study's test, so one claim of it starts a strand.
  joins     a kind that is a move only in company: it attaches to a strand an `opens` kind started
            and may conclude it, and never starts one.
  never     everyday or refusal kinds. Explicit, so every kind the registry names has a decision
            (`tests/test_strife_kinds.py` refuses a registry kind in none of the three).
  concludes the kinds that may conclude a strand AT THE PERSON READING: a kind concludes only if
            every code it maps to in `strife_moves.yaml` is terminal (`ends` above 0 and not XP),
            so a kind that maps to one code which never ends a case does not conclude (`detention.ended`
            and `ban.ended` map to AM; `field.won` and `field.lost` to WR; `tenure.closed` to BR;
            `requisition.taken` to VI). Of those `field.won` and `field.lost` ended a case in the world reading (code WA, through the verb
            and side) until B12a.04, which made them OPENING moves (never terminal); the rest end no case
            in either reading. A hand-maintained list over the opens and joins kinds, checked
            by `tests/test_strife_kinds.py`'s re-derivation (it is red where the list and the rule
            disagree). B12a.05 (A-45): a content-opening kind (`queries/world_q.py::CONTENT_OPENING_KINDS`:
            `succession.claimed`, `petition.filed`) is never in it, whatever its codes -- a claim of the
            movement's own beginning is no end of it; `check_strife_openers` refuses the overlap at import.
            Top-down the world sees a war end; bottom-up a
            person who holds only a field's outcome may still doubt it.
The checks at import: a kind in any list absent from `EVENT_KINDS`; a kind in more than one of opens, joins and never; a `concludes` kind outside opens and joins. `concludes` is checked against `ends` counts hand-read from the study and cross-checked against it (A3, `strife-00` §10; `strife_moves.yaml`). [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: each of the five rulings of `strife-01` §6 reverses alone by moving one kind between `opens` and `joins`, or striking one content opener; to revert `concludes`, make it an empty derivation in code: a code edit at `Move.terminal`'s construction in both readings (`queries/world_q.py::flows_in` and `_known_moves`) and in `_check_strife_kinds`. Dropping `concludes` from `values:`/`lists:` raises a KeyError at import (`world_q` and `data/verbs.py` index it directly). With no concluding kinds no strand ever concludes.]

foreign_factions.source: CR-75: moved here from `harness/strife_moves.yaml` (one owner; R16's text unchanged), so `queries/world_q.py`, which may not import the harness, can read it. Read by `data/rosters.py::FOREIGN_FACTIONS`.
foreign_factions.note: The two foreign nations, external, functioning as spoilers and limits on the game world (Jordan, 2026-11-04): the Altonian Empire and Schoenland. NOT `foreign_cast`: that row names the factions `build_realm(foreign=True)` seats, and Schoenland is not among them. `queries/world_q.py::side_against` reads this, through `data/rosters.py::FOREIGN_FACTION_IDS`, for the side rule's `O` (a foreign faction, whatever it governs).

endings.source: v9 IN-27 (END-VICTORY), on #457 D6's adopted answer (`workplans/valoria_master_workplan_v9_part5.md` RS-21 row 3): *"the ending vocabulary is a Query over holds and seats that the season reports -- never an actor"*. Read by `queries/world_q.py::endings_reached`, reported by `loop/driver.py::SeasonDriver.season` as `endings`.
endings.note: WHAT ENDS A PLAYED REALM, as opposed to its running out of seasons. Terms, defined where the loader reads them (`CLAUDE.md` §4): an ENDING is a row here; it is REACHED when every hold its `holds:` selects is live and every holder coheres under `under:`, AND an act opened at least one edge the condition stands on (`T-b`: the realm as built reaches nothing; a holder's `commit` is such an edge only when it is his sole live commit to that faction, so a redundant `commit` act is not credited). ⚠ THE CROSSING ITSELF MAY BE AUTHORLESS: an old `commit` act is credited while a MATTER death (no act) completes the condition, and no pure read can locate the crossing, because the moment the condition was last false is not stored (`T-a`) [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]. Revert: every edge the condition reads opened by an act -- which makes `peninsular_sovereignty` unreachable by construction (every seeded territory hold re-opened by an act, and `terr_T15`'s, unheld at build, by a verb that does not exist, `H-186`). A `holds:` selects by a world field, EXACTLY ONE of `{post: <an offices.yaml seat post>}` (every Office with that post; since v10 CP-T02-02 a seat an `offices.yaml` row stands for is built under that row's id, and a seat with no row keeps its `off_<holder>` slug) or `{rung_kind: <a rung_kinds member>}` (every rung of that kind UNDER A `realm` RUNG, held at or above it, `holder_faction_of`'s walk; `terr_T16`, Schoenland's foreign root, is outside the realm and not selected), which may carry `settled: true` beside it and nothing else (only the rungs with a `settlement` rung among their descendants). `under:` is a `factions` member, or `one_faction` (every selected holder under the same faction, whichever). `victory:` marks GD-1's win path; GD-1 permits exactly one, and the load refuses a second. A row stores nothing and is not an actor: reaching one emits no Event, halts nothing and writes nothing (`SeasonDriver.season` reports it). ⚠ NOT CARRIED, BY THE CUTS: no stored stability or legitimacy value, no threshold counter, no clock (#457 §5; `T-a`, `T-b`, `T-c`).

peninsular_sovereignty.source: GD-1 (`canon/04_game_design_constraints.md`): *"Peninsular Sovereignty is the sole victory condition ... control all 15 territories"*.
peninsular_sovereignty.assumption_note: [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct] GD-1's other clauses are not carried: `Accord >= 2` and `Political Stability <= 6` read stored scalars #457 §5 cuts, `sustained 2 consecutive seasons` is a clock, and `treaties counting` has no carrier. Every SETTLED territory under a `realm` rung counts (`settled: true`: a `settlement` rung among its descendants), not a fixed 15; `terr_T15`, which has none, and the foreign root (`terr_T16`, Schoenland's, kept out of the realm by `build_realm`) are not asked for. A structural predicate, no territory id named. A consumer that treats `victory: true` as the game's end must carry this caveat itself -- the row is GD-1 minus its sustain, Accord and Stability clauses, and nothing in the loop halts on it (`SeasonDriver.season` only reports `endings`). Revert: Jordan names a carrier for any of them.

theocracy.source: #457 D6's context (RS-21 row 3), Jordan 2026-10-04: *"ratcheting of Church as faction until it attempts to seize lands and become a theocracy"* -- an endpoint. NOT a victory: GD-1 strikes `Altonian Theocracy` as an alternate win path.
theocracy.assumption_note: [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct] "become a theocracy" is read as the King's seat held by a person who coheres under the Church of Solmund (a Church man crowned, or a king converted). The land half ("seize lands") is not a condition. Revert: Jordan names the Church's endpoint.

advantage_sources.source: CP-T01-05 (`proposals/2026-10-23-subsystem-completion/2026-10-23-subsystem-completion-01-resolution- and-dice.md` §2), read as INTENT; the form is `resolution-diagnostic` §2's: advantage reaches a roll only as named levels through `levels_to_net_sigma` -> `net_boost`, a mu-shift, never a flat bonus on the net and never an Ob reduction.
advantage_sources.note: THE ONLY DOOR INTO THE SOCIAL ROLL'S SIGMA TERM. `seam/wrappers/sigma.py::contest_input` sums the named levels each member returns for the act and hands the sum to `levels_to_net_sigma`; with no member contributing (the shipped chooser forms no `effort`) the term is 0.0 and the roll is as it was. A later source (a threat, a held secret, a held finding, a bribe) is a ROW HERE plus its function in `sigma.ADVANTAGE_SOURCES`, never a flat bonus on the net and never an inline re-derivation of `net_boost`. `seam/wrappers/sigma.py` refuses at import a member with no function and a function with no member, so the roster is the closed set and the table is its binding. `effort`: an act carrying `effort` e in its payload (0, 1 or 2) contributes e levels named by the `effort_level` fixture (`Fixtures`, shipped `moderate`) and fills `1 + e` of its scene's interaction slots (`state/carriers.py::Scene.slots`), so effort's whole cost is the acts the person does not take in that scene. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete this row and `sigma.ADVANTAGE_SOURCES`' `effort` entry -- the channel then sums to 0.0 and `Scene.slots` counts every act as one slot]. `capability` (B05.10, MAP §G edit 6): the `edge` rows of `tables.capability_uses` at the act's site, read by ONE function (`sigma._capability_levels`), so a skill, an attribute or a trait becomes a level on the roll by a ROW and never by a function per trait. THE CHANNEL IS SIGNED: each member returns `(levels for the roller, levels against him)`; `levels_to_net_sigma` takes both lists. A row's count is once when held (`per: held`), once per rank (`per: rank`) or the signed steps of the held value from its scale's mid-point (`per: mid`: above counts for the side named, below against; an unauthored value is the mid-point, zero steps); `against: true` flips the sign, so it counts against the ROLLER. No `edge` row ships at the social roll (B05.25: the roller's attributes are in his dice, averaged, and the opponent's is the opposition's), so the member returns no level and the roll is as it was. `proofs` (B05.17, PES-A edit 1): one `proof_level` per whole unit of `world_q.proofs(speaker, opponent, venue)` (the remove-weighted, unmirrored sum, rounded half up). `favour`: one `favour_level` per whole unit of `reception_gain x reception` where that is positive. Both are FOR the roller only (the defender list waits on cited items, B24); a hostile bench is not here but the obstacle's `reception` member. A fixture of None is the control: the source brings no level. `office` (B05.20, U1-D, D-U1-01a): the one level named by the `modifier:` of the seat an act is exercised through (`Act.via`), where the prize row says `heard_by: bench` and that seat sits over the room (`state/gate.py::sits_over`); FOR the roller only (the defender column is struck, OBS §3). A seat declaring none, an act through no seat and a prize no bench hears bring no level; no shipped row authors a `modifier:` (the bench seats' first values land with B05.23). `wounds` (B05.60, ADV Edits B to D; A-8): one `wound_level` AGAINST the roller per `wound_step` of body his person has lost below his `body_ceiling`, and one FOR him per `wound_step` the person he acts on has lost, each side at most `wound_levels_max` (`sigma._wound_levels`); never an obstacle term and never a die. A person subject's body is read only by the true input: a believer's own body is his to know, another's is not (`believed_input`). A `wound_level` of None is the control: the source brings no level.

thread_operations.source: `09_WR_threadwork_module` edit 3: the seven operations `systems/threadwork/sim/operations.py` has an entry point for (`attempt_leap`, `attempt_weaving`, `attempt_pulling`, `attempt_past_pulling`, `attempt_locking`, `attempt_dissolution`, `attempt_mending`).
thread_operations.note: WHAT A THREAD OPERATION IS: one named working a practitioner attempts on the thread, as an operation is one task performed. The closed set of their names, read by `data/verbs.py`'s verb loader: a verb row that names one through its `operation:` column names a member or the load refuses at import, as it refuses an off-roster `beneficiary:`. NO SHIPPED ROW NAMES ONE YET -- the thread rows (CP-T07-03, -04, -11) are B35's. The names are the roster's own spelling, not the oracle's labels (`operations.py` reports `Weaving`, `Past-Oriented Pulling`, `Locking`): the oracle under `systems/` may not import `engine/season`, so it reads no list from here and keeps its labels. `knot` joins when the `tie` / `knot` split lands (A-28, B35).

standing_occasion_opened_by.note: THE EVENT KINDS THAT OPEN A STANDING OCCASION OF EACH REFERENT CLASS, most specific first -- a mapping, `{class: [kinds]}`, each class a `referent_classes` member. A standing occasion is a classed referent a person's question carries (`state/carriers.py::Question.classes`: a vacancy, a writ held, a wounded person, a detainee, a larder, a flow stake); the OPENING Event is the first kind listed here that `World.last_emission_of(kind, referent, written=True)` finds in the log, and `loop/resolve.py::_occasion_ids` puts its id after the act's own in `causes[]` of every Event the act folds (one id, so `causes[]` does not fan; nothing when the log holds none, as for a seat vacant since the build). Read by `data/rosters.py::STANDING_OCCASION_OPENED_BY`; held at import to `data/verbs.py::EVENT_KINDS`, which is every verb row's `emits` plus the fold, MATTER and CALENDAR kinds (`_check_standing_occasion_opened_by`, beside `_check_strife_kinds`), and to `referent_classes`. Switched by `Fixtures.standing_occasion_cause` (H-457; `False` is the control: no opening Event is named). site_yield.source: `W8` / `H-93`. #353 §25 lists `yield` as written at MATTER and *blocked on `season_factor`'s distribution* (§22.3); it never says what a place produces.
site_yield.note: ⚠ WHAT A HARBOUR PRODUCES IS INVENTED. #353 supplies the BARRIER, the ORDER and the BLOCKER and no quantities at all, so this table is an injected default with a row and a sweep — the same standing as `alignment` and `band_floors`, and stated here rather than left to look derived. ⚠ WHAT IS *NOT* INVENTED IS THE SCALING. Production is the base scaled by the site's `condition / condition_scale` and then by `season_factor`. Condition is the model (`H-38` closed with *"`Site.condition` is the model"*), `condition_scale` is an existing registered fixture, and `season_factor` is #353's own named blocker — so a WORN PLACE PRODUCES LESS without a second wear concept being invented to make it do so. That is why yield is keyed on the SITE and not on the rung: the rung has no quantity that could fall. ⚠ `none` IS THE CONTROL ARM, not a third opinion: with every cell zero the economy has no source, every store depletes monotonically, and `W8`'s own proof clause must fail. A sweep whose control arm cannot break the claim is not a control.

band_floors.source: #353 §12.1 / L5 — the band edges a crossing fires on. `H-08`.
band_floors.note: ⚠ MOVED OUT OF THE INSTRUMENT BODY BY `W8` for `wear_per_season`'s reason. The verb keys are SITE-USE verbs (what the site is good for at that condition), NOT verb-table rows, so unlike `alignment` this table is not validated against `verb_table.yaml` — a check that would fail on every cell. The outer key IS validated against `site_kinds`. ⚠ THE FLOORS ARE INVENTED. #353 states that a band edge crossing emits and may produce no outcome; it supplies no edges. `H-08` is the row, and until `W8` it was an `assumption` with no `site:` and no sweep at all — one of `PLAN.md` §1.5's unowned residue, now owned. ⚠ `dwelling: {}` IS EMPTY ON PURPOSE (`24d-i`, the control arm beside `wear_per_season`'s `dwelling: 0`). No floor means no band edge, so `loop/matter.py`'s `_crossings` fires nothing for a dwelling at any wear. `halved` and `doubled` leave an empty cell empty. ⚠ AN EMPTY CELL IS NOT A WORKABLE SITE, AND THE `floor` READ SAYS SO TYPED: `queries/ world_q.py`'s `floor` stem checks `if not floors:` before `min(floors.values())` and raises a typed `Unspecified` (S12.1) rather than a bare `ValueError` on `{}` (`world_q.py`'s own comment at the guard names `dwelling`'s control-arm row by id). It is unreached only while no question names a dwelling as a referent, since `work` binds its `site` from the referent. None does at the control arm; `24d-i`'s test in `engine/season/tests/test_governance_build.py` asserts it over one populated season. ⚠ `garrison: {}` IS EMPTY FOR THE SAME REASON, NOT A SEPARATE CHOICE (M4, `ED-IN-0279` clause (a)). A field battle's fortification term reads `Site.condition` DIRECTLY -- `queries/ world_q.fortification_of` -- never through `floor`'s band-crossing read, so the empty cell is never reached: nothing names a garrison as a `work`-style referent, and no march-battle code calls `floor` on one. Filling this in would invent a band-crossed Question a garrison cannot yet answer (no verb writes `Site.exists`/`condition` toward it from the field-battle side except through the unbuilt `restore`), which is `wear_per_season`'s `garrison: 0` note applied to the other half of the same table.

lifepath_templates.note: ⚠ A CUT, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION. Every authored dice magnitude (+1D, +2D, TS +3, Ob and strain changes) is DROPPED: a template names which of the skills a verb's `capability:` column names (`copying`, `argue`, `inquiry`; `descriptors.CAPABILITIES`) a lifepath's starting skills draw on, and nothing else. A key is held at `pool_default`, so the grant changes no pool; it makes the key one `train` can raise (`loop/effects_combat.py::_eff_train` raises only a key the subject already holds). A lifepath whose starting skills no key covers holds NONE (`holds: []`), RECORDED here and not invented. ⚠ THE RULE EACH ROW WAS READ BY, so a reviewer can re-read the text and not the taste. Only the `★` skills count: the `Third Skill (spark)` column is a skill that may be sparked later, not held at creation (the archived file's own header, `Starting Skills (★)` against `Third Skill (spark)`). `argue` is named when a starting skill's text says the Argue act, or adds dice to, or moves a resistance parameter of, the Argue exchange itself (a Recall bonus in a contest genre, an Obscuring bonus in a private negotiation, Audience Resistance: `social_contest_v30.md:102,115,168,177`); a strain, an Appraise, a Regroup or a payout on a win is not the roll and holds nothing. `inquiry` is named when it says Investigation, institutional records or documents recalled (`research`), assessing or authenticating a thing of the kinds `examine` reads (evidence, architecture, documents, objects: `verb_table.yaml` `examine`), or recon of a place (`surveil`: observe a location, person or operation). `copying` is named when it says relaying or copying a text; no starting skill does, so no row holds it. A text that says only a bonus in a domain, a defence, a strain, an identification of forces, the threat of a being or a navigation holds nothing, and the near misses are said in the row's own `ground:` (3-CH3, 3-CR5, 3-HA3, 3-LO2, 3-LO4, and 3-CF4's Knot, which names copying). The wider reading (Appraise, strain and Regroup effects inside the contest also hold `argue`) is NOT adopted; it would add argue to 3-CR3, 3-VA1, 3-VA4, 3-GU1, 3-LO3, 3-CF3 and 3-CF5. CLOSED, BOTH WAYS (`data/rosters.py::_load_lifepaths`): a row for every id of `rosters: lifepaths` and for nothing else, each `holds:` entry a skill of `descriptors.CAPABILITIES`, a `ground:` on every row. affiliation_engagement.source: the retired affiliation-content draft (its `FORK:` row in `references/restructure_ledger.md`) §4.2 (R-C4.1, R-C4.2, R-C4.3) and §4.3 (the sketch), FOLDED INTO THE BUILD by Jordan 2026-10-06 (RS-1, ED-IN-0291). The shared column's ten cells and their reasons are the old `sacred` alignment row as it stood before IN-08's cells work removed it (`git show 16faff76:engine/season/ rosters.yaml`, the `sacred:` block of `alignment`), carried as R-C4.1 says. v9 IN-11 (#453 R-3 (b)) cut `repudiate` and DROPPED its shared cell (-0.6, the vow-break) with the row -- not moved onto `release`, which ends a commitment voluntarily and is a different act -- so nine of the ten remain.
affiliation_engagement.note: THREE CLAUSES, ONE TABLE. (R-C4.1) THE SHARED COLUMN `sacred`: the vow-shaped verbs engage EVERY affiliation identically -- a vow is a vow under every creed on the roster -- so the column is not per affiliation; a verb's cell here is its cell for every affiliation a person holds. (R-C4.2) THE PER-AFFILIATION CELLS: a verb violates a NAMED affiliation only where canon says that affiliation condemns the act's kind. They are graded `derived, sign only`, so each is `-1` or `1` and the loader refuses any other value: the 1 is a unit, not a weight, and a reader that wants a magnitude must be given authored values first. A verb carries a shared cell or per-affiliation cells, never both: no source says how the two would compose, so the loader refuses the overlap rather than choose a rule. (R-C4.3) CONTENT-KEYED VIOLATIONS ARE NOT CELLS: `utter`, `speak`, `tell`, `create_record` and `destroy_record` violate an affiliation by WHAT is said or recorded (forbidden vocabulary, an Einhir record destroyed), which needs a tag on the Proposition or Record read at RESOLVE by the same scar writer. No such tag exists; nothing here stands in for it, and `destroy_record`'s shared cell is the vow-shaped half only. ⚠ TWO OF THE DRAFT'S CELLS ARE NOT CARRIED, BOTH NARROWER READINGS [ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct]. (i) `restore` "as Mending" (draft §4.3: `-` under `solmund_orthodoxy`, `+` under `einhir_restoration`): the draft read `restore` as Mending's nearest verb on the premise that it is unresolvable; that premise is stale -- `restore` executes, and what it does is raise a Site's `condition` (`loop/effects_economy.py::_eff_restore`), a repair of fabric, not a thread operation. With no way to tell a Mending from mending a wall, carrying the cell would scar every orthodox witness of a house repair. Revert: a thread-operation verb or a restore kind exists, and the two cells land on it. (ii) The shared column's `fight` (was `kill / wound`) and `surveil` cells are `null`, as R-C4.1 strikes them: the first reason was self-flagged as unsourced inference, the second is a cost rather than a creed. ⚠ NEARLY INERT IN PLAY TODAY, AND SAID RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Every cast row holds `affiliations:` since IN-64 (a cast person can be scarred on one); the corpus builder `build_at` still fills no `Person.conviction`, so the `11` and corpus worlds hold none. Of the verbs carrying a negative cell, only `destroy_record` is in `resolvable_verbs()`, and it refuses through the fold (`H-75`); `thread_read` writes nothing at RESOLVE, and the scar is earned only by an outcome that MOVED state (`_fold`'s `changed`), so its cell cannot fire even when it becomes resolvable unless it gains a RESOLVE write.

[ASSUMPTION; Jordan to correct: that renewal gives one step and clears the count -- basis: the source's "faith renewed"; no figure beyond +1.] Success -- HE HOLDS: nothing on the intensity, and `scar: threshold_less_one` (the count is set to the threshold less one, so it will take another wound to test him again). The third arm replaces the unbuilt RESTABILISE branch of `conviction_after_crisis`, so no person in crisis is a no-op; `conviction_map`'s closed spine is kept (integers, clamped), so no rounding rule is needed. role_template_pursuits.source: systems/factions/reference/faction_canon_v30.md §4 "Role Templates and Expected Convictions" (per PP-686 §3.3.1, over the PP-684 13-Conviction taxonomy). TIER 2 — near-canon, and it survives because `systems/world/` has no competing concept, the same standing `role_templates` itself has.
role_template_pursuits.note: ⚠ **WHAT A FACTION EXPECTS OF ITS MEMBERS, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS WHAT ANY MEMBER HOLDS.** `pursuit_projection` maps a PERSON's fifteen weights into the seven axes; this maps a ROLE TEMPLATE's expectations onto the same fifteen. The two multiply against each other nowhere — they are different objects with one shared vocabulary, and the vocabulary is the canonical fifteen in both cases, read from the single owner. ⚠ **TRANSCRIBED, THEN MIGRATED BY A STATED RULE.** Every cell is §4's own weight, carried to the fifteen by the retired pursuit-cells draft's §4.1/§4.2 (see the comment above `cells:`). Nothing is normalised, rounded or filled in here, and a template's unlisted pursuits read `default_cell` (0.0) rather than being assigned a share. ⚠ **SIX TEMPLATES, AND TWO FACTIONS HAVE NONE.** `role_templates.by_faction` covers Crown, Church of Solmund, Hafenmark, Varfell, Löwenritter and Restoration Movement. `Guilds` and `Schoenland` are absent from §4's player-eligible column and get no row — the same deliberate gap `role_templates` already records, and inventing `mercantile-procedural` for the Guilds is exactly the fabrication the source-precedence ruling exists to stop. ⚠ `intelligence-diplomatic` IS UNCLAIMED BY ANY FACTION and is transcribed anyway, because §4 carries it and `role_templates` already lists it as a member no faction holds. ⚠ **VARFELL AND LÖWENRITTER SHARE `military-order`, WHICH IS CANON.** §4: *"their differentiation comes from Mission, leader Convictions, and stat profile, not role template."* So the two factions have the SAME expectation vector and differ in who actually holds what — which is precisely the quantity `cast.loyalty` measures.

pursuit_projection.source: the retired pursuit-cells draft (its `FORK:` row in `references/restructure_ledger.md`) §2 (the 105 cells; grid at §2.16, revision 5), FOLDED INTO THE BUILD by Jordan 2026-10-06 (RS-1, ED-IN-0291); `doctrine` and `stewardship` named by RS-2 and RS-4. Shape 15x7, sign per `references/descriptor_registry.yaml: axis_roster.scale`.
pursuit_projection.note: ⚠⚠ **105 CELLS, EVERY ONE GRADED, NONE NULL, AND EACH ROW CITES THE DRAFT SECTION THAT ARGUES IT.** The draft's grades are `cited` (transcribed from a source holding the number, at most a sign flip), `derived`/`analogy` (direction read off a source, magnitude the draft's) and `reasoned` (no corpus citation; placed by stated definitional reasoning — the 55 cells Jordan accepted "as placed" in the 2026-10-06 fold). A row's comment marks its reasoned cells. The per-cell argument is the draft's §2.N table for that pursuit, readable at its `FORK:` ref once the draft retires; the values here are the build's, and the draft is not a reason the behaviour is correct (`CLAUDE.md` §0.05). ⚠ **IT IS A PROJECTION, NOT A SECOND OPINION ABOUT VERBS.** It maps a person's fifteen pursuit weights into the seven-axis basis and stops there. What a verb is worth on an axis is `alignment`'s, and nothing here names a verb. ⚠ **THE `doctrine` ROW IS PROVISIONAL** at the draft's revision-5 values (Jordan 2026-10-06, RS-3: *"when we get to cell values and cosines for the axes*poles stuff, doctrine will change"*). It is the MAGNITUDE of a person's orientation toward religious matters, not its DIRECTION (which side is `Person.conviction`'s, ED-IN-0251 R1/R2) — so its cells are non-zero only where all four of Jordan's examples agree (§2.11). THE DOCTRINE PAIR (Jordan's devout Solmund builder against the Einhir dismantler, both high `doctrine`) IS MEASURED, NOT GATED: at `doctrine` .45 the two persons' projections through THIS table read cos +0.229 — inside the 60-degree bar (cos <= 0.5); at `doctrine` .60 / .70 the draft read +0.524 / +0.527, just outside it. H7 (B-H) builds the standing test that pins it. ⚠ **`row: H-46`, CLOSED AS FRAMED BY IN-43.** Jordan, 2026-09-02: *"convictions roster and axes etc may be modified in future."* The sweep is the standard three: `declared` is this matrix, `uniform` makes every pursuit project identically and is THE CONTROL — under it a person's pursuits cannot discriminate between axes at all — and `sign_only` keeps the directions the draft argues and discards the magnitudes it calibrates.

alignment.note: ⚠ THESE WEIGHTS ARE ARGUED, NOT SOURCED, AND THE ROW IS WHAT MAKES THAT LAWFUL. PLAN `W5`: the table is "**registered as its own `assumption` row** … **the table is a row before it is a formula**." §G's discipline is DECLARE · DEFAULT · SWEEP, and all three are discharged — `H-66` is the declaration, this is the default, and `sweep: [declared, uniform, sign_only]` is the sweep. Each cell carries its grade and one-line reason: `carried` (an old-table cell moved to the new axis with its reason, sign per `axis_roster.scale`), `derived` (direction read off the verb row's text or an old reason re-homed, magnitude the draft's) and `reasoned` (the six extension verbs, placed by the same method in IN-08's cells commit). A reason is not a citation. ⚠ `selfish_selfless` CARRIES NO NON-NULL CELL, BY DESIGN (draft §3.4): the per-candidate fact "for whom" is single-owned by `verb_table.yaml`'s `beneficiary:` column (ED-IN-0261: *"the selfish axis score supplies the disposition, the column supplies the per-candidate fact"*); a cell here would be a second copy of that column. Its row is all `null`, so the density rule still sees every verb considered on it. ⚠ EXCEPT `fight` AND `accept` (v11 CR-87, ED-IN-0340, RULED: *"almost every pursuit-conviction profile finds it unwanted"*): their cell is a COST OF VIOLENCE, -0.3 on every axis, this one included, not a reading of who benefits [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: `fight` null here and on four more axes (+0.3 on `deontological_instrumental`), and `accept`'s own cells]. ⚠ IT MUST NOT BE A ZERO MATRIX and `--check` enforces it. PLAN §W5's guardrail: "a zero matrix makes convictions inert, which is the dead-carrier defect #353 `:739-744` names, and it would pass every test while meaning nothing". `default_cell: 0.0` is the SPARSE default for an unlisted pair, which is a different thing from an all-zero table: the loader raises if every listed cell is also zero. ⚠ `uniform` IS THE CONTROL, not a third opinion. Every cell equal makes `Σ_axis conviction · alignment` constant across verbs, so convictions cannot discriminate at all. A verdict that does NOT move between `declared` and `uniform` is a verdict the table was never deciding. VERB KEYS ARE VERB-TABLE KEYS, spelled exactly as `verb_table.yaml` spells them (`evade / defy`, `fight`). The loader raises on a key naming no verb, so a rename over there cannot leave a silently dead cell over here. The draft's `kill`/`wound` cells are moot: they are not verbs (Jordan, RS-5; ED-IN-0288).

verbs.requires_typed_note: §E3 `:426` — *the Proposition exists (immutable, §14)*. Definite article: the one the act commits to, which is the act's `subject`. §14 makes a Proposition immutable and `utter` is the only verb that creates one, so this is the clause that makes `utter` a precondition of the social layer rather than a formality. B21.63 (`16_PESSIMIST_FA_B` edit 3, G3; R-04 membership, R-02 an admission sought, granted, refused; [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the second conjunct, which restores the single `existence` cell) ADDED THE SECOND, `relation` of `subject`, `admitted` (`data/requires.py`; `queries/world_q.py::admitted_to`): joining is an offer the faction's side answers, not a sentence the joiner speaks. It is true of every Proposition that is no rostered faction's (a cause, a covenant: `commit` is unchanged there), of a faction nobody belongs to, of a member's re-commit, and of a joiner an admission stands for -- an `OUGHT` naming him and the faction, `commit`ted to by a member who may admit (`state/gate.py::may_admit`: the faction's `head_seat` holder, or a member whose seat's grant carries `confer`; any member where the faction has no such seat) -- unless he belongs to a rostered faction incompatible with it (`rosters.yaml: factions.compatible_with` names the exceptions; the default is incompatible, `data/rosters.py::factions_compatible`). WORLD-ONLY, so a person forms the Candidate on anyone he knows of and the fold refuses a joining no one answered (`commitment.refused`); `world_q.propositions_heard` carries a faction's Proposition into the question of a man an admission names, so he forms the joining the admission offers.
verbs.refusal_note: §E2 -- 'failure emits, never raises': a verb with a `requires` needs a refusal channel, or a failed precondition produces no Event, no witness and no arc. Refusal conditions: the Proposition does not exist (§14 -- it is immutable and must be uttered first); or it is a rostered faction's, the actor belongs to none of it, and no admission of him stands (B21.63)

verbs.counterparty_note: IN-53: THE CONFEREE IS THE SECOND SIDE, AND A COMPUTED `confer` MUST CARRY HIM. The row is untyped (`_req_confer`'s `or` and its cardinality have no cell in the closed grammar, and the fold evaluates a typed cell OR a predicate, never both, `loop/resolve.py`), and an untyped row carries nothing, so `_eff_confer`'s `_operand(a, 'to')` would raise `InstrumentDefect` (H-207 cause 4). `to` is a `known_person_operands` member, so `VerbRow.known_person_operands` fans the Candidate over the persons the conferrer KNOWS (`give`'s receiver, `tell`'s hearer): one bag per known person, none when he knows nobody. `determine`'s precedent for a row naming its second side; the fold's counterparty clause (`loop/resolve.py::_admits`) refuses a hand-built `confer` naming nobody as `confer.refused` (the conferrer himself is admitted, `counterparty_may_be_self` below). Formed only on an Office referent (`referent_class` above).

verbs.refusal_note: B21.80 (`proposals/2026-11-12-subsystem-audit-suite/proposals/01_CORE_predicates_name_their_clause.md` step two, edit 4; B09.19's channel): KEYED PER CLAUSE, ONE KIND FOR EACH CLAUSE `_req_confer` DECLARES (`loop/predicates.py`'s `requires_predicate(clauses=)` is the owner of the eight names; `data/verbs.py::VerbRow.precondition_evaluable` admits the row only while its keys are exactly those plus the fold's own), so a refused `confer` says WHICH clause refused and a person who holds a seat can read it. The fold's own three clauses keep the kind the flat row emitted: `eligibility`, `write` and `counterparty` (which is also the seam's party gap, `loop/resolve.py::_refuse_party_gap`, so a contested row keying two or more kinds is lawful) are `confer.refused`. verbs.governing_note: B05.25 (`proposals/2026-11-13-verb-governing-attributes.md` §2) [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct at BA1.13].
verbs.referent_class_note: v11 CR-56 (reasons-to-convene RL1, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: drop the `matters_awaiting` term in `questions_for` and the re-slot loop in `loop/calendar.py`]): THE TIER WHERE A MATTER WAITS JOINS THE VENUES. `queries/world_q.py::matters_awaiting` stamps, as `Rung` beside `places_named`, for each undated person-matter on the docket the lowest rung among the convener's own seats granting this row's remit act that contains the matter's place; a sitting convened there fires a slot `world_q.slot_for` reaches from the matter, and CALENDAR's re-slot step fills the waiting matter into it (and into any open slot that reaches it). RL2 (this row stops forming on `places_named`, as a class of its own) was NOT taken, its stated revert: the score reads the verb, never the matter (reasons-to-convene N6). RL5, a matter-sensitive score term, is NOT BUILT: it would be a fourth `score_terms` summand, which amends `ARCHITECTURE_V2.md` §F2 (the resolution design's I6, RJ-layer1), a Layer-1 question. v10 REM-28 (B10-06, AM-A-14, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): THE VENUE. FORMED ONLY ON A `Rung`-CLASSED REFERENT -- the Rungs the standing occasions already stamp onto the question he answers: `queries/world_q.py::places_named` (every Rung his own ledger names that the ladder would seat him in and that he does not live under) and `larders_in_purview` (a stocked Rung in his seat's purview) -- and `subject` binds it through the unchanged referent rule (`decision/options.py::_derive_operand`). `loop/predicates.py::_req_convene` (a Rung of rank above `person`, or no subject) and `loop/effects_governance.py::_eff_convene` (which reads `subject` as the venue) are unchanged. THE CLASS REMOVES WRONG-KIND FORMATIONS. THE LIMIT, STATED: THE RUNG STAMP IS PLACES-TO-SETTLE, NOT VENUES. `Rung` is `occasion_only`, so the question's own Rung referent and the place he lives under are NOT carried and every place he has been told of IS, so the row also forms on hearths and settlements known by hearsay (`_req_convene` asks no presence of a convener: 'convene could happen at any scale except individual/person'); each convened date carries the seat that convened it (SC-01's holder step), so CALENDAR forms a docket slot (CP-T05-02, B10-13). No contest sits on the row (`14_VERBS_BINDING_D` UNDECIDED (U2): a draw on the sender's act beside the man's own answer would be two ladders for one quantity), so `contests:` is not added and `grade: ruled` stands. B21.55 (14_VERBS_BINDING_D commit D2, A-22; [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: empty `rosters.yaml: command_declines`]): FORMATION ASKS THE SAME RULE PERSON-SIDE. `decision/options.py::operand_bags` forms a `dispatch` only on a `subject` the sender can read as commanded (`queries/person_q.py::commanded_read`, the men his ledger names as sworn and the holders it names of other seats; `VerbRow.commanded_operand` reads the row off `rosters.yaml: command_declines`, one body with `issue`'s `to` fan), so no order is offered to a stranger the fold would refuse and nobody orders himself; what he cannot read stays the fold's refusal. THE CLASS REMOVES WRONG-KIND FORMATIONS ONLY: this row's eligibility (`remit:dispatch`) and its cell are unchanged; whom a seat may order is `commands`, at formation by what the sender reads and at the fold by the world. THE LIMIT, STATED: `dispatch` is an UNTYPED PREDICATE row, so a refusal records no `observed` read -- REM-11 files its refusals under 'other', and REM-22's test shape for the typed rows (a refusal on an `exists:<kind>` read) cannot observe it; the kind failure is read off the predicate's own refusal clause (REM-14's `_refuse` trace) and `tests/test_referent_class_stamps.py` holds the untyped row to that. The class is shared with `open_case` and `petition` and moves no derived set: `DECLARED_CLASSES` already holds `Person`, and `RUNG_REMIT_ACTS` reads `Rung` rows alone. A computed `dispatch` forms only on an id `World.class_of` holds, so `person.demanded` (SE-01's census individuation trigger, `loop/census.py`) is reachable only by a hand-built act. REVERT: delete this column.

verbs.requires_note: Evaluated as `_req_establish` in `loop/predicates.py` (`13f`), AND THE READING IS STATED THERE: *the establishing office* is the office the act describes -- the one being founded, or re-remitted on an id that exists -- NOT the office the actor sits in. That office's declared `conferral` must pass the SAME basis test `_req_confer` asks (`has_conferral_basis`), so an establish can never found a seat `confer` would refuse forever. Operands ride on the payload when an act carries them: `office`, `post`, `rung`, `remit`, `body` and/or `faction`, `conferral`, optional `revocation` -- the office overlay's own keys; otherwise (v11 CR-25, CR-11's design, decision 3) `loop/predicates.py::office_founded_by` (the World-taking sibling of `office_described_by`, read by `_req_establish` and `_eff_establish` alike) DERIVES the office from `subject` (a holding, admitted by `queries/world_q.py::founds_over`'s four conjuncts) and `Act.via` (the seat exercised): post from `offices.yaml: titles.domains`, faction and body the seat's, remit the seat's less `confer` and `revoke`, conferral `appointed`, revocation `rung_above_in_holdings`. Clause 5 carries H-144 (b) (any existing office asks `may_fill`) and H-132 (b) (a reduction of a sitting holder's grant asks `may_revoke`). No operand is added.

Side one is `transfer`'s cell verbatim, `stores(from, kind) >= amount`: the actor gives `amount` of `kind` from where he stands. Side two is `stores(to, return_kind) >= return_amount`: the other side gives back `return_amount` of `return_kind`. It could not be written before IN-33 because `rosters.yaml: requires_operands` had no names for the second side -- inside the eight, one `kind` and one `amount` would bind BOTH sides, a like-for-like swap that moves nothing. IN-33 coined `return_kind` / `return_amount` (*in return*: what comes back), the reserved coining `H-94` held. Operands, person-side (`decision/options.py::_derive_operand`): `from`, `kind`, `amount`, `to` exactly as `transfer`'s (`to` is the question's referent, the other larder); `return_kind` is the fixture `default_return_kind` and `return_amount` is `default_transfer_amount` -- DECISION [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct] at `hole_register.yaml` H-58, REVERT there. verbs.requires_typed_note: v9 IN-12 (`give` + Rung, #453 §9.6): THE CELL HAS NO `existence` CONJUNCT; THE OBJECT'S KIND IS THE EFFECT'S, `seize`'s precedent (v9 IN-13): the typed grammar has no disjunction, and `existence` of `subject` kind `Record` refused every Rung, so *a Record or a Rung* cannot be spelt. The cell keeps the conjuncts that carry the licence (`held_by`, `with`); `_eff_give` declines a subject that is neither a Record nor a Rung (`give.refused`, the `write` clause), and the gate's `handover` still admits only a non-seat `hold`, so a seat handed over is `NotYours`. THAT LOOSENS FORMATION (#453 §9.6 says so): the cell no longer filters on what the subject IS, so the person-side reading of the `held_by` conjunct (`OwnStateReader`, B10.59; formerly `rosters.yaml: own_hold_declines`, deleted at B10.61) is what keeps a person from forming a gift of a referent he does not hold. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: restore the `existence` conjunct (`kind: Record`); the Rung half is then unformable.] The typed cell (plan position `14`, U7-own) is what makes a gift formable, in place of `loop/predicates.py::_req_give`. TWO CONJUNCTS, each on an existing form and stem: `relation` of `subject`, `held_by` (the actor holds it -- `succeed`'s and `found`'s cell; `hold_force`'s raise on two live holders is not asked here because the gate's `handover` makes two unreachable); `relation` of `to`, `with` (the receiver stands where the actor does, UNKNOWN for a receiver who is no person, so *a person* rides here too; `with` is the telling workplan's `T4` stem, `data/requires.py: REQUIRES_STEMS`, `relation` of `to` -- `tell`'s `hearer`). *A person other than the actor* is `ED-IN-0210` ruling 1's second party and is the FOLD's (`loop/resolve.py::_admits`, the `counterparty` clause), not this cell's: the grammar has no negation. THE CELL BINDS `to` BESIDE `subject`, so `TypedRequires.known_person_operands` names `to` and `decision/options.py::operand_bags` forms one Candidate per person the giver KNOWS (`known_persons`, `tell`'s primitive) -- the topic is the referent (the Record) and the receiver is somebody known, never the referent. `with` is WORLD-ONLY, so a giver forms the Candidate on whom he knows and the fold refuses an absent receiver.
verbs.counterparty_note: THE RECEIVER. The typed cell binds `to`, so every Candidate carries it (from `operand_bags`' known persons) and `opening_set` declines only a gift to oneself, as it does a petition; the FOLD refuses the same case for a hand-built act (`_admits`' `counterparty` clause).
verbs.writes_note: ONE PER SIDE, `confer`'s pair: the giver's `hold` closes (`Tenure.until`) and the receiver's opens (`Tenure.since`), in ONE effect (`loop/effects.py::_eff_give`), so the fold never sees two live holders. The gate admits the close as `T-m` and the open as `handover` (`state/gate.py`), and the second requires the first IN THE SAME WRITE -- release-before-mint is the gate's condition, not the effect's habit (r2 `05` row 6, ⊕ R14). No `write_matrix.yaml` row is added: both pairs exist.
verbs.emits_note: v9 IN-12 (`give` + Rung): `rung.ceded` is the Rung half's kind (the cession of a rung `hold`), `seize`'s `rung.seized` beside it -- each half's subjects earn their own kind (`Subject.earns`), so a handed Record never publishes a ceded rung, and the dominance roster (`rosters.yaml`) lists the taking and not the gift. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: the Rung half emits `record.given`.] ⚠ `record.given` IS A NEW KIND, AND IT MUST NOT BE `record.created` OR `tenure.opened`/`tenure.closed`. `epistemic.py::_ch_chronicle` broadcasts every kind a `binding_decision` row emits and `_ch_post_remit` every kind a `remit:`-eligible row emits, both by kind; `confer`, `revoke` and `release` emit the tenure kinds and `issue` shares `record.created`'s family, so reusing either would make every handover in the realm public. `record.given` is emitted by this row alone, `social` and `own`-eligible, so neither channel reads it.
verbs.grade_note: RATIFIED PROGRAM POSITION 16 -- *one two-party verb ... `own` + `hold:<record>` eligibility, writing the holder's `hold` closed and the receiver's open* -- named against `architecture/VOCABULARY.md` (no row for give, grant, hand, convey or deliver; checked again at the build), and the gate's basis for the receiver's edge settled at G3's pre-flight (`ED-IN-0277`). `hold:<record>` is a PLACEHOLDER and declines on both sides (`H-75`); `own` admits first, as `transfer`'s `own | hold:<store>` does.

verbs.referent_class_note: B21.54 (14_VERBS_BINDING_D commit D1, A-21, A-22; [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete this column, and `issue` forms on the question's plain referent again, so a writ's `terms` names a person]): WHAT A WRIT ORDERS IS A PROPOSITION. FORMED ONLY ON A `Proposition`-CLASSED REFERENT -- the plain referent of the question he answers that is a Proposition (`queries/world_q.py::own_referents_of_class`), the Propositions he has heard of (`propositions_heard`) and the Propositions he is committed to as an OUGHT (`ambitions`, stamped by `questions_for` beside them) -- and `decision/options.py::opening_set` then forms on the classed ids alone (IN-53 D1's partition), so `subject` (the writ's `terms`) binds a Proposition and never a person, while `to` still fans over the persons the seat commands (the typed cell is unchanged: `executors`, `authority`, `terms`). THE CLASS REMOVES WRONG-KIND FORMATIONS ONLY: the row's eligibility, its cell and whom a seat may address are unchanged. DECLARED WIDENING, shared with `argue` (the other `Proposition`-classed row): both form on the Propositions their person is committed to; `commit` does not, `rosters.yaml: held_edge_declines` declining a cause he already holds.

verbs.requires_note: EVALUABLE (plan position `19`), AND SO `issue` IS RESOLVABLE. r2 `02` §A.6's proposal -- `commit`'s `existence of subject kind Proposition` -- is NOT taken: the prose says nothing about the terms, and a computed act binds `subject` and `to` to the question's ONE referent (`H-94`), so the Proposition conjunct and the executor conjunct could never hold at once and every computed `issue` would refuse -- `confer`'s 100% at `★`, for a clause the row does not state. IN-10 separated the two (`requires_typed_note`: `to` fans over known persons), and the Proposition conjunct is STILL not taken: a writ's `terms` may name a person or a Record (a warrant), not only a Proposition (#453 §10.1).
verbs.requires_typed_note: PLAN POSITION IN-10 (#453 §10.1, *`issue` joins the known-person fan for `to`*): `terms` IS THE CELL'S THIRD CONJUNCT (with `executors` and `authority`, below), AND ITS JOB IS TO BIND `subject`. A computed `issue` would otherwise bind `subject` and `to` to the question's ONE referent, so every writ's `terms` would name its own executor (`loop/effects_information.py::_eff_issue`) -- and a warrant read off such a writ would have the holder arrest himself. A cell binding `subject` beside `to` puts `to` in `TypedRequires.known_person_operands` (`data/requires.py`: the fan is empty for a cell binding `to` alone), so `decision/options.py::operand_bags` forms one `issue` per person the issuer knows and `data/verbs.py::act_key` keys each act by `subject>to`: the referent is the writ's `terms`, a known person its executor. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: an unpriced `terms` clause, which the grammar cannot write (a keyed row names every conjunct, and no form holds of every referent)] WHAT THE CONJUNCT ASKS: the issuer HOLDS A CLAIM ON THE TERMS (`own_ledger`, §F.24a form 6, `tell`'s form) -- a writ is about something its issuer knows of. It is the weakest clause the grammar can write on a referent of any class: a `claim_landed` referent is a claim the issuer holds, so it never refuses one. Refused, it is `issue.refused` -- the issuer, not the seat, said no. ⚠ TWO SHAPES CONSIDERED AND NOT TAKEN: the seat's purview over the terms (`Basis` `purview`) REFUSES A PROPOSITION, which has no place -- so a covenant dispensation, whose `terms` is a Proposition (#453 K-54, `commit`'s route), could never be issued; and r2 `02` §A.6's `existence of subject kind Proposition` refuses a warrant, whose `terms` is a person (#453 §10.1, `arrest`/`seize`). ⚠ A NAMED `own_ledger` CONJUNCT CARRIES `said` (`decision/options.py::opening_set`, telling `T4`), and a Candidate with nothing to say is declined: an `issue` act's payload holds the issuer's newest claim on the terms. Nothing reads it off an `issue` -- WITNESS reads `said` on `news.told` only, and the mint reads the kind's keys -- except `decision/choose.py::declare_intents`, which treats any act carrying `said` as a telling at a swept `intent_disclosure` > 0 (shipped 0). The Person clause stays on the executor alone: `terms` may name a person, a Record, a place or a Proposition. So `operands_for` carries `subject`, `kind` and `amount` for a computed requisition exactly as for a transfer (`kind`/`amount` from a held shortfall claim, else the fixtures, `H-94`). PLUS the conjunct the plan gives every remit verb, *'a predicate reading `via.scope`'*: `Basis` (§F.24a form 7, `data/requires.py`) with the `purview` rule, so the requisitioning seat's purview must reach the requisitioned rung (ruling (4), `04:330`) -- and a rungless seat, which reaches nothing, is refused before the effect could look for a treasury it lacks. ONE OWNER: the whole cell is typed, no predicate beside it (`test_wa_one_owner_...`).
verbs.writes_note: ×2, ONE PER SIDE -- PLAN POSITION `19`, `transfer`'s shape and the W3 audit's reason (*'six grain left the world and arrived nowhere'*): the requisitioned rung goes down and the seat's treasury, the rung of `Act.via`, goes up by the same, in one effect (`loop/effects.py::_eff_requisition`, through `_shift`, the one body of every move between two rungs' stores). The second pair is check-only.
verbs.draw_note: B07.01 (18-A item 4; A-81): the `draw` clause's Event reports a LOST DRAW, not a refusal (04 §C.4: a refusal is a precondition failed, a loss an outcome that went against you) -- emitted at the Failure band once `task_draw_arm` is `on` (B07.05), with no typed write; its durable write is the Event and the claims WITNESS deposits of it. Kept out of the refusal union (`data/verbs.py::VerbRow.draw_kinds`).
verbs.refusal_note: PLAN POSITION `19`: KEYED PER CLAUSE (`04 §B.13` invariant 4's per-conjunct half). `requisition.refused` is §27.1's SCARCITY channel -- *the second claimant on an emptied granary gets a DIFFERENT Event* -- and it is now the `stores` conjunct's alone: two requisitions on one larder in one fold, and the second finds it short (`tests/test_u7_remit.py`). `requisition.unauthorized` is the SEAT refusing: none exercised grants `issue`, or its purview does not reach the rung. A witness can tell a seat that could not reach the larder from a larder that could not cover the requisition.
verbs.eligibility_note: §E3's eligibility cell carried a PRECONDITION as well as the remit act (`remit:requisition + ...`). The act is the eligibility and the basis is a `requires`: the fold splits on the first `:` and tests the whole tail against the remit roster.
verbs.eligibility_substitution_note: The source cell named `remit:requisition`, and `requisition` IS NOT IN `remit_acts` (issue · determine · confer · revoke · dispatch · convene, a CLOSED roster). `remit:issue` is substituted, declared here: an instrument may fill exactly what the register declares (§42.2/G.4.8), so either `requisition` joins the roster (a ruling: it is a SEVENTH remit act) or `issue` is genuinely the remit a requisition exercises (defensible -- a requisition is issued). The same substitution is live on `establish`, which uses `remit:confer` and is likewise not a remit act. The substitution EXECUTES (a holder granted `issue` can requisition), and the open eligibility question (plan position `19`: *'stays an open eligibility question this position inherits (a neighbour of `H-52`)'*) is carried by `H-52`'s row.

verbs.referent_class_note: v10 REM-27 (B10-06, AM-A-13 limit, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]): THE FIELD. FORMED ONLY ON A `Rung`-CLASSED REFERENT -- the Rungs the standing occasions already stamp onto the question he answers: `queries/world_q.py::places_named` (every Rung his own ledger names that the ladder would seat him in and that he does not live under, so every known settlement but the one he lives under) and `larders_in_purview` (a stocked Rung in his seat's purview) -- and `subject` binds it through the unchanged referent rule (`decision/options.py::_derive_operand`). NO STAMP TERM OF ITS OWN: a `fields_named` term (Rungs of a `rosters.yaml: march_target_kinds` kind, offered to a seat granting a `Rung` row's remit act) was built and found unearned -- `places_named` already stamps what it would; its marginal reach is the settlement he lives under, which is not a target (`engine/season/tests/test_referent_class_stamps.py::test_rem27_*`). A non-settlement Rung `march` forms on (a hearth, a larder) is `loop/sides.py::sides_of`'s to refuse against the roster (H-149, `requires_typed_note` below). No operand, no seam: the field still enters through the mass-battle wrapper and its composition row, and `loop/sides.py::sides_of` still enforces the roster. THE DERIVED WIDENING, NAMED: classing this row adds its `remit:dispatch` to `RUNG_REMIT_ACTS` (`{issue}` to `{issue, dispatch}`), so `larders_in_purview` offers larders to dispatch-holding seats and `requisition` and `migrate` may form on a stamped settlement, and `march` on a stamped place or larder (the H-163 shared-class cost, read by REM-27's stop rule, not prevented). THE READING IS 'REACHES A FIELD', NEVER 'CONTESTS ONE': at `troops=weight` a realm force routs on contact whoever is stronger (`modules/mass_battle/massbattle.py::_weighted_unit`); who wins is REM-32's and JQ-4's. REVERT: delete this column; `RUNG_REMIT_ACTS` loses `dispatch` (the set is the union of the `remit:` acts over the `Rung` rows, `data/verbs.py`, so `convene`'s and `requisition`'s still stand).

verbs.requires_typed_note: ⚠ v9 IN-13: `sides_of`'s H-149 check now refuses a target outside `march_target_kinds` (a settlement or a territory since ED-IN-0306 phase 4) by mustering an EMPTY army (the provider's empty-`claimants` PARTY-GAP), and `subject = None` means only 'no opposing holder' -- the marcher's own faction holds the target, or nobody does -- which resolves `Unopposed` and arrives. M4 (`ED-IN-0279` clause (a)). Mirrors `kill / wound`'s own cell exactly, `kind: Rung` in place of `Person` -- `queries/world_q.py`'s `WorldReader.read` already answers `exists:Rung` generically (`arg.lower()+"s"` against `World._STATE_COLLECTIONS`), so this needed no new predicate. ⚠ DOES NOT NARROW TO `kind: settlement` (`march_target_kinds`, H-149): the five typed requirement forms answer *does an entity of this TYPE exist*, never a sub-kind filter, and inventing a sixth form for one row would be the second resolver S27.2 refuses at a smaller scale. `loop/sides.py::sides_of` checks the restriction itself, against `MARCH_TARGET_KINDS` (not a hardcoded kind string), on `sides_of`/`world_q`'s own precedent (`_eff_transfer`'s "a side that is not a rung means the transfer did not happen", checked at the seam and not in `requires_typed`). `sides_of` owns the check; `_eff_march` does not carry it. IN-36 (a), A-103: one march a season into each territory, a test limit, binding across the season's laps and not within one (the log takes a lap's Events at the lap's end; H-620's STATED REACH); refused on `march.refused`. The second conjunct is `march.nth <= march.cap` (`Fixtures march_cap_per_territory`, H-620; `queries/world_q.py::marches_into`): the marches this tick has admitted into the target's territory, a settlement counted against the territory containing it, with this one, against the cap; both read 0 at 0 or None, so no cap holds. UNNAMED, as the row is FLAT (one refusal kind): a refusal's `observed` carries the `march.nth` and `march.cap` reads that refused it. It rides `scalar_threshold`, a stem pair of an existing form, never a sixth typed form; no claim conjunct (`IS-B3-FA-04` (4)).
verbs.writes_provision_note: v9 IN-52 (the levy-to-field feed, [ASSUMPTION LF-3, delegated-ruled]): `Won` and `Lost` gain `Rung.stores` ONCE PER SIDE, `requisition`'s ×2 shape -- a fought field eats its ration from the attacker's treasury (the rung of `Act.via`'s office) and the defender's (the nearest held rung at or above the target), `settlements.provision`'s `consumed`, debited by `_eff_march` last, after the casualties and the arrival. Both pairs are check-only (the effect runs once, on `Person.body`). `Unopposed` fights no field and eats nothing. While `field_provisioning` is off (shipped) the entry consumes nothing and no store moves; the pairs are still gated, as every declared pair is. Revert: delete both pairs from both bands.
verbs.writes_note: v9 IN-13 (#453 §10.4 step 8, THE ARRIVAL): `Won` and `Unopposed` add `move`'s three pairs -- every claimant's live `contain` closes (`Tenure.until`), one opens to the destination (`Tenure.since`), and the destination is appended to his `Person.travel_leg` -- through `move`'s one journey body (`loop/effects_migration.py::_relocate`, keyed on the mover), at ENCOUNTER (`write_matrix.yaml`'s three `ENC` cells, M4's precedent). The gate admits the marcher's own legs as `T-m` and every other claimant's under `muster` (`state/gate.py::may_muster`: the seat granted `dispatch`, the claimant committed to its faction). `Lost` is unchanged -- a routed army stays at its origin (#453 R-7, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct]). No `hold` is written on any band: a won field moves presence, never title (#453 R-6, β). CP-T04-06 (B10-12, AM-C-11): `Invested` writes `(Site, condition)` ALONE -- under the `besiege` posture (`march_postures`) an OPPOSED march fights no field, relocates nobody and hurts nobody, and `loop/effects_combat.py::_eff_march` lowers each garrison Site in the target's subtree by `condition -= _fall(w, site)` (`loop/effects_economy.py`, `sabotage`'s one formula) WRITTEN DIRECTLY through the gate: wear staged through `World.stage` at ENCOUNTER is never applied (`loop/encounter.py` has no `take_staged`; the accumulator is RESOLVE-scoped). No accumulator, no fixture, no ratio. No `travel_leg` is written: a besieger makes no journey. An unopposed `besiege` is `Unopposed`, as a storm would be. A band whose subtree holds no garrison with condition to lose writes nothing and declines to `march.refused`. Revert: delete the `Invested` band.
verbs.writes_grade_note: M4 (`ED-IN-0279` clause (a)), Jordan's ruling on the second open clause: a loss writes "casualties only, decrease in morale, and a grudge token" -- nothing else, and nothing specified for the winner. `Won`/`Lost` here are the ATTACKER's own outcome (`seam/ladder.py::field_degree`), so `_eff_march` reads which SIDE actually lost from `resolution.result`'s `parties` and writes there -- the defenders on `Won`, the attacker's own claimants on `Lost`. CR-24 (`field_winner_casualties`, `H-360`, shipped `engine`): the winners take their own engine casualties on `body` only, each at his own side's or subunit's survivor ratio -- no stance row, no morale hit, and a winner is not a loser (`touched`); `off` is the field as it was. `Declared` writes nothing: it is RESOLVE's own deferral fold (`loop/resolve.py::_contest`). ⚠ SINCE v9 IN-13 an unopposed march, which has no losing side to write on, writes the ARRIVAL (`writes_note`), as `Won` does beside its casualties. v9 IN-52: the ration debit on `Won`/`Lost` (`writes_provision_note`) is not a loss effect: both sides of a fought field eat (LF-2/LF-3, delegated-ruled, `_part5` section J.2), and the sentences above govern casualties, morale and the grudge token: nothing specified for the winner, and CR-24 gives the winner a `body` casualty only. B17.01 (A-67, A-68, A-70, A-80, A-81): `Drawn` is the band of a field in which both sides are out (routed or conceded) or neither is (`seam/ladder.py::field_degree`): every band names its durable write, and `Drawn`'s is each side's `body`, scaled by its own side's (or own subunit's) share exactly as a winner's is (`field_casualty_model`), the ration debit as on `Won` and `Lost`, and `field.drawn` told to those present. No stance row is written (nobody lost), nobody is relocated (each army stands at its station: the aggressor where the march began, the defender at its own base, so there is no journey to write), and the fatigue half of A-69 is `27_MB_E`'s write (B22).
verbs.emits_note: v9 IN-13: `army.arrived` beside the band's kind on the two bands where the army arrives (#453 §9.6). ORDER IS READ: the band's own kind FIRST (`loop/effects_combat.py::_band_kind` takes `emits[band][0]` as the kind the losers earn when NOBODY MOVES, so a `Won` whose army already stood at the target publishes `field.won` and no arrival; with an army that moves, both kinds are published). A band whose army moves nobody and fells nobody declines to `march.refused`. CP-T02-01 / HR-1 (H-152): `Won` and `Lost` -- the bands whose `field_casualty_model: total` arm calls `remove_person` -- declare `person.died` and `tenure.closed`, earned only by a loser that arm kills and by each seat his death empties (`state/gate.py::death_subjects`); every other subject names the band's own kinds (`own_kinds`), so a fought field with no death publishes exactly what it did before. CP-T04-06: `siege.pressed`, the `Invested` band's one kind, is earned by each garrison Site whose condition fell (it is the threat `surrender` answers, CP-T04-07); it has one emitter, so `data/verbs.py::KIND_VERB` maps it here.

verbs.requires_typed_note: ⚠ v9 IN-59 (b) (RS-26, the AUDIENCE half of the access gate) ADDED `move`'s second conjunct here too, `relation` of `to`, `audience` -- otherwise a settler walks past the guard a traveller is stopped by. NAMED `audience` because the row keys its refusals, and keyed to `travel.blocked`: a guarded door refusing him is the journey failing, the fact `path` already emits; `audience` is WORLD-ONLY, so no witness deposits it as a belief about the road. [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: the single `path` cell.] `move`'s cell, clause for clause and for `move`'s reasons (§E3 `:408`, *a `contain` path exists*): the journey is the same journey, so a person who believes there is no road (`contain.path:<to>` False, deposited off a `travel.blocked`) forms neither a `move` nor a `migrate` there, through the one reader (`belief_contradicts`). NAMED `path` because the row keys its refusals. ⚠ v10 REM-29 (B10-06, `-08` AM-A-15, [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: delete the `room` conjunct and its refusal key, the `room` stem and `world_q.has_room`, so the throttle is the effect's inline decline again]) ADDED THE THIRD CONJUNCT, `relation` of `to`, `room` -- RR-2's throttle, which was the effect's hidden decline (`04 §B.13` inv. 4: every failable clause has a refusal kind). Room is the destination's capacity against its residents PLUS the migrant's own weight, unless he already lives under it -- a fact about the PAIR (rung, actor), so it is a `relation` stem asked of the destination and the actor (`audience`'s shape), answered by `queries/world_q.py::has_room`, the one owner `_eff_migrate`'s decline also calls; the grammar compares nothing new. NOT world-only: the refusal's read `(to, room:<actor>, False)` rides `Event.observed`, WITNESS deposits it to the actor (`observation_deposit_mode: actor`), and `belief_contradicts` reads it back, so a migrant refused for room does not re-form that `migrate`. THE LIMIT, STATED (AX-2 permits it): the belief is the migrant's alone and outlives any measured run (`confidence_default` 100 over `claim_decay_per_season` 5), so room freed later -- a death, a departure, a dwelling built -- is not seen by him until he is told otherwise. `room` is asked at admission, before the effect's custody and ladder declines, so a detained or off-ladder migrant aimed at a full rung is refused on `room` (the same `migrate.refused`). Still the effect's decline (`write`): a destination the ladder will not seat him in, and one he already lives in.

verbs.counterparty_note: ⚠ THE OTHER PARTY TO THE ACT, NAMED BY THE OPERAND THAT CARRIES THEM (plan position `15`). `decision/options.py::opening_set` forms no Candidate whose counterparty is the person themselves -- the contested-verb rule one column over (*a person is not their own adversary*), for the same reason: being oneself is not a belief anyone can be wrong about, so it is declined person-side rather than attempted and refused. Declined only at the fold, a self-address is a feedback loop: each refusal deposits a claim about the petitioner that raises another question about them, and no read the fold makes can say *that is you*. The loader requires the operand to be one the row's typed cell BINDS, so the Candidate always carries it.
verbs.requires_note: — no dedup, no cap, no per-venue limit (§26.3). ⚠ THOSE THREE ABSENCES STAND; WHAT CHANGED AT PLAN POSITION `15` IS THAT A PETITION NOW NAMES WHOM IT IS FOR. The cell was `—` and the verb had no effect, so it was never folded; the moment it mints a document it must say to whom, or it is a fiat. ⚠ AND IT IS NOW RESOLVABLE -- typed precondition plus `_eff_petition` -- so NPCs form and file petitions in computed play: a declared behaviour change that moves every run whose chooser can reach it.
verbs.requires_typed_note: ⚠ TWO-SIDED, PER `ED-IN-0210` RULING 2 (Jordan, 2026-09-10): *`petition` <-> WITHDRAW (petitioner) or DENY (receiver) ... `petition`'s pair is TWO-SIDED (withdraw and deny close the same state from opposite sides), the first in the set where a counterparty is structurally required.* RULING 1 on the same row is what makes each side an EXISTENCE clause: *a fiat needs no counterparty, so nothing checked that the object of an `oblige` was an entity* -- so each named side must BE one, and the grammar's `existence` form is the check. ⚠ THE RECEIVER IS A PERSON, BECAUSE RULING 2 NAMES WHAT THE RECEIVER DOES -- *DENY* -- and only a person acts (AX-1); the next position's `give` (`16`, H-84) moves a Record *to another person*, which is how a petition reaches the hand that may deny it. THE SEAT READING (`kind: Office`) IS NOT TAKEN: no question's referent is ever a seat, so every such petition would be refused, a constant scene tax with nothing behind it. The self-petition that `kind: Person` admits is declined person-side by `counterparty:` (above), not here: the grammar has no negation. `from` is the operand's one meaning (`decision/options.py::_derive_operand`: where the actor is) -- the place the petition rises from, #353 §36.1's *a demand rises from a hearth*. ⚠ WHAT A COMPUTED ACT CANNOT YET SAY: `to` and `subject` both bind the question's ONE referent (`_REFERENT_OPERANDS`), so a computed petition is addressed to the person it is about.
