verbs.counterparty_note: TELLING WORKPLAN `T4` (`ED-IN-0282`): THE HEARER IS THE SECOND SIDE, AND THE TOPIC IS NOT. `subject` stays what the telling is ABOUT and `to` is whom it is told to; the contest's opponent is `to` (`loop/resolve.py::_contest` reads `row.counterparty or "subject"`), so `sigma` throws the teller's pool against the HEARER's standing and not against a rung or a person merely talked about. `to` comes from `decision/options.py::operand_bags` -- one Candidate per person the teller KNOWS (`queries/person_q.py::known_persons`, `rosters.yaml: known_person_operands`) -- and never from the question's referent. `opening_set` forms none whose `to` is the teller (`petition`'s rule); a telling ABOUT oneself to somebody else IS formed, because a row naming its counterparty is not caught by the contested-verb self-subject skip (Decision 3). ⚠ NO `addressed` CHANNEL: an emitter names no recipient (§19.3, T-e). The addressee hears by PRESENCE, through `co_located`, like every bystander -- the `hearer` conjunct only refuses a telling to someone who is not there.
verbs.requires_typed_note: TELLING WORKPLAN `T4` (`ED-IN-0282`): TWO NAMED CONJUNCTS. `holds` -- the cell below, unchanged in what it asks. `hearer` -- `relation` (form 5) on the new `with` stem (`data/requires.py: REQUIRES_STEMS`): the person told and the teller share a place (`world_q.place_of`); UNKNOWN if either is no person or has no place, and ALWAYS UNKNOWN person-side (`WORLD_ONLY_STEMS`), so the teller forms the Candidate on whom they know and the fold refuses an absent hearer with `tell.refused` keyed `hearer` (`news.untold` before CP-T05-03; it is now the lost telling's kind alone). `holds` being NAMED is also what `opening_set` reads to carry `said` and to decline a Candidate with nothing to say (`TypedRequires.named_own_ledger_operands`); `survey` and `reconstruct` share the form unnamed and carry nothing. ⚠ THE CELL'S FIRST CONJUNCT, AS IT WAS: §E3 `:417` — *the teller holds a claim on the subject*. §F.24a form 6's first named cell, and the one the `F8` carve-out was written for. This is `_req_tell` verbatim: `any(c.subject == subj for c in teller.ledger)`, with the ledger reached through a reader that can name no other person's. `any(c.subject == subj ...)` is UNTYPED on predicate, so a `seen` claim satisfies it exactly as a `condition.worn` or `stores:grain` claim does (`R8.1`): `seen` gives the teller more subjects to hold a claim on, and the same ambient claim reaching the RECIPIENT means more of what is told is already held firsthand and the dedup guard drops it.
verbs.emits_note: v9 IN-18 `G6` (`H-197`, confidences): `confidence.broken` is DECLARED on every band that tells and EMITTED only when the act breaks a circle -- the teller holds the said claim under a `Claim.visibility` circle (a confided telling's deposit, `loop/witness.py::_circle_of`) and the addressee `to` is outside it (`loop/resolve.py::_confidence_broken`, the fold's one act-earned kind; `tell` writes nothing, so no effect earns it). Not on `Failure`: a telling the hearer did not take in told nothing. It adds no refusal route. At the shipped `telling_privacy` 0 no circle exists and the kind is never emitted.
verbs.contests_note: The prize is `a standing`, which is already rostered: loader invariant 9 (`04:467`) requires a verb's prize to be in the subsystem roster, and inventing a prize to dodge a ruling was considered and refused (`U1` / R-09, ED-SC-0037). `tell.refused` is the one kind on `emits_on_refusal:`, and `news.untold` stays on `emits:` at `Failure` ONLY (CP-T05-03, AM-D-04), so a lost telling is a realised act (the loop drops it until the next season, as `argument.lost` drops a lost `argue`) and a refused one -- the hearer is absent, nothing is held, the counterparty is no person -- is not, and re-forms next round. `04 §F.20b:1084` records that the derived Event-kind roster is SPECIFIED AND UNBUILT, so loader invariant 7 is not what admits the kinds. `writes:` IS `[]` AT EVERY BAND AND THAT IS LAWFUL RATHER THAN A HOLE. `04 §C.4:630-634` rules that a `Failure: []` is the only place in this architecture where writing nothing is correct, because the act still EMITS -- the difference between a refusal, where the precondition failed and no contest occurred, and a loss, where the contest occurred and went against you. A telling deposits at WITNESS, not here. There is NO `Person.stance` WRITE (TELLING WORKPLAN `T4`, `ED-IN-0282`): (1) the opponent is `to`, not `subject` -- the contest is thrown against the HEARER (`counterparty: to`, read by `loop/resolve.py::_contest`), so `subject` is the TOPIC and was never the party a standing is won from; (2) what a telling leaves is a chain, not a write: the hearer's told claim carries `chain = said.chain + (teller,)` (`T3b`), and how far a hearer credits the teller is read off that chain when the claim is weighed (`T3a`'s `teller_weight`), never stored as a stance. So `claim_subjects`' (`H-79`) empty-changes fallback lands the claim on what was told, `test_n3_..._a_telling_is_about_what_was_told` holds, `H-62`'s producer gap for `(Person, stance)` stays closed by `march` (M4), and the judged half of regard is the gated `G1`. A telling with nothing to say is not formed (T1's deferred decline, taken at T4): `opening_set` declines a `tell` Candidate whose `said_of` is `None`, because the `holds` conjunct is NAMED; `survey`/`reconstruct` share the form unnamed and are not declined.

verbs.eligibility_note: `H-160` LIMIT 1, THROUGH `H-158`'s FIRST REMEDY -- *'an eligibility alternative that names a seat'* -- [ASSUMPTION; medium; Jordan to correct; revert: the other remedy, a ruling that an `own` verb may be exercised through a seat]. `remit:issue` is the existing grammar's way to name one (`decision/options.py::exercised_seat` returns the hold that grants it, `pack_scenes` puts it on `Act.via`, `loop/resolve.py::_eligible` admits through `seat_hold`), so no fifth eligibility kind and no new form. FIRST, because the first alternative that admits decides which one `via` reflects: a holder of a seat granting `issue` gives THROUGH it, and his `from` is the seat's rung, its treasury (`treasury_of`, off the grant's `seat_rung` snapshot); anyone else falls through to `own` exactly as before. The fold admits the same acts either way (`own` still follows), so WHO PAYS FROM WHERE moves, and with it what `Act.via` reaches: the seat's obligees at its rung witness the transfer (`epistemic._ch_post_remit`; `off_restoration_leader` grants `issue` and has one), `_renewals` clauses 1-2 become meetable, and the fold admits the withdrawal through `own` without re-asking the seat (a queued withdrawal survives a same-round revoke or re-stamp; `test_term_upkeep`'s `_ONE_CLAUSE_BROKEN` asserts such a transfer still executes, so no `_eff_transfer` guard); a rungless seat is passed over (`need_treasury`). ⚠ `issue` IS `requisition`'s SUBSTITUTION CARRIED ONE VERB OVER, not a ruling -- `transfer` is not a remit act (`rosters.yaml: remit_acts` is closed), and a payment out of a treasury is read as issued, the converse of a requisition into it (`H-52`'s neighbour; its `eligibility_substitution_note`). ⚠ AND A HOLDER OF SUCH A SEAT NO LONGER FORMS A TRANSFER AS HIMSELF: one alternative per row decides, so his gifts from his own home are not formed. A candidate per admitting alternative is where that choice would go if it ever matters.

verbs.requires_typed_note: §E3 `:418` — ***`stores(hearth(giver), kind) >= amount`*** (§54 it. 7), the scarcity predicate §27.1 rests on. The cell carries no `operand_defaults:`: a fold supplying the person's operands would be two owners of one value AND an incoherence (the cell would ADMIT a transfer on operands it had invented, and `_eff_transfer` would then raise on those same operands being absent from the payload). The values `kind: grain` / `amount: 1` live in `DEFAULT_FIXTURES` (`default_store_kind`, `default_transfer_amount`), where `operands_for` derives them PERSON-SIDE and the act CARRIES them; `from` is the actor's own live `contain` Tenure and `to` is the question's referent, so neither is a fixture at all.
verbs.writes_note: ×2, ONE PER SIDE (§E3 `:418`). Both sides are declared: a ×1 declaration decremented only the giver, so grain left the world and arrived nowhere, in an economy where `yield` is the only source (#353 `:856`).  ||  ⚠ PLAN POSITION `17b`: `Tenure.term` ADDED, and `term.renewed` beside `transfer.made`. A transfer is a PAYMENT OF UPKEEP when it is exercised through a seat (`Act.via`) the actor sits in, out of that seat's own rung, to another rung that is the home of persons obliged to the seat: it then renews as many of their `oblige` terms as the amount covers at `upkeep_of(seat)` apiece (`loop/effects.py::_renewals` states the four clauses and why each is there; the gate admits each renewed edge under the `renewal` basis). This is `04 F.18`'s repair -- *'A MATTER payment would be a fourth clock, so the repair is a verb'* -- and the retirement plan's G2, *'payment = the existing `transfer` verb'*: no new verb, no new operand. The third pair is check-only, like the second. `term.renewed` is earned only by an edge whose term actually moved, and each rung earns `transfer.made` by name, so an ordinary transfer emits exactly what it did before `17b`. Since `H-160` limit 1 (`eligibility_note` above), a holder of a seat granting `issue` now gives through it, out of its rung, so a computed transfer CAN meet `_renewals`' clauses 1 and 2; whether one reaches an obligee's home is the chooser's and the world's.

verbs.requires: condition >= floor(verb) (§12.1)
verbs.requires_typed_note: §E3 `:420` — *`condition >= floor(verb)`* (§12.1). THE THRESHOLD IS A DECLARED READING OF `floor(verb)` FOR A VERB THAT NAMES NO USE: `WorldReader.read`'s `floor` branch returns `min(floors.values())` and argues for doing so — *`work` is the GENERIC labour verb, so a site is workable if it clears the floor of its LEAST demanding use*; `max` refuses a seam surface-gleaning supports, and `UNKNOWN` destroys the gate outright, since `work`'s precondition could then never return False. `floor` reads **100** for `site_harbour` and **50** for `site_seam`, and a named workable site emits `site.worked` (`test_tracer_is_honest.py`). The objection the reading answers is real: `band_floors`' inner keys are SITE-USE verbs (bulk_shipping, fishing, deep_mining …), **NOT verb-table rows**, so `work` is not among them, and on a harbour the cell asks `condition >= 100` where `floor(bulk_shipping)` is 800 -- every condition in 100..800 is ADMITTED WHERE THE PROSE REFUSES, an UNDER-refusal, which `G4` weighs equally with an invention. THE SITE-USE IS AN OPERAND THE CLOSED ROSTER DOES NOT CARRY, so the reader answers with `min` WITH THE READING STATED, not UNKNOWN. What stays open is that a `work` MEANING deep-mining is admitted on a seam only surface-gleaning could support, because nothing on the act says which use is intended. `W-C` binds `site` to the question's referent, so the substitution is reached on every computed `work`. Registered on `H-08`/`H-94`; typing the threshold needs a site-use operand first.
verbs.writes_note: WHAT THE WRITE CARRIES, since plan position `24e`: the act's own DECLARED delta where it declares one (`H-94`'s hand-built channel, unchanged), and otherwise -- only at a site a live works names (a `works` Record planning this site's kind at its rung, `queries/world_q.py::works_for`) -- `restore`'s rise, `loop/effects.py::_rise`: the headroom to the works' ceiling over those standing at the fabric. That is *'`work` advances `stage`'* read against r2 `04` §A.6.1, which RULED out a `stage` key on the Record: the stage a works has reached is its fabric's condition against the ceiling its ripened terms allow. DR-3 · §24 *"dockets form"*, no actor. ⚠ V11 CR-55: MAT is the lapse -- MATTER takes an item off the docket (slot and all) once it has been held beyond `Fixtures docket_lapse` seasons, one gate write per item (`loop/matter.py`), `matter.lapsed` its Event; a dead party, a venue that seats no bench and a matter that is no person otherwise hold their item for ever. ⚠ PLAN POSITION `19`: the RES cell has its first two producers -- `open_case` puts a matter ON the docket and `determine` takes it OFF (the item's `matter` written back to `None`), both through their own effects (`loop/effects_information.py`). CALENDAR still forms the actorless empty slot (`{date, matter: None}`); since v9 SC-01's fired-slot step `open_case` FILLS such a slot where one holds the matter (`world_q.slot_for`, the slot keeps its `date`) and appends a dateless item only where none is open. ⚠ V11 CR-56: CAL ALSO RE-SLOTS -- after forming slots, CALENDAR moves each undated person-matter into the open slot `world_q.slot_for` finds for it (`loop/calendar.py`, `docket.formed` at the venue), since no act back-fills a matter already waiting. The waiting item TAKES the slot's place dated with its `date` (`_reslot`), moving whole as CR-55's lapse removes one whole. THE SLOT THEREFORE GAINS the `arrangement` and `petition` keys the waiting item carries (RES wrote them on it), through this `matter` cell and not through those RES cells: B10-13's Lens B grades that CONVENTION (a `(DocketItem, date)` CAL row would be the conformant shape, unmeasured against the hash).
